`README.md`:

```md
# wow-live

Live WoW game state from the stock client's own network traffic, and the tools built on it.
The traffic is recorded and decrypted as it is written, then turned into JSON lines that any
tool can read. Nothing is injected into the game process or reads its memory. Works with retail (Midnight 12.1.5) and
WoW Forever (1.60.1).

| part | what |
|---|---|
| **the feed** (`tools/`, `protocol/`) | capture, decrypt, and the combat feed: auras, cooldowns, power and every combat event as JSON lines, served over WebSocket by `feedhub` |
| **the rotation helper** (`rotation/`, Rust) | a Hekili-style "press this next" that reads the feed, with SimC's Havoc Demon Hunter APL and an icon overlay |
| **the radar** (`radar/`) | every unit and object the server shows around you, mob paths, quest givers, herb and ore nodes, enemy players; a 3D web view, an overlay, and an MCP server so Claude can see around your character |

```
bnetrelay (login, records the world-key secrets)  ─┐
tcpdump of the world port (world.pcap)            ─┴→ worldstream (decrypt as it grows)
                                                       ├→ combatfeed → rotation → feedhub → overlay
                                                       └→ radar (web view, overlay, MCP)
```

## Setup (macOS)

Needs Go 1.23+, Rust (for the rotation helper), python3 with PyObjC (overlays), jq, and sudo for tcpdump.

```bash
sudo setup/connect-client.sh      # once: local certs, trusted CA, hosts entry, portal file (undo: ... undo)
sudo -v                           # tcpdump runs under sudo
tools/capture-live --dry-run      # check everything without starting anything
```

The client logs in through `tools/bnetrelay` on this Mac, which keeps the session's world-key
secrets so the world connection can be decrypted. Recordings go to `captures/<timestamp>/`
(git-ignored, mode 0700). **They hold your session's keys: never share or commit them.**

| environment | default |
|---|---|
| `WOW_RETAIL_DIR` | `/Applications/World of Warcraft/_retail_` |
| `WOW_FOREVER_DIR` | `/Applications/World of Warcraft/_forever_` |
| `WOW_LIVE_CAPTURES` | `captures/` in this repo |
| `WOW_LIVE_CERTS` | `certs/` in this repo |
| `WOW_FOREVER_DB` | an optional SQLite db of Forever names (`npcs`, `objects`, `quests`, `spells` tables) |

## Use

```bash
# the Havoc rotation helper: records, decodes, suggests and draws, until you quit the game
(cd rotation && cargo build --release) && rotation/tools/havoc-helper

# the feed by itself
tools/capture-live --game retail                       # relay + tcpdump + the game; quit the game to stop
go run ./tools/combatfeed -run captures/<run> -follow -spelldata <wago CSVs>

# the radar on a run that is recording, then http://127.0.0.1:8791
go run ./radar -run captures/<run> -follow             # retail; Forever: add -build 70755
claude mcp add --transport http wow-radar http://127.0.0.1:8791/mcp   # let Claude Code see around you
```

See [rotation/README.md](rotation/README.md), [rotation/HAVOC.md](rotation/HAVOC.md) and
[radar/README.md](radar/README.md) for each part.

## Feed lines

```
{"type":"player","guid":"..."}                        CMSG_PLAYER_LOGIN seen
{"type":"target","guid":"..."}                        CMSG_SET_SELECTION
{"type":"event","t":...,"sub":"SPELL_DAMAGE",...}     every combat event
{"type":"auras","unit":"player","auras":[...]}        the unit's auras, on every change
{"type":"cooldowns","gcd_ms":...,"cooldowns":[...]}   what is still recovering (absent = ready)
{"type":"power","powers":[{"type":17,"name":"fury","amount":42}]}
```

## The feed as a WebSocket server

`tools/feedhub` goes at the end of any feed pipe. It passes every line through to stdout
unchanged and serves the same lines to any number of local WebSocket clients: overlays,
dashboards, Discord bots, hardware displays. Lines that filters earlier in the pipe add,
such as the rotation's `next`, are served too.

```bash
combatfeed ... | wow-rotation <rotation.toml> --feed | go run ./tools/feedhub | auraoverlay.py --rotation
```

| endpoint (default `127.0.0.1:7373`) | what |
|---|---|
| `ws://…/feed` | each line as one message, `{"v":1,"seq":N,...}` |
| `ws://…/feed?types=auras,next` | only those types |
| `http://…/state` | the current state as JSON lines |
| `http://…/` | a live view in the browser |

A new client first gets the current state (the latest line of each type, per `unit` where
the line has one; never old `event`s; a `player` line, a login or relog, starts the state
afresh), then `{"type":"hub","live":true}` with the latest
`seq`, then the stream. From then on `seq` rises by one per line, so a gap means a missed
line. A client that can't keep up is closed with 1008 "too slow" and never holds up the
feed. Browser pages can connect only from the hub's own page or a `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`
origin (`-origin` adds more); `-token` requires `?token=`. When the feed ends, clients are
closed with 1000 "feed ended".

```js
const ws = new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:7373/feed?types=next');
ws.onmessage = e => console.log(JSON.parse(e.data).queue?.[0]?.name);
```

On macOS `combatfeed -follow` wakes the moment tcpdump appends to the capture (kqueue), so a
packet reaches the feed about a millisecond after it lands.

## What's here

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `tools/capture-live` | records the stock client on live: bnet relay, tcpdump of the world port, the game, decrypt at the end |
| `tools/bnetrelay` | the Battle.net relay that records the session's world-key secrets |
| `tools/worlddecrypt` | a finished capture to one JSON line per message |
| `tools/combatfeed` | the live feed |
| `tools/combatlog` | a capture's combat log, printed |
| `tools/feedhub` | the feed as a local WebSocket server, with a live view |
| `protocol/worldstream` | incremental decryption of a growing pcap |
| `protocol/combatlog` | CLEU-style events rebuilt from the server's combat messages |
| `protocol/spellstate` | cooldowns, charges, the GCD and power from the stream |
| `protocol/opcodes`, `codec`, `framing`, `pktlog`, `version` | the wire format |
| `auth`, `transport`, `world` | Battle.net, the connection and the world-key derivation |

| `tools/agent_relay.py` | sits between the game and the Battle.net Agent while capture-live starts it |
| `setup/connect-client.sh` | the one-time machine setup |
| `rotation/` | the rotation helper (its own README) |
| `radar/` | the radar (its own README) |
| `protocol/updateobject`, `state` | the world's objects and their update fields |

`auth/bnet/account.go`:

```go
package bnet

import "context"

// AccountService v2 method ids (account_service.proto, the fork's
// api/client/v2 stubs). The stock client calls these four right after
// LogonComplete (EVIDENCE.md E37).
const (
	MethodGetAccountInfo            = 101
	MethodGetRestriction            = 104
	MethodGetGameAccountInfo        = 201
	MethodGetGameAccountRestriction = 203
)

// GetAccountInfo sends AccountService.GetAccountInfo with an empty request
// and returns the raw response.
func (c *Client) GetAccountInfo(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error) {
	return c.Call(ctx, AccountService, MethodGetAccountInfo, nil)
}

// GetRestriction sends AccountService.GetRestriction with an empty request.
func (c *Client) GetRestriction(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error) {
	return c.Call(ctx, AccountService, MethodGetRestriction, nil)
}

func gameAccountRequest(g GameAccountHandle) []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.bytes(1, g.encode())
	return w.b
}

// GetGameAccountInfo sends AccountService.GetGameAccountInfo for g.
func (c *Client) GetGameAccountInfo(ctx context.Context, g GameAccountHandle) ([]byte, error) {
	return c.Call(ctx, AccountService, MethodGetGameAccountInfo, gameAccountRequest(g))
}

// GetGameAccountRestriction sends AccountService.GetGameAccountRestriction
// for g.
func (c *Client) GetGameAccountRestriction(ctx context.Context, g GameAccountHandle) ([]byte, error) {
	return c.Call(ctx, AccountService, MethodGetGameAccountRestriction, gameAccountRequest(g))
}

// DecodeGameAccountName returns GetGameAccountInfoResponse.info.name
// (info = field 1, name = field 2).
func DecodeGameAccountName(b []byte) (string, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	for _, f := range fs {
		if f.Num != 1 || f.Wire != wireBytes {
			continue
		}
		inner, err := pbParse(f.B)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		for _, g := range inner {
			if g.Num == 2 && g.Wire == wireBytes {
				return string(g.B), nil
			}
		}
	}
	return "", nil
}

```

`auth/bnet/client.go`:

```go
package bnet

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"sync"
)

var (
	// ErrClosed means the client's connection ended.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("bnet: connection closed")
	// ErrBindlessRequired means the server did not accept bindless RPC. The
	// only alternative is ConnectionService.Bind, which the client's own
	// descriptors mark obsolete and the shipped client never calls.
	ErrBindlessRequired = errors.New("bnet: server did not accept use_bindless_rpc; Bind is obsolete and not modelled")
)

// StatusError is a response whose Header.status is non-zero.
type StatusError struct {
	Status      uint32
	ServiceHash uint32
	Method      uint32
}

func (e *StatusError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("bnet: service %#08x method %d returned status %#x", e.ServiceHash, e.Method, e.Status)
}

// LogonError is a LogonComplete notification with a non-zero error_code.
type LogonError struct{ Code uint32 }

func (e *LogonError) Error() string { return fmt.Sprintf("bnet: logon failed with error %d", e.Code) }

// Handler receives the payload of a server-initiated request.
type Handler func(body []byte)

// ResponseServiceID is the header service id of an RPC response.
const ResponseServiceID = 254

type handlerKey struct{ hash, method uint32 }

type response struct {
	hdr  Header
	body []byte
}

// Client issues bgs RPC requests over a Conn and matches responses to them by
// token. Server-initiated requests (the AuthenticationListener callbacks) go
// to registered handlers, routed by service hash.
type Client struct {
	conn   *Conn
	router *Router
	closer io.Closer

	mu       sync.Mutex
	next     uint32
	pending  map[uint32]chan response
	handlers map[handlerKey]Handler
	ciid     string
	done     chan struct{}
	err      error
	// unhandled, when set, sees every server-initiated message no handler
	// took (the loop drops them, unanswered).
	unhandled func(h Header, body []byte)
}

// OnUnhandled sets the observer for server requests no handler takes.
func (c *Client) OnUnhandled(f func(h Header, body []byte)) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.unhandled = f
	c.mu.Unlock()
}

// NewClient starts the read loop over rw. If rw is an io.Closer, Close closes it.
func NewClient(rw io.ReadWriter) *Client {
	c := &Client{
		conn:     NewConn(rw),
		router:   NewRouter(),
		pending:  map[uint32]chan response{},
		handlers: map[handlerKey]Handler{},
		done:     make(chan struct{}),
	}
	if cl, ok := rw.(io.Closer); ok {
		c.closer = cl
	}
	go c.readLoop()
	return c
}

// Router exposes the service routing table.
func (c *Client) Router() *Router { return c.router }

// SetCIID sets the client instance id attached to requests for services whose
// options say use_client_id. Connect fills it from ConnectResponse.ciid when
// the server supplies one.
func (c *Client) SetCIID(id string) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.ciid = id
	c.mu.Unlock()
}

// Handle registers the handler for a server-initiated method.
func (c *Client) Handle(svc Service, method uint32, h Handler) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.handlers[handlerKey{svc.Hash, method}] = h
	c.mu.Unlock()
}

// Err reports why the client stopped, or nil while it runs.
func (c *Client) Err() error {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return c.err
}

// Close ends the client and closes the stream if it can be closed.
func (c *Client) Close() error {
	c.fail(ErrClosed)
	if c.closer != nil {
		return c.closer.Close()
	}
	return nil
}

func (c *Client) fail(err error) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	if c.err != nil {
		return
	}
	if err == io.EOF {
		err = ErrClosed
	}
	c.err = err
	close(c.done)
}

func (c *Client) readLoop() {
	for {
		f, err := c.conn.ReadFrame()
		if err != nil {
			c.fail(err)
			return
		}
		// Responses are matched by token. The flag is checked too, but a server
		// that never sets it (the TrinityCore fork does not) still answers with
		// the request's token, and tokens are unique per connection.
		c.mu.Lock()
		ch, pending := c.pending[f.Header.Token]
		c.mu.Unlock()
		if f.Header.IsResponse || pending {
			c.mu.Lock()
			delete(c.pending, f.Header.Token)
			c.mu.Unlock()
			if ch != nil {
				ch <- response{f.Header, f.Body}
			}
			continue
		}
		hash, ok := c.router.Hash(f.Header)
		c.mu.Lock()
		var h Handler
		if ok {
			h = c.handlers[handlerKey{hash, f.Header.MethodID}]
		}
		un := c.unhandled
		c.mu.Unlock()
		if h != nil {
			h(f.Body)
			continue
		}
		// ConnectionService.Echo is the server's keepalive (live sends one
		// ~30 s after the realm join, E37); the client answers with an empty
		// EchoResponse under service id 254, the response id.
		if ok && hash == ConnectionService.Hash && f.Header.MethodID == MethodEcho {
			_ = c.conn.WriteFrame(Frame{Header: Header{ServiceID: ResponseServiceID, Token: f.Header.Token}})
			continue
		}
		if un != nil {
			un(f.Header, f.Body)
		}
	}
}

// request builds the header the client's request builder writes
// (0x1022dce60): service_id (0 when bindless), method_id, token, the service
// hash and, for services that use the client id, the ciid.
func (c *Client) request(svc Service, method uint32) (Header, chan response) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	tok := c.next
	c.next++
	h := Header{
		ServiceID:   c.router.ServiceID(svc.Hash),
		MethodID:    method,
		Token:       tok,
		ServiceHash: svc.Hash,
	}
	if svc.UseClientID && c.ciid != "" {
		h.CIID = c.ciid
	}
	ch := make(chan response, 1)
	c.pending[tok] = ch
	return h, ch
}

// Call sends a request and waits for the response with the same token. A
// non-zero Header.status becomes a *StatusError.
func (c *Client) Call(ctx context.Context, svc Service, method uint32, req []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	h, ch := c.request(svc, method)
	if err := c.conn.WriteFrame(Frame{Header: h, Body: req}); err != nil {
		c.mu.Lock()
		delete(c.pending, h.Token)
		c.mu.Unlock()
		return nil, err
	}
	select {
	case r := <-ch:
		if r.hdr.Status != 0 {
			return r.body, &StatusError{Status: r.hdr.Status, ServiceHash: svc.Hash, Method: method}
		}
		return r.body, nil
	case <-ctx.Done():
		c.mu.Lock()
		delete(c.pending, h.Token)
		c.mu.Unlock()
		return nil, ctx.Err()
	case <-c.done:
		return nil, c.Err()
	}
}

// Connect performs the ConnectionService.Connect bootstrap with the request
// the client builds (DefaultConnectRequest) and records the ciid the server
// hands out. It fails with ErrBindlessRequired if the server does not accept
// bindless RPC.
func (c *Client) Connect(ctx context.Context) (ConnectResponse, error) {
	return c.ConnectWith(ctx, DefaultConnectRequest())
}

// ConnectWith is Connect with an explicit request.
func (c *Client) ConnectWith(ctx context.Context, req ConnectRequest) (ConnectResponse, error) {
	body, err := c.Call(ctx, ConnectionService, MethodConnect, req.Encode())
	if err != nil {
		return ConnectResponse{}, err
	}
	resp, err := DecodeConnectResponse(body)
	if err != nil {
		return ConnectResponse{}, err
	}
	// Live Battle.net (us.actual.battle.net, 2026-11-04) omits
	// use_bindless_rpc from ConnectResponse and still serves bindless
	// requests, so an absent flag is not a refusal. Only the fork sets it.
	_ = ErrBindlessRequired
	if resp.CIID != "" {
		c.SetCIID(resp.CIID)
	}
	return resp, nil
}

// Bind issues the obsolete ConnectionService.Bind for the given services and
// records the returned ids in the router, assuming (as the descriptor's
// repeated imported_service_id suggests but the binary does not confirm) that
// ids come back in request order. Nothing in the shipped client calls it.
func (c *Client) Bind(ctx context.Context, imported ...Service) error {
	var req BindRequest
	for _, s := range imported {
		req.DeprecatedImportedHashes = append(req.DeprecatedImportedHashes, s.Hash)
	}
	body, err := c.Call(ctx, ConnectionService, MethodBind, EncodeBindRequest(req))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	resp, err := DecodeBindResponse(body)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(resp.ImportedServiceIDs) != len(imported) {
		return fmt.Errorf("bnet: Bind returned %d ids for %d services", len(resp.ImportedServiceIDs), len(imported))
	}
	for i, s := range imported {
		c.router.Set(s.Hash, resp.ImportedServiceIDs[i])
	}
	return nil
}

// Logon sends AuthenticationService.Logon and waits for the server's
// OnLogonComplete callback, whose LogonRecord carries the session key and the
// login ticket. The callback handler is installed before the request goes
// out, because the server may deliver it before the Logon response.
func (c *Client) Logon(ctx context.Context, req LogonRequest) (LogonRecord, error) {
	done := make(chan LogonComplete, 1)
	bad := make(chan error, 1)
	c.Handle(AuthenticationListener, MethodOnLogonComplete, func(body []byte) {
		if os.Getenv("WOW_LOGIN_DEBUG") != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "logoncomplete %x\n", body)
		}
		n, err := DecodeLogonComplete(body)
		if err != nil {
			bad <- err
			return
		}
		done <- n
	})
	if _, err := c.Call(ctx, AuthenticationService, MethodLogon, req.Encode()); err != nil {
		return LogonRecord{}, err
	}
	select {
	case n := <-done:
		if n.ErrorCode != 0 {
			return n.Record, &LogonError{Code: n.ErrorCode}
		}
		return n.Record, nil
	case err := <-bad:
		return LogonRecord{}, err
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return LogonRecord{}, ctx.Err()
	case <-c.done:
		return LogonRecord{}, c.Err()
	}
}

// ProcessTask sends GameUtilitiesService.ProcessTask, the carrier of every
// realm command, and decodes the attribute results.
func (c *Client) ProcessTask(ctx context.Context, req ProcessTaskRequest) (ProcessTaskResponse, error) {
	body, err := c.Call(ctx, GameUtilities, MethodProcessTask, req.Encode())
	if err != nil {
		return ProcessTaskResponse{}, err
	}
	return DecodeProcessTaskResponse(body)
}

// ProcessTaskV1 sends GameUtilities.ProcessTask against the v1 service hash and
// with v1 Variant numbering.
func (c *Client) ProcessTaskV1(ctx context.Context, req ProcessTaskRequest) (ProcessTaskResponse, error) {
	body, err := c.Call(ctx, ServiceV1(GameUtilities), MethodProcessTaskV1, req.EncodeV1())
	if err != nil {
		return ProcessTaskResponse{}, err
	}
	return DecodeProcessTaskResponse(body)
}

func TestServiceHashes(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		svc  Service
		want uint32
		at   string
	}{

	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		if tc.svc.Hash != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: table says %#x, binary immediate at %s is %#x", tc.svc.Name, tc.svc.Hash, tc.at, tc.want)

		}

		t.Errorf("Services has %d entries, test covers %d", len(Services), len(tests))
	}

// pair returns a Client connected to a Peer over an in-memory pipe.
func pair(t *testing.T) (*Client, *Peer) {
	t.Helper()
	a, b := net.Pipe()
	p := NewPeer(b)
	go p.Serve()
	c := NewClient(a)
	t.Cleanup(func() { c.Close(); b.Close() })
	return c, p
}

func ctx(t *testing.T) context.Context {
	c, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	return c
}

`auth/bnet/conn.go`:

```go
package bnet

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"sync"
)

// Conn reads and writes whole RPC frames over a byte stream. It mirrors the
// client's read state machine (0x1022e7118): u16 big-endian header length,
// header, then Header.size payload bytes.
//
// WriteFrame is safe for concurrent use; ReadFrame must be called from one
// goroutine.
type Conn struct {
	rw  io.ReadWriter
	wmu sync.Mutex
}

// NewConn wraps a stream (a TLS connection to the bgs endpoint in production,
// a pipe in tests).
func NewConn(rw io.ReadWriter) *Conn { return &Conn{rw: rw} }

// WriteFrame encodes f and writes it with a single Write.
func (c *Conn) WriteFrame(f Frame) error {
	raw, err := Encode(f)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	c.wmu.Lock()
	defer c.wmu.Unlock()
	_, err = c.rw.Write(raw)
	return err
}

// ReadFrame reads one frame. A clean end of stream before the first byte is
// io.EOF; an end inside a frame is io.ErrUnexpectedEOF.
func (c *Conn) ReadFrame() (Frame, error) {
	var pre [2]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.rw, pre[:]); err != nil {
		return Frame{}, err
	}
	hlen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(pre[:]))
	hb := make([]byte, hlen)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.rw, hb); err != nil {
		return Frame{}, unexpected(err)
	}
	h, err := decodeHeader(hb)
	if err != nil {
		return Frame{}, err
	}
	if h.Size >= MaxPayload {
		return Frame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: header says %d", ErrPayloadTooLarge, h.Size)
	}
	body := make([]byte, h.Size)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.rw, body); err != nil {
		return Frame{}, unexpected(err)
	}
	return Frame{Header: h, Body: body}, nil
}

func unexpected(err error) error {
	if err == io.EOF {
		return io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
	}
	return err
}

```

`auth/bnet/external.go`:

```go
package bnet

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
)

// ExternalChallenge is authentication.v2.client.ExternalChallengeNotification
// as live Battle.net sends it: payload_type (field 2) "web_auth_url" and the
// URL in payload (field 3). Observed on us.actual.battle.net, 2026-11-04
// (EVIDENCE E32).
type ExternalChallenge struct {
	PayloadType string
	Payload     string
}

// DecodeExternalChallenge parses an ExternalChallengeNotification.
func DecodeExternalChallenge(b []byte) (ExternalChallenge, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ExternalChallenge{}, err
	}
	var c ExternalChallenge
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ExternalChallengeNotification.payload_type"); err != nil {
				return c, err
			}
			c.PayloadType = string(f.B)
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ExternalChallengeNotification.payload"); err != nil {
				return c, err
			}
			c.Payload = string(f.B)
		}
	}
	return c, nil
}

// WebLogin performs the web (Aurora) login at url and returns the token the
// server verifies (the login_ticket).
type WebLogin func(ctx context.Context, url string) (token string, err error)

// LogonExternal is the live v2 logon: Logon without a token, the server's
// OnExternalChallenge with the web_auth_url, the web login there, then
// AuthenticationService.VerifyAuthToken(auth_token = field 1) on the same
// connection, ending in OnLogonComplete. The fork's
// AuthenticationService.cpp implements the same order.
func (c *Client) LogonExternal(ctx context.Context, req LogonRequest, web WebLogin) (LogonRecord, error) {
	done := make(chan LogonComplete, 1)
	chal := make(chan ExternalChallenge, 1)
	bad := make(chan error, 2)
	c.Handle(AuthenticationListener, MethodOnLogonComplete, func(body []byte) {
		n, err := DecodeLogonComplete(body)
		if err != nil {
			bad <- err
			return
		}
		done <- n
	})
	c.Handle(AuthenticationListener, MethodOnExternalChallenge, func(body []byte) {
		x, err := DecodeExternalChallenge(body)
		if err != nil {
			bad <- err
			return
		}
		select {
		case chal <- x:
		default:
		}
	})
	c.Handle(AuthenticationListener, MethodOnLogonQueueEnd, func([]byte) {})
	c.Handle(AuthenticationListener, MethodOnLogonQueueUpdate, func([]byte) {})
	req.Options.AuthToken = nil
	if _, err := c.Call(ctx, AuthenticationService, MethodLogon, req.Encode()); err != nil {
		return LogonRecord{}, err
	}
	for {
		select {
		case x := <-chal:
			if x.PayloadType != "web_auth_url" {
				return LogonRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("bnet: external challenge %q is not a web login", x.PayloadType)
			}
			token, err := web(ctx, x.Payload)
			if err != nil {
				return LogonRecord{}, err
			}
			var w pbWriter
			w.str(1, token)
			if _, err := c.Call(ctx, AuthenticationService, MethodVerifyAuthToken, w.b); err != nil {
				return LogonRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("bnet: VerifyAuthToken: %w", err)
			}
		case n := <-done:
			if n.ErrorCode != 0 {
				return n.Record, &LogonError{Code: n.ErrorCode}
			}
			return n.Record, nil
		case err := <-bad:
			return LogonRecord{}, err
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return LogonRecord{}, ctx.Err()
		case <-c.done:
			return LogonRecord{}, c.Err()
		}
	}
}

```

`auth/bnet/frame.go`:

```go
// Package bnet is the Battle.net (bgs) RPC layer that runs before the world
// socket exists: the frame envelope, the Header message, the bootstrap
// (ConnectionService.Connect), the authentication Logon, and the generic
// attribute-bag GameUtilities.ProcessTask that carries the realm commands.
//
// Everything here is read off the client's own code and the protobuf
// descriptors it embeds (docs/EVIDENCE.md E26, tools/pbdesc.py).
//
// # Frame
//
// On the wire a bgs RPC frame is
//
//	u16 big-endian  header length
//	Header          protobuf, that many bytes
//	payload         Header.size bytes
//
// The client's read state machine (rpc_frame_transport_default.cpp,
// OnReadComplete at 0x1022e7118) has three states: 0 reads the u16 and
// byte-swaps it (FUN_1022dd1fc: *p>>8 | *p<<8), 1 reads and parses that many
// header bytes and takes Header.size (rejecting size >= 1<<20, the
// `>>0x14 == 0` test), 2 reads size payload bytes. The write side
// (SendMessage 0x1022e77c8, FUN_1022dd174) is the mirror: it writes the swapped
// ByteSize of the header, the header, then the message body.
package bnet

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
)

// MaxPayload is the exclusive upper bound on Header.size. The client rejects
// a header whose size has any bit at or above 1<<20 (0x1022e7118,
// `*(uint *)(hdr + 0xb4) >> 0x14 == 0`).
const MaxPayload = 1 << 20

// maxHeader is the largest header the u16 prefix can describe.
const maxHeader = 0xffff

// ProcessID is bgs.protocol.ProcessId (rpc_types.proto).
type ProcessID struct {
	Label uint32 // field 1, required
	Epoch uint32 // field 2, required
}

func (p ProcessID) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.varint(1, uint64(p.Label))
	w.varint(2, uint64(p.Epoch))
	return w.b
}

func decodeProcessID(b []byte) (ProcessID, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ProcessID{}, err
	}
	var p ProcessID
	var got [2]bool
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ProcessId.label"); err != nil {
				return p, err
			}
			p.Label, got[0] = uint32(f.V), true
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ProcessId.epoch"); err != nil {
				return p, err
			}
			p.Epoch, got[1] = uint32(f.V), true
		}
	}
	if !got[0] || !got[1] {
		return p, fmt.Errorf("%w: ProcessId", ErrMissingRequired)
	}
	return p, nil
}

// ObjectAddress is bgs.protocol.ObjectAddress.
type ObjectAddress struct {
	Host     ProcessID // field 1, required
	ObjectID uint64    // field 2
}

func (a ObjectAddress) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.bytes(1, a.Host.encode())
	if a.ObjectID != 0 {
		w.varint(2, a.ObjectID)
	}
	return w.b
}

func decodeObjectAddress(b []byte) (ObjectAddress, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ObjectAddress{}, err
	}
	var a ObjectAddress
	var host bool
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ObjectAddress.host"); err != nil {
				return a, err
			}
			if a.Host, err = decodeProcessID(f.B); err != nil {
				return a, err
			}
			host = true
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ObjectAddress.object_id"); err != nil {
				return a, err
			}
			a.ObjectID = f.V
		}
	}
	if !host {
		return a, fmt.Errorf("%w: ObjectAddress.host", ErrMissingRequired)
	}
	return a, nil
}

// ErrorInfo is bgs.protocol.ErrorInfo; all four fields are required.
type ErrorInfo struct {
	ObjectAddress ObjectAddress // field 1
	Status        uint32        // field 2
	ServiceHash   uint32        // field 3
	MethodID      uint32        // field 4
}

func (e ErrorInfo) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.bytes(1, e.ObjectAddress.encode())
	w.varint(2, uint64(e.Status))
	w.varint(3, uint64(e.ServiceHash))
	w.varint(4, uint64(e.MethodID))
	return w.b
}

func decodeErrorInfo(b []byte) (ErrorInfo, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ErrorInfo{}, err
	}
	var e ErrorInfo
	var got [4]bool
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ErrorInfo.object_address"); err != nil {
				return e, err
			}
			if e.ObjectAddress, err = decodeObjectAddress(f.B); err != nil {
				return e, err
			}
			got[0] = true
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ErrorInfo.status"); err != nil {
				return e, err
			}
			e.Status, got[1] = uint32(f.V), true
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ErrorInfo.service_hash"); err != nil {
				return e, err
			}
			e.ServiceHash, got[2] = uint32(f.V), true
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ErrorInfo.method_id"); err != nil {
				return e, err
			}
			e.MethodID, got[3] = uint32(f.V), true
		}
	}
	for _, g := range got {
		if !g {
			return e, fmt.Errorf("%w: ErrorInfo", ErrMissingRequired)
		}
	}
	return e, nil
}

// FanoutTarget is bgs.protocol.FanoutTarget.
type FanoutTarget struct {
	ClientID string // field 1
	Key      []byte // field 2
	ObjectID uint64 // field 3
}

func (t FanoutTarget) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	if t.ClientID != "" {
		w.str(1, t.ClientID)
	}
	if len(t.Key) != 0 {
		w.bytes(2, t.Key)
	}
	if t.ObjectID != 0 {
		w.varint(3, t.ObjectID)
	}
	return w.b
}

func decodeFanoutTarget(b []byte) (FanoutTarget, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return FanoutTarget{}, err
	}
	var t FanoutTarget
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "FanoutTarget.client_id"); err != nil {
				return t, err
			}
			t.ClientID = string(f.B)
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "FanoutTarget.key"); err != nil {
				return t, err
			}
			t.Key = append([]byte(nil), f.B...)
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "FanoutTarget.object_id"); err != nil {
				return t, err
			}
			t.ObjectID = f.V
		}
	}
	return t, nil
}

// Header is bgs.protocol.Header (rpc_types.proto; descriptor at image offset
// 0x31f72dc, dumped by tools/pbdesc.py). Field numbers are the descriptor's;
// the serializer at 0x10238c750 confirms the order and the key bytes for the
// fields the client writes (0x08 service_id, 0x10 method_id, 0x18 token,
// 0x20 object_id, 0x28 size, 0x5d service_hash, ...).
//
// ServiceID and Token are `required` in the descriptor and are always
// emitted, including a zero ServiceID: the client's request builder
// (0x1022dce60) sets service_id to an explicit 0, together with method_id,
// token and service_hash (has-bits 0x2160), and Size via 0x1022dce28. Every
// other field is omitted at its zero value. Size is not caller-set: Encode
// fills it from the payload length, as the client does.
type Header struct {
	ServiceID      uint32         // 1, required
	MethodID       uint32         // 2
	Token          uint32         // 3, required
	ObjectID       uint64         // 4
	Size           uint32         // 5, payload length; Encode sets it
	Status         uint32         // 6
	Errors         []ErrorInfo    // 7
	Timeout        uint64         // 8
	IsResponse     bool           // 9
	ForwardTargets []ProcessID    // 10
	ServiceHash    uint32         // 11, fixed32
	CIID           string         // 13, client instance id
	FanoutTargets  []FanoutTarget // 14
	CIIDFanout     []string       // 15
	ClientRecord   []byte         // 16
	OriginalSender []byte         // 17
	SenderToken    uint32         // 18
	RouterLabel    uint32         // 19
	ErrorReason    string         // 20
	SpanTraceID    string         // 21 (Span.trace_id)
}

func encodeHeader(h Header) []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.varint(1, uint64(h.ServiceID))
	if h.MethodID != 0 {
		w.varint(2, uint64(h.MethodID))
	}
	w.varint(3, uint64(h.Token))
	if h.ObjectID != 0 {
		w.varint(4, h.ObjectID)
	}
	w.varint(5, uint64(h.Size))
	if h.Status != 0 {
		w.varint(6, uint64(h.Status))
	}
	for _, e := range h.Errors {
		w.bytes(7, e.encode())
	}
	if h.Timeout != 0 {
		w.varint(8, h.Timeout)
	}
	if h.IsResponse {
		w.boolean(9, true)
	}
	for _, p := range h.ForwardTargets {
		w.bytes(10, p.encode())
	}
	if h.ServiceHash != 0 {
		w.fixed32(11, h.ServiceHash)
	}
	if h.CIID != "" {
		w.str(13, h.CIID)
	}
	for _, t := range h.FanoutTargets {
		w.bytes(14, t.encode())
	}
	for _, s := range h.CIIDFanout {
		w.str(15, s)
	}
	if len(h.ClientRecord) != 0 {
		w.bytes(16, h.ClientRecord)
	}
	if len(h.OriginalSender) != 0 {
		w.bytes(17, h.OriginalSender)
	}
	if h.SenderToken != 0 {
		w.varint(18, uint64(h.SenderToken))
	}
	if h.RouterLabel != 0 {
		w.varint(19, uint64(h.RouterLabel))
	}
	if h.ErrorReason != "" {
		w.str(20, h.ErrorReason)
	}
	if h.SpanTraceID != "" {
		var sp pbWriter
		sp.str(1, h.SpanTraceID)
		w.bytes(21, sp.b)
	}
	return w.b
}

// decodeHeader is strict: known fields must carry the wire type the
// descriptor gives them, the two required fields must be present, and
// structurally malformed input is an error. Field numbers the descriptor does
// not define are skipped, which is what a proto2 parser does with unknown
// fields.
func decodeHeader(b []byte) (Header, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return Header{}, err
	}
	var h Header
	var hasService, hasToken bool
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.service_id"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.ServiceID, hasService = uint32(f.V), true
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.method_id"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.MethodID = uint32(f.V)
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.token"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.Token, hasToken = uint32(f.V), true
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.object_id"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.ObjectID = f.V
		case 5:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.size"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.Size = uint32(f.V)
		case 6:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.status"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.Status = uint32(f.V)
		case 7:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.error"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			e, err := decodeErrorInfo(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.Errors = append(h.Errors, e)
		case 8:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.timeout"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.Timeout = f.V
		case 9:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.is_response"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.IsResponse = f.V != 0
		case 10:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.forward_targets"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			p, err := decodeProcessID(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.ForwardTargets = append(h.ForwardTargets, p)
		case 11:
			if err := f.want(wireFixed32, "Header.service_hash"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.ServiceHash = uint32(f.V)
		case 13:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.ciid"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.CIID = string(f.B)
		case 14:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.fanout_target"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			t, err := decodeFanoutTarget(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.FanoutTargets = append(h.FanoutTargets, t)
		case 15:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.ciid_fanout_target"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.CIIDFanout = append(h.CIIDFanout, string(f.B))
		case 16:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.client_record"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.ClientRecord = append([]byte(nil), f.B...)
		case 17:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.original_sender"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.OriginalSender = append([]byte(nil), f.B...)
		case 18:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.sender_token"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.SenderToken = uint32(f.V)
		case 19:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Header.router_label"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.RouterLabel = uint32(f.V)
		case 20:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.error_reason"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			h.ErrorReason = string(f.B)
		case 21:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Header.span"); err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			sp, err := pbParse(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return h, err
			}
			for _, sf := range sp {
				if sf.Num == 1 {
					if err := sf.want(wireBytes, "Span.trace_id"); err != nil {
						return h, err
					}
					h.SpanTraceID = string(sf.B)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if !hasService || !hasToken {
		return h, fmt.Errorf("%w: Header.service_id/token", ErrMissingRequired)
	}
	return h, nil
}

// Frame is one complete bgs RPC message.
type Frame struct {
	Header Header
	Body   []byte
}

// ErrPayloadTooLarge means a payload does not fit under MaxPayload.
var ErrPayloadTooLarge = fmt.Errorf("bnet: payload exceeds %d bytes", MaxPayload-1)

// Encode renders a complete frame. Header.Size is set from len(f.Body).
func Encode(f Frame) ([]byte, error) {
	if len(f.Body) >= MaxPayload {
		return nil, ErrPayloadTooLarge
	}
	f.Header.Size = uint32(len(f.Body))
	hdr := encodeHeader(f.Header)
	if len(hdr) > maxHeader {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("bnet: header of %d bytes does not fit the u16 length prefix", len(hdr))
	}
	out := make([]byte, 0, 2+len(hdr)+len(f.Body))
	out = binary.BigEndian.AppendUint16(out, uint16(len(hdr)))
	out = append(out, hdr...)
	return append(out, f.Body...), nil
}

// Decode parses one frame from the front of b and reports its total encoded
// length. A buffer that ends early yields ErrShortFrame.
func Decode(b []byte) (Frame, int, error) {
	if len(b) < 2 {
		return Frame{}, 0, ErrShortFrame
	}
	hlen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[0:2]))
	if len(b) < 2+hlen {
		return Frame{}, 0, ErrShortFrame
	}
	h, err := decodeHeader(b[2 : 2+hlen])
	if err != nil {
		return Frame{}, 0, err
	}
	if h.Size >= MaxPayload {
		return Frame{}, 0, ErrPayloadTooLarge
	}
	total := 2 + hlen + int(h.Size)
	if len(b) < total {
		return Frame{}, 0, ErrShortFrame
	}
	body := make([]byte, h.Size)
	copy(body, b[2+hlen:total])
	return Frame{Header: h, Body: body}, total, nil
}

`auth/bnet/frame_test.go`:

```go
package bnet

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"reflect"
	"testing"
)

// The golden request frame is what the client's request builder produces
// (0x1022dce60): service_id explicitly 0, method_id, token, size and the
// fixed32 service_hash, in field order, behind a big-endian u16 header length.
// 0x5dbb51c2 is GameUtilities (stub 0x10239446c), method 1 is ProcessTask.
func TestGoldenRequestFrame(t *testing.T) {
	f := Frame{
		Header: Header{ServiceID: 0, MethodID: 1, Token: 5, ServiceHash: 0x5dbb51c2},
		Body:   []byte{0xaa, 0xbb, 0xcc},
	}
	got, err := Encode(f)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want, _ := hex.DecodeString("000d" + // u16 BE header length = 13
		"0800" + "1001" + "1805" + "2803" + "5dc251bb5d" + // service_id 0, method 1, token 5, size 3, hash
		"aabbcc")
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("frame\n got %x\nwant %x", got, want)
	}
	back, n, err := Decode(got)
	if err != nil || n != len(got) {
		t.Fatalf("Decode: n=%d err=%v", n, err)
	}
	if back.Header.Size != 3 || back.Header.ServiceHash != 0x5dbb51c2 || !bytes.Equal(back.Body, f.Body) {
		t.Fatalf("round trip %+v", back)
	}
}

func TestHeaderRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		h    Header
	}{
		{"request", Header{ServiceID: 0, MethodID: 3, Token: 9, ServiceHash: 0x65446991}},
		{"response", Header{ServiceID: 0, Token: 9, IsResponse: true}},
		{"response with status", Header{ServiceID: 0xfe, Token: 70000, IsResponse: true, Status: 0x3ee, ObjectID: 1 << 40}},
		{"client instance id", Header{Token: 1, MethodID: 1, ServiceHash: 1, CIID: "7b1e0b36-8d41-4b6a-9f0e-0123456789ab"}},
		{"timeout and reason", Header{Token: 2, Timeout: 45000000, ErrorReason: "no such method"}},
		{"errors", Header{Token: 3, Errors: []ErrorInfo{
			{ObjectAddress: ObjectAddress{Host: ProcessID{Label: 1, Epoch: 2}, ObjectID: 7}, Status: 5, ServiceHash: 0x9da8116b, MethodID: 1},
			{ObjectAddress: ObjectAddress{Host: ProcessID{Label: 3, Epoch: 4}}, Status: 6, ServiceHash: 1, MethodID: 2},
		}}},
		{"forward and fanout", Header{Token: 4,
			ForwardTargets: []ProcessID{{Label: 9, Epoch: 8}},
			FanoutTargets:  []FanoutTarget{{ClientID: "c", Key: []byte{1, 2}, ObjectID: 3}},
			CIIDFanout:     []string{"a", "b"},
			ClientRecord:   []byte{9}, OriginalSender: []byte{8, 7},
			SenderToken: 12, RouterLabel: 13, SpanTraceID: "trace"}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			raw, err := Encode(Frame{Header: tc.h, Body: []byte("payload")})
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			got, n, err := Decode(raw)
			if err != nil || n != len(raw) {
				t.Fatalf("Decode: n=%d err=%v", n, err)
			}
			want := tc.h
			want.Size = 7
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Header, want) {
				t.Fatalf("header\n got %+v\nwant %+v", got.Header, want)
			}
			if string(got.Body) != "payload" {
				t.Fatalf("body %q", got.Body)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestZeroOptionalFieldsAreOmitted(t *testing.T) {
	raw, err := Encode(Frame{Header: Header{ServiceID: 0, Token: 0}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// u16 length, then only the required service_id and token and the size the
	// client always writes: 08 00 | 18 00 | 28 00.
	want, _ := hex.DecodeString("0006" + "0800" + "1800" + "2800")
	if !bytes.Equal(raw, want) {
		t.Fatalf("frame %x, want %x", raw, want)
	}
}

func TestDecodeRejects(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		raw  string
		want error
	}{
		{"empty", "", ErrShortFrame},
		{"one byte", "00", ErrShortFrame},
		{"header cut short", "0006" + "0800", ErrShortFrame},
		{"payload cut short", "0006" + "080018002803" + "01", ErrShortFrame},
		{"missing token", "0002" + "0800", ErrMissingRequired},
		{"missing service id", "0002" + "1800", ErrMissingRequired},
		{"empty header", "0000", ErrMissingRequired},
		{"unterminated varint", "0001" + "ff", ErrBadVarint},
		{"wrong wire type for service_id", "0003" + "0a0100", ErrBadMessage},
		{"hash with the wrong wire type", "0006" + "0800" + "1800" + "5801", ErrBadMessage},
		{"group wire type", "0002" + "0b0c", ErrBadMessage},
		{"truncated length-delimited", "0004" + "0800" + "6a05", ErrBadMessage},
		{"size over the cap", "0008" + "0800" + "1800" + "28808040", ErrPayloadTooLarge},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			raw, err := hex.DecodeString(stripSpaces(tc.raw))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if _, _, err := Decode(raw); !errors.Is(err, tc.want) {
				t.Fatalf("got %v, want %v", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func stripSpaces(s string) string {
	var b bytes.Buffer
	for _, r := range s {
		if r != ' ' {
			b.WriteRune(r)
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

func TestUnknownHeaderFieldsAreSkipped(t *testing.T) {
	// Field 99 (varint) after the required pair; a proto2 parser skips it.
	raw, _ := hex.DecodeString("0009" + "0800" + "1805" + "98060a" + "2800")
	f, _, err := Decode(raw)
	if err != nil || f.Header.Token != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("Decode: %+v %v", f, err)
	}
}

func TestEncodeLimits(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := Encode(Frame{Body: make([]byte, MaxPayload)}); !errors.Is(err, ErrPayloadTooLarge) {
		t.Fatalf("oversized payload: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := Encode(Frame{Body: make([]byte, MaxPayload-1)}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("largest payload: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := Encode(Frame{Header: Header{ClientRecord: make([]byte, 0x10000)}}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("header beyond the u16 prefix must not encode")
	}
}

func TestVarintHelpers(t *testing.T) {
	for _, v := range []uint64{0, 1, 127, 128, 300, 1<<32 - 1, 1 << 63} {
		b := appendVarint(nil, v)
		got, n, err := readVarint(b, 0)
		if err != nil || got != v || n != len(b) {
			t.Fatalf("%d: got %d n=%d err=%v", v, got, n, err)
		}
	}
	if _, _, err := readVarint([]byte{0x80, 0x80}, 0); !errors.Is(err, ErrBadVarint) {
		t.Fatalf("truncated: %v", err)
	}
	if _, _, err := readVarint(bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xff}, 11), 0); !errors.Is(err, ErrBadVarint) {
		t.Fatalf("overlong: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestConnReadsFramesAcrossArbitrarySplits(t *testing.T) {
	var wire bytes.Buffer
	c := NewConn(&wire)
	frames := []Frame{
		{Header: Header{MethodID: 1, Token: 1, ServiceHash: 0x65446991}, Body: []byte{1, 2, 3}},
		{Header: Header{Token: 2, IsResponse: true}},
		{Header: Header{MethodID: 1, Token: 3, ServiceHash: 0x5dbb51c2}, Body: bytes.Repeat([]byte{7}, 70000)},
	}
	for _, f := range frames {
		if err := c.WriteFrame(f); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	// Feed one byte at a time to prove the reader does not rely on message
	// boundaries.
	r := NewConn(readWriter{Reader: oneByteReader{bytes.NewReader(wire.Bytes())}})
	for i, want := range frames {
		got, err := r.ReadFrame()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("frame %d: %v", i, err)
		}
		if got.Header.Token != want.Header.Token || !bytes.Equal(got.Body, want.Body) {
			t.Fatalf("frame %d mismatch: %+v", i, got.Header)
		}
	}
	if _, err := r.ReadFrame(); err != io.EOF {
		t.Fatalf("end of stream: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestConnTruncatedFrameIsUnexpectedEOF(t *testing.T) {
	raw, _ := Encode(Frame{Header: Header{Token: 1}, Body: []byte{1, 2, 3, 4}})
	for _, cut := range []int{3, len(raw) - 1} {
		r := NewConn(readWriter{Reader: bytes.NewReader(raw[:cut])})
		if _, err := r.ReadFrame(); err != io.ErrUnexpectedEOF {
			t.Fatalf("cut at %d: %v", cut, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestConnRejectsOversizedSizeBeforeAllocating(t *testing.T) {
	// size = 1<<20 exactly: the client's `size >> 0x14 == 0` test fails.
	raw, _ := hex.DecodeString("0008" + "0800" + "1800" + "28808040")
	r := NewConn(readWriter{Reader: bytes.NewReader(raw)})
	if _, err := r.ReadFrame(); !errors.Is(err, ErrPayloadTooLarge) {
		t.Fatalf("got %v", err)
	}
}

// oneByteReader returns at most one byte per Read.
type oneByteReader struct{ r io.Reader }

func (o oneByteReader) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if len(p) == 0 {
		return 0, nil
	}
	return o.r.Read(p[:1])
}

// readWriter glues independent halves into an io.ReadWriter.
type readWriter struct {
	io.Reader
	io.Writer
}

`auth/bnet/logon.go`:

```go
package bnet

import "fmt"

// Authentication messages (authentication_service.proto,
// authentication_types.proto, authentication_listener.proto, all v2/client) and
// the account handle they reference (common/v2/game_account_handle.proto).

// TitleIDWoW is the fourcc "WoW" as the client stores it, the value of the
// title_id in its Logon request (the u32 at 0x1031d3810, read by the builder
// 0x1013a4824 into LogonRequest field 1).
const TitleIDWoW = 5730135 // 0x00576f57

// PlatformMacARM is the platform string of the Logon request: the builder
// converts the fourcc built from "MacA" (0x1022b4cfc) back to text.
const PlatformMacARM = "MacA"

// GameAccountHandle is bgs.protocol.account.v2.GameAccountHandle.
type GameAccountHandle struct {
	ID      uint64 // field 1
	TitleID uint32 // field 2
	Region  uint32 // field 3
}

func (g GameAccountHandle) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.varint(1, g.ID)
	w.varint(2, uint64(g.TitleID))
	w.varint(3, uint64(g.Region))
	return w.b
}

func decodeGameAccountHandle(b []byte) (GameAccountHandle, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return GameAccountHandle{}, err
	}
	var g GameAccountHandle
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "GameAccountHandle.id"); err != nil {
				return g, err
			}
			g.ID = f.V
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "GameAccountHandle.title_id"); err != nil {
				return g, err
			}
			g.TitleID = uint32(f.V)
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "GameAccountHandle.region"); err != nil {
				return g, err
			}
			g.Region = uint32(f.V)
		}
	}
	return g, nil
}

// LogonOptions is authentication.v2.client.LogonOptions. The client fills
// auth_token (field 1) and user_agent (field 2) in its Logon builder
// (0x1013a4824); which JSON-flow value it passes as the token is not settled
// by the binary (see docs/EVIDENCE.md E26), so AuthToken is whatever the
// caller supplies.
type LogonOptions struct {
	AuthToken []byte // 1
	// WebCredentials is the login ticket, sent as cached_web_credentials (12) in
	// the request encoding above.
	WebCredentials []byte
	UserAgent      string // 2
	DeviceID       string // 3
	Email          string // 10 (oneof additional_id)
	PhoneNumber    string // 11 (oneof additional_id)
	AuthPlatform   string // 12
}

func (o LogonOptions) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	if len(o.AuthToken) != 0 {
		w.bytes(1, o.AuthToken)
	}
	if o.UserAgent != "" {
		w.str(2, o.UserAgent)
	}
	if o.DeviceID != "" {
		w.str(3, o.DeviceID)
	}
	if o.Email != "" {
		w.str(10, o.Email)
	}
	if o.PhoneNumber != "" {
		w.str(11, o.PhoneNumber)
	}
	if o.AuthPlatform != "" {
		w.str(12, o.AuthPlatform)
	}
	return w.b
}

// LogonRequest is AuthenticationService.Logon's request, in the server's v1
// shape: program "WoW" (field 1, the FourCC as text), platform, locale,
// application version, and the web credentials the logon ticket goes in.
// The client's own builder writes a title_id varint in field 1 (E26) and the
// two shapes differ; a v1 server reads program as a string.
type LogonRequest struct {
	TitleID            uint32       // 1, varint (v2 shape the client uses, E26)
	Platform           string       // 2
	Locale             string       // 3
	Email              string       // 4
	ApplicationVersion uint32       // 6
	Options            LogonOptions // 10; also carries the web credentials
}

// Encode serializes the request.
func (r LogonRequest) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.varint(1, uint64(r.TitleID))
	if r.Platform != "" {
		w.str(2, r.Platform)
	}
	if r.Locale != "" {
		w.str(3, r.Locale)
	}
	if r.ApplicationVersion != 0 {
		w.varint(4, uint64(r.ApplicationVersion))
	}
	w.bytes(10, r.Options.encode())
	return w.b
}

// DecodeLogonRequest parses a LogonRequest; the server half for tests.
func DecodeLogonRequest(b []byte) (LogonRequest, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return LogonRequest{}, err
	}
	var r LogonRequest
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			// v1 sends program as a string; a title_id varint is accepted too
			switch f.Wire {
			case wireVarint:
				r.TitleID = uint32(f.V)
			case wireBytes:
				// v1 servers send program as text
			default:
				return r, fmt.Errorf("bnet: LogonRequest.program has wire type %d", f.Wire)
			}
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRequest.platform"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.Platform = string(f.B)
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRequest.locale"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.Locale = string(f.B)
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "LogonRequest.application_version"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.ApplicationVersion = uint32(f.V)
		case 10:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRequest.logon_options"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			ofs, err := pbParse(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			for _, of := range ofs {
				switch of.Num {
				case 1:
					r.Options.AuthToken = append([]byte(nil), of.B...)
				case 2:
					r.Options.UserAgent = string(of.B)
				case 3:
					r.Options.DeviceID = string(of.B)
				case 10:
					r.Options.Email = string(of.B)
				case 11:
					r.Options.PhoneNumber = string(of.B)
				case 12:
					r.Options.AuthPlatform = string(of.B)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return r, nil
}

// LogonRecord is authentication.v2.client.LogonRecord, the payload of
// OnLogonComplete. SessionKey (field 5) is what the client later sends back as
// Param_BnetSessionKey: it is stored by the LogonComplete handler 0x1013a5fd0
// (has-bit 2 of the record, the third string slot, into the global at
// 0x10407e3e8) and read by the realm-join builder 0x1013ad9a8, which passes
// that global to 0x101434b44.
type LogonRecord struct {
	AccountID    uint64              // 1
	GameAccounts []GameAccountHandle // 2
	BattleTag    string              // 3
	GeoIPCountry string              // 4
	SessionKey   []byte              // 5
	EmployeeOnly bool                // 6
	LoginTicket  string              // 7
}

// Encode serializes the record; the server half for tests.
func (r LogonRecord) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	if r.AccountID != 0 {
		w.varint(1, r.AccountID)
	}
	for _, g := range r.GameAccounts {
		w.bytes(2, g.encode())
	}
	if r.BattleTag != "" {
		w.str(3, r.BattleTag)
	}
	if r.GeoIPCountry != "" {
		w.str(4, r.GeoIPCountry)
	}
	if len(r.SessionKey) != 0 {
		w.bytes(5, r.SessionKey)
	}
	if r.EmployeeOnly {
		w.boolean(6, true)
	}
	if r.LoginTicket != "" {
		w.str(8, r.LoginTicket)
	}
	return w.b
}

func decodeLogonRecord(b []byte) (LogonRecord, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return LogonRecord{}, err
	}
	var r LogonRecord
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "LogonRecord.account_id"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.AccountID = f.V
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRecord.game_account"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			g, err := decodeGameAccountHandle(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.GameAccounts = append(r.GameAccounts, g)
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRecord.battle_tag"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.BattleTag = string(f.B)
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRecord.geoip_country"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.GeoIPCountry = string(f.B)
		case 5, 9:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRecord.session_key"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.SessionKey = append([]byte(nil), f.B...)
		case 6:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "LogonRecord.employee_only_mode"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.EmployeeOnly = f.V != 0
		case 8:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonRecord.login_ticket"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.LoginTicket = string(f.B)
		}
	}
	return r, nil
}

// LogonComplete is authentication.v2.client.LogonCompleteNotification.
type LogonComplete struct {
	ErrorCode uint32      // 1
	Record    LogonRecord // 2
}

// Encode serializes the notification; the server half for tests.
func (n LogonComplete) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	if n.ErrorCode != 0 {
		w.varint(1, uint64(n.ErrorCode))
	}
	w.bytes(2, n.Record.Encode())
	return w.b
}

// DecodeLogonComplete parses a LogonCompleteNotification.
func DecodeLogonComplete(b []byte) (LogonComplete, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return LogonComplete{}, err
	}
	var n LogonComplete
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "LogonComplete.error_code"); err != nil {
				return n, err
			}
			n.ErrorCode = uint32(f.V)
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "LogonComplete.record"); err != nil {
				return n, err
			}
			if n.Record, err = decodeLogonRecord(f.B); err != nil {
				return n, err
			}
		}
	}
	return n, nil
}

`auth/bnet/msgs.go`:

```go
package bnet

import "context"

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
)

// Messages. Field numbers are the embedded descriptors' (tools/pbdesc.py);
// presence is explicit where proto2 distinguishes it and a zero value is a
// legal, meaningful value.

// SemanticVersion is bgs.protocol.SemanticVersion (semantic_version.proto).
type SemanticVersion struct {
	Major, Minor, Patch uint32 // fields 1-3
	VersionString       string // field 4
}

func (v SemanticVersion) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.varint(1, uint64(v.Major))
	w.varint(2, uint64(v.Minor))
	w.varint(3, uint64(v.Patch))
	if v.VersionString != "" {
		w.str(4, v.VersionString)
	}
	return w.b
}

// ClientSdkVersionInfo is bgs.protocol.connection.v1.ClientSdkVersionInfo.
type ClientSdkVersionInfo struct {
	SDKName         string          // field 1
	SDKVersion      SemanticVersion // field 2
	ProtocolVersion SemanticVersion // field 3
}

func (c ClientSdkVersionInfo) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.str(1, c.SDKName)
	w.bytes(2, c.SDKVersion.encode())
	w.bytes(3, c.ProtocolVersion.encode())
	return w.b
}

// BoundService is bgs.protocol.connection.v1.BoundService (both required).
type BoundService struct {
	Hash uint32 // field 1, fixed32
	ID   uint32 // field 2
}

func (s BoundService) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.fixed32(1, s.Hash)
	w.varint(2, uint64(s.ID))
	return w.b
}

// BindRequest is bgs.protocol.connection.v1.BindRequest. ConnectionService.Bind
// is marked obsolete in its method options (BGSMethodOptions field 10), and
// the shipped client connects bindless, so nothing here is exercised by it;
// the message is modelled from the descriptor only.
type BindRequest struct {
	DeprecatedImportedHashes []uint32       // field 1, fixed32
	DeprecatedExported       []BoundService // field 2
	Exported                 []BoundService // field 3
	Imported                 []BoundService // field 4
}

func (b BindRequest) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	for _, h := range b.DeprecatedImportedHashes {
		w.fixed32(1, h)
	}
	for _, s := range b.DeprecatedExported {
		w.bytes(2, s.encode())
	}
	for _, s := range b.Exported {
		w.bytes(3, s.encode())
	}
	for _, s := range b.Imported {
		w.bytes(4, s.encode())
	}
	return w.b
}

// EncodeBindRequest serializes a BindRequest.
func EncodeBindRequest(b BindRequest) []byte { return b.encode() }

// BindResponse is bgs.protocol.connection.v1.BindResponse.
type BindResponse struct {
	ImportedServiceIDs []uint32 // field 1
}

// DecodeBindResponse parses a BindResponse.
func DecodeBindResponse(b []byte) (BindResponse, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return BindResponse{}, err
	}
	var r BindResponse
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "BindResponse.imported_service_id"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.ImportedServiceIDs = append(r.ImportedServiceIDs, uint32(f.V))
		}
	}
	return r, nil
}

// METERING_LEVEL_CATEGORIZED, connection_service.proto MeteringLevel.
const MeteringCategorized = 1

// ConnectRequest is bgs.protocol.connection.v1.ConnectRequest.
type ConnectRequest struct {
	ClientID       *ProcessID            // field 1
	BindRequest    *BindRequest          // field 2
	UseBindlessRPC bool                  // field 3
	MeteringLevel  uint32                // field 4 (0 is omitted)
	ClientSDK      *ClientSdkVersionInfo // field 5
}

// DefaultConnectRequest is the request the client builds in OnConnect
// (0x1022c0ae4, bgs_low.cpp): client_sdk_info with sdk_name "BGS C++ SDK"
// (0x1022b4c54), sdk_version 11.5.2 / "11.5.2" (0x1022b4c64; major, minor from
// the pair at 0x103138970 = (11, 5), patch 2) and protocol_version 3.33.19 /
// "3.33.19-2ddb4a936f" (0x1022b4bc8; (3, 33) at 0x1031d3820, patch 0x13), and
// two further single-field flags both stored as 1: use_bindless_rpc and
// metering_level = CATEGORIZED. client_id and bind_request are not set.
func DefaultConnectRequest() ConnectRequest {
	return ConnectRequest{
		UseBindlessRPC: true,
		MeteringLevel:  MeteringCategorized,
		ClientSDK: &ClientSdkVersionInfo{
			SDKName:         "BGS C++ SDK",
			SDKVersion:      SemanticVersion{Major: 11, Minor: 5, Patch: 2, VersionString: "11.5.2"},
			ProtocolVersion: SemanticVersion{Major: 3, Minor: 33, Patch: 19, VersionString: "3.33.19-2ddb4a936f"},
		},
	}
}

// Encode serializes the request.
func (r ConnectRequest) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	if r.ClientID != nil {
		w.bytes(1, r.ClientID.encode())
	}
	if r.BindRequest != nil {
		w.bytes(2, r.BindRequest.encode())
	}
	if r.UseBindlessRPC {
		w.boolean(3, true)
	}
	if r.MeteringLevel != 0 {
		w.varint(4, uint64(r.MeteringLevel))
	}
	if r.ClientSDK != nil {
		w.bytes(5, r.ClientSDK.encode())
	}
	return w.b
}

// ConnectResponse is bgs.protocol.connection.v1.ConnectResponse. The content
// handle arrays (fields 5 and 8) are skipped.
type ConnectResponse struct {
	ServerID        ProcessID     // field 1, required
	ClientID        *ProcessID    // field 2
	BindResult      uint32        // field 3
	BindResponse    *BindResponse // field 4
	ServerTime      uint64        // field 6
	UseBindlessRPC  bool          // field 7
	CIID            string        // field 9, the client instance id
	ConnectedRegion uint32        // field 10
}

// DecodeConnectResponse parses a ConnectResponse.
func DecodeConnectResponse(b []byte) (ConnectResponse, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ConnectResponse{}, err
	}
	var r ConnectResponse
	var hasServer bool
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ConnectResponse.server_id"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			if r.ServerID, err = decodeProcessID(f.B); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			hasServer = true
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ConnectResponse.client_id"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			p, err := decodeProcessID(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.ClientID = &p
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ConnectResponse.bind_result"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.BindResult = uint32(f.V)
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ConnectResponse.bind_response"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			br, err := DecodeBindResponse(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.BindResponse = &br
		case 6:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ConnectResponse.server_time"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.ServerTime = f.V
		case 7:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ConnectResponse.use_bindless_rpc"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.UseBindlessRPC = f.V != 0
		case 9:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ConnectResponse.ciid"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.CIID = string(f.B)
		case 10:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ConnectResponse.connected_region"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.ConnectedRegion = uint32(f.V)
		}
	}
	if !hasServer {
		return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: ConnectResponse.server_id", ErrMissingRequired)
	}
	return r, nil
}

// EncodeConnectResponse is the server half, used by tests and replay peers.
func EncodeConnectResponse(r ConnectResponse) []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.bytes(1, r.ServerID.encode())
	if r.ClientID != nil {
		w.bytes(2, r.ClientID.encode())
	}
	if r.BindResult != 0 {
		w.varint(3, uint64(r.BindResult))
	}
	if r.BindResponse != nil {
		var b pbWriter
		for _, id := range r.BindResponse.ImportedServiceIDs {
			b.varint(1, uint64(id))
		}
		w.bytes(4, b.b)
	}
	if r.ServerTime != 0 {
		w.varint(6, r.ServerTime)
	}
	if r.UseBindlessRPC {
		w.boolean(7, true)
	}
	if r.CIID != "" {
		w.str(9, r.CIID)
	}
	if r.ConnectedRegion != 0 {
		w.varint(10, uint64(r.ConnectedRegion))
	}
	return w.b
}

// DecodeConnectRequest parses a ConnectRequest; the server half for tests.
func DecodeConnectRequest(b []byte) (ConnectRequest, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ConnectRequest{}, err
	}
	var r ConnectRequest
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ConnectRequest.client_id"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			p, err := decodeProcessID(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.ClientID = &p
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ConnectRequest.use_bindless_rpc"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.UseBindlessRPC = f.V != 0
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "ConnectRequest.metering_level"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.MeteringLevel = uint32(f.V)
		case 5:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ConnectRequest.client_sdk_info"); err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			sdk, err := decodeSdkInfo(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return r, err
			}
			r.ClientSDK = &sdk
		}
	}
	return r, nil
}

func decodeSemver(b []byte) (SemanticVersion, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return SemanticVersion{}, err
	}
	var v SemanticVersion
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1, 2, 3:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "SemanticVersion"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			switch f.Num {
			case 1:
				v.Major = uint32(f.V)
			case 2:
				v.Minor = uint32(f.V)
			default:
				v.Patch = uint32(f.V)
			}
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "SemanticVersion.version_string"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			v.VersionString = string(f.B)
		}
	}
	return v, nil
}

func decodeSdkInfo(b []byte) (ClientSdkVersionInfo, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ClientSdkVersionInfo{}, err
	}
	var c ClientSdkVersionInfo
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ClientSdkVersionInfo.sdk_name"); err != nil {
				return c, err
			}
			c.SDKName = string(f.B)
		case 2, 3:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ClientSdkVersionInfo.version"); err != nil {
				return c, err
			}
			v, err := decodeSemver(f.B)
			if err != nil {
				return c, err
			}
			if f.Num == 2 {
				c.SDKVersion = v
			} else {
				c.ProtocolVersion = v
			}
		}
	}
	return c, nil
}

// ---- GameUtilities / bgs.protocol.v2 attributes --------------------------

// VariantKind selects the member of the bgs.protocol.v2.Variant oneof
// (attribute_types.proto, common/v2).
type VariantKind int

const (
	VariantNone   VariantKind = iota // an empty Variant message
	VariantBool                      // bool_value = 1
	VariantInt                       // int_value = 2
	VariantFloat                     // float_value = 3
	VariantString                    // string_value = 4
	VariantBlob                      // blob_value = 5
	VariantUint                      // uint_value = 6
)

// Variant is bgs.protocol.v2.Variant. The client's own parameter bag uses the
// same numbering: its type codes 4 (string), 5 (blob) and 6 (uint) are what
// 0x10139f648, 0x10139f734 and 0x10139f594 set.
type Variant struct {
	Kind   VariantKind
	Bool   bool
	Int    int64
	Float  float64
	String string
	Blob   []byte
	Uint   uint64
}

func (v Variant) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	switch v.Kind {
	case VariantBool:
		w.boolean(1, v.Bool)
	case VariantInt:
		w.varint(2, uint64(v.Int))
	case VariantFloat:
		w.double(3, v.Float)
	case VariantString:
		w.str(4, v.String)
	case VariantBlob:
		w.bytes(5, v.Blob)
	case VariantUint:
		w.varint(6, v.Uint)
	}
	return w.b
}

func decodeVariant(b []byte) (Variant, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return Variant{}, err
	}
	var v Variant
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Variant.bool_value"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			v = Variant{Kind: VariantBool, Bool: f.V != 0}
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Variant.int_value"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			v = Variant{Kind: VariantInt, Int: int64(f.V)}
		case 3:
			if err := f.want(wireFixed64, "Variant.float_value"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			v = Variant{Kind: VariantFloat, Float: math.Float64frombits(f.V)}
		case 4:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Variant.string_value"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			v = Variant{Kind: VariantString, String: string(f.B)}
		case 5:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Variant.blob_value"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			v = Variant{Kind: VariantBlob, Blob: append([]byte(nil), f.B...)}
		case 6:
			if err := f.want(wireVarint, "Variant.uint_value"); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			v = Variant{Kind: VariantUint, Uint: f.V}
		}
	}
	return v, nil
}

// Attribute is bgs.protocol.v2.Attribute. A name-only attribute still carries
// an (empty) Variant, as the client's bag does (0x10139efb0 allocates the
// value on creation), so Value is always encoded.
type Attribute struct {
	Name  string  // field 1
	Value Variant // field 2
}

func (a Attribute) encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	w.str(1, a.Name)
	w.bytes(2, a.Value.encode())
	return w.b
}

func decodeAttribute(b []byte) (Attribute, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return Attribute{}, err
	}
	var a Attribute
	for _, f := range fs {
		switch f.Num {
		case 1:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Attribute.name"); err != nil {
				return a, err
			}
			a.Name = string(f.B)
		case 2:
			if err := f.want(wireBytes, "Attribute.value"); err != nil {
				return a, err
			}
			if a.Value, err = decodeVariant(f.B); err != nil {
				return a, err
			}
		}
	}
	return a, nil
}

// ProcessTaskRequest is GameUtilitiesService.ProcessTask's request
// (game_utilities_service.proto): repeated attribute = 1, repeated payload = 2.
type ProcessTaskRequest struct {
	Attributes []Attribute
	Payload    []Attribute
}

// Encode serializes the request.
func (r ProcessTaskRequest) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	for _, a := range r.Attributes {
		w.bytes(1, a.encode())
	}
	for _, a := range r.Payload {
		w.bytes(2, a.encode())
	}
	return w.b
}

// DecodeProcessTaskRequest parses a request; the server half for tests.
func DecodeProcessTaskRequest(b []byte) (ProcessTaskRequest, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ProcessTaskRequest{}, err
	}
	var r ProcessTaskRequest
	for _, f := range fs {
		if f.Num != 1 && f.Num != 2 {
			continue
		}
		if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ProcessTaskRequest"); err != nil {
			return r, err
		}
		a, err := decodeAttribute(f.B)
		if err != nil {
			return r, err
		}
		if f.Num == 1 {
			r.Attributes = append(r.Attributes, a)
		} else {
			r.Payload = append(r.Payload, a)
		}
	}
	return r, nil
}

// ProcessTaskResponse is the response: repeated result = 1.
type ProcessTaskResponse struct {
	Results []Attribute
}

// Encode serializes the response; the server half for tests.
func (r ProcessTaskResponse) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	for _, a := range r.Results {
		w.bytes(1, a.encode())
	}
	return w.b
}

// DecodeProcessTaskResponse parses a response.
func DecodeProcessTaskResponse(b []byte) (ProcessTaskResponse, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return ProcessTaskResponse{}, err
	}
	var r ProcessTaskResponse
	for _, f := range fs {
		if f.Num != 1 {
			continue
		}
		if err := f.want(wireBytes, "ProcessTaskResponse.result"); err != nil {
			return r, err
		}
		a, err := decodeAttribute(f.B)
		if err != nil {
			return r, err
		}
		r.Results = append(r.Results, a)
	}
	return r, nil
}

// Lookup returns the attribute with the given name. The client's own lookup
// (0x10139ee2c) returns nothing when the name occurs more than once, so a
// duplicate is treated as absent here too.
func Lookup(attrs []Attribute, name string) (Attribute, bool) {
	var found Attribute
	n := 0
	for _, a := range attrs {
		if a.Name == name {
			found = a
			n++
		}
	}
	return found, n == 1
}

// GetAllValuesForAttributeRequest is GameUtilities.GetAllValuesForAttribute:
// the attribute key (field 1, a string).
type GetAllValuesForAttributeRequest struct {
	AttributeKey string // 1
}

// Encode serializes the request.
func (r GetAllValuesForAttributeRequest) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	if r.AttributeKey != "" {
		w.str(1, r.AttributeKey)
	}
	return w.b
}

// GetAllValuesForAttributeResponse is repeated attribute_value = 1.
type GetAllValuesForAttributeResponse struct {
	Values []Variant
}

// Encode serializes the response; the server half for tests.
func (r GetAllValuesForAttributeResponse) Encode() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	for _, v := range r.Values {
		w.bytes(1, v.encode())
	}
	return w.b
}

// DecodeGetAllValuesForAttributeResponse parses a response.
func DecodeGetAllValuesForAttributeResponse(b []byte) (GetAllValuesForAttributeResponse, error) {
	fs, err := pbParse(b)
	if err != nil {
		return GetAllValuesForAttributeResponse{}, err
	}
	var r GetAllValuesForAttributeResponse
	for _, f := range fs {
		if f.Num != 1 {
			continue
		}
		if err := f.want(wireBytes, "GetAllValuesForAttributeResponse.attribute_value"); err != nil {
			return r, err
		}
		v, err := decodeVariant(f.B)
		if err != nil {
			return r, err
		}
		r.Values = append(r.Values, v)
	}
	return r, nil
}

// The v1 GameUtilities service is what the TrinityCore fork (and the bnet
// server side generally) registers: its hash is FNV-1a of
// "bgs.protocol.game_utilities.v1.GameUtilitiesService", and its Variant oneof
// numbers every kind two higher than v2 (string 5, blob 6, uint 9).
// Attribute names/values keep fields 1 and 2.
const (
	GameUtilitiesV1Hash = 0x51923A28
	// GameUtilitiesV2Hash is the same service's OriginalHash; its handlers read
	// ProcessTask and keep attribute names untruncated.
	GameUtilitiesV2Hash = 0x3FC1274D
	MethodProcessTaskV1 = 1
	MethodAllValuesV1   = 2
)

// EncodeV1 is Variant.encode with the v1 field numbers.
func (v Variant) EncodeV1() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	switch v.Kind {
	case VariantBool:
		w.boolean(2, v.Bool)
	case VariantInt:
		w.varint(3, uint64(v.Int))
	case VariantString:
		w.str(5, v.String)
	case VariantBlob:
		w.bytes(6, v.Blob)
	case VariantUint:
		w.varint(9, v.Uint)
	}
	return w.b
}

func (a Attribute) encodeV1() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	if a.Name != "" {
		w.str(1, a.Name)
	}
	w.bytes(2, a.Value.EncodeV1())
	return w.b
}

// EncodeV1 is ProcessTaskRequest.Encode with v1 variants.
func (r ProcessTaskRequest) EncodeV1() []byte {
	var w pbWriter
	for _, a := range r.Attributes {
		w.bytes(1, a.encodeV1())
	}
	for _, a := range r.Payload {
		w.bytes(2, a.encodeV1())
	}
	return w.b
}

// EncodeV1 is GetAllValuesForAttributeRequest.Encode; the key is field 1 in
// both versions and only the variants differ.
func (r GetAllValuesForAttributeRequest) EncodeV1() []byte { return r.Encode() }

// ServiceV1 returns a Service addressed by the v1 server-side hash.
func ServiceV1(s Service) Service { s.Hash = GameUtilitiesV1Hash; return s }

// ServiceV2 returns a Service addressed by the v2 (OriginalHash) server-side
// hash.
func ServiceV2(s Service) Service { s.Hash = GameUtilitiesV2Hash; return s }

// ProcessTaskV2 sends GameUtilities.ProcessTask with the v2 Variant numbering,
// which is the shape the client's own builders emit.
func (c *Client) ProcessTaskV2(ctx context.Context, req ProcessTaskRequest) (ProcessTaskResponse, error) {
	body, err := c.Call(ctx, ServiceV2(GameUtilities), MethodProcessTask, req.Encode())
	if err != nil {
		return ProcessTaskResponse{}, err
	}
	return DecodeProcessTaskResponse(body)
}

`auth/bnet/pb.go`:

```go
package bnet

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"math"
)

// Protobuf wire helpers. The bgs messages in this package are small and their
// numbering is read straight out of the descriptors embedded in the client
// image (tools/pbdesc.py), so they are hand-coded rather than generated: no
// protobuf dependency, and every field number sits next to its evidence.

// Wire types (protobuf encoding spec).
const (
	wireVarint  = 0
	wireFixed64 = 1
	wireBytes   = 2
	wireFixed32 = 5
)

var (
	// ErrShortFrame means the buffer does not hold a complete frame.
	ErrShortFrame = errors.New("bnet: short frame")
	// ErrBadVarint means a protobuf varint was malformed.
	ErrBadVarint = errors.New("bnet: malformed varint")
	// ErrBadMessage means a protobuf message was structurally malformed.
	ErrBadMessage = errors.New("bnet: malformed protobuf message")
	// ErrMissingRequired means a proto2 required field was absent.
	ErrMissingRequired = errors.New("bnet: required field missing")
)

func appendVarint(dst []byte, v uint64) []byte {
	for v >= 0x80 {
		dst = append(dst, byte(v)|0x80)
		v >>= 7
	}
	return append(dst, byte(v))
}

func readVarint(b []byte, pos int) (uint64, int, error) {
	var v uint64
	var shift uint
	for {
		if pos >= len(b) {
			return 0, pos, ErrBadVarint
		}
		c := b[pos]
		pos++
		v |= uint64(c&0x7f) << shift
		if c < 0x80 {
			return v, pos, nil
		}
		shift += 7
		if shift > 63 {
			return 0, pos, ErrBadVarint
		}
	}
}

// pbWriter appends fields in the order they are written; callers write in
// ascending field-number order, as the client's own serializers do.
type pbWriter struct{ b []byte }

func (w *pbWriter) tag(field, wire int) {
	w.b = appendVarint(w.b, uint64(field)<<3|uint64(wire))
}

func (w *pbWriter) varint(field int, v uint64) {
	w.tag(field, wireVarint)
	w.b = appendVarint(w.b, v)
}

func (w *pbWriter) boolean(field int, v bool) {
	if v {
		w.varint(field, 1)
	} else {
		w.varint(field, 0)
	}
}

func (w *pbWriter) fixed32(field int, v uint32) {
	w.tag(field, wireFixed32)
	w.b = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(w.b, v)
}

func (w *pbWriter) double(field int, v float64) {
	w.tag(field, wireFixed64)
	w.b = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint64(w.b, math.Float64bits(v))
}

func (w *pbWriter) bytes(field int, v []byte) {
	w.tag(field, wireBytes)
	w.b = appendVarint(w.b, uint64(len(v)))
	w.b = append(w.b, v...)
}

func (w *pbWriter) str(field int, v string) {
	w.tag(field, wireBytes)
	w.b = appendVarint(w.b, uint64(len(v)))
	w.b = append(w.b, v...)
}

// pbField is one parsed key/value. Num is the field number; for varint and
// fixed fields V holds the value, for length-delimited fields B does.
type pbField struct {
	Num  int
	Wire int
	V    uint64
	B    []byte
}

// pbParse splits a message into its fields. It is strict about structure:
// truncated values, group wire types and field number 0 are errors. What each
// field means is left to the caller.
func pbParse(b []byte) ([]pbField, error) {
	var out []pbField
	pos := 0
	for pos < len(b) {
		key, next, err := readVarint(b, pos)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		pos = next
		f := pbField{Num: int(key >> 3), Wire: int(key & 7)}
		if f.Num == 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: field number 0", ErrBadMessage)
		}
		switch f.Wire {
		case wireVarint:
			f.V, pos, err = readVarint(b, pos)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
		case wireFixed64:
			if pos+8 > len(b) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated fixed64", ErrBadMessage)
			}
			f.V = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(b[pos:])
			pos += 8
		case wireFixed32:
			if pos+4 > len(b) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated fixed32", ErrBadMessage)
			}
			f.V = uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[pos:]))
			pos += 4
		case wireBytes:
			n, next, err := readVarint(b, pos)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			if n > uint64(len(b)-next) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated length-delimited field %d", ErrBadMessage, f.Num)
			}
			f.B = b[next : next+int(n)]
			pos = next + int(n)
		default:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: wire type %d (field %d)", ErrBadMessage, f.Wire, f.Num)
		}
		out = append(out, f)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// want checks that a known field arrived with the wire type its descriptor
// declares.
func (f pbField) want(wire int, name string) error {
	if f.Wire != wire {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s (field %d) has wire type %d, want %d", ErrBadMessage, name, f.Num, f.Wire, wire)
	}
	return nil
}
