```go
// Group counts: every group equal to 70707's except the two main groups, which
// each gained exactly one message.
func Test70755GroupCounts(t *testing.T) {
	old, cur := bothTables(t)
	if len(old.Groups) != 46 || len(cur.Groups) != 46 {
		t.Fatalf("groups: 70707 %d, 70755 %d", len(old.Groups), len(cur.Groups))
	}
	if got := cur.NumberedCount(ServerToClient); got != 1683 {
		t.Errorf("70755 s2c = %d, want 1683 (70707: %d)", got, old.NumberedCount(ServerToClient))
	}
	if got := cur.NumberedCount(ClientToServer); got != 1046 {
		t.Errorf("70755 c2s = %d, want 1046 (70707: %d)", got, old.NumberedCount(ClientToServer))
	}
	for i, g := range cur.Groups {
		o := old.Groups[i]
		if g.Name != o.Name || g.Base != o.Base || g.Direction != o.Direction {
			t.Fatalf("group %d: %s %#x vs 70707 %s %#x", i, g.Name, uint32(g.Base), o.Name, uint32(o.Base))
		}
		want := o.Count()
		if g.Name == "Client" || g.Name == "c2s_44" {
			want++
		}
		if g.Count() != want {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d opcodes, want %d (70707 %d)", g.Name, g.Count(), want, o.Count())
		}
	}
	if g, _ := cur.GroupOf(ServerToClient, 0x470000); uint32(g.End) != 0x47038F {
		t.Errorf("Client end %#x, want 0x47038f", uint32(g.End))
	}
}

// The shift boundaries, as the 70755 getters show them.
func Test70755ShiftBoundaries(t *testing.T) {
	old, cur := bothTables(t)
	c2s := func(tb *Table, idx uint32) bool { return tb.Known(ClientToServer, 0x440000|idx) }
	// 0x44: 0x6D, 0x6E, 0x70 keep their numbers (no 0x6F in either build);
	// 0x71 is gone, 0x72 is new, 70707 0x71.. sit two higher.
	for _, c := range []struct {
		idx      uint32
		old, now bool
	}{
		{0x6D, true, true}, {0x6E, true, true}, {0x6F, false, false}, {0x70, true, true},
		{0x71, true, false}, {0x72, true, true}, {0x73, true, true},
		{0x1B3, true, true}, {0x1B4, false, true}, {0x1B5, false, true}, {0x1B6, false, false},
	} {
		if c2s(old, c.idx) != c.old || c2s(cur, c.idx) != c.now {
			t.Errorf("c2s 0x44%04X: 70707 %v (want %v), 70755 %v (want %v)", c.idx, c2s(old, c.idx), c.old, c2s(cur, c.idx), c.now)
		}
	}
	if !cur.Known(ServerToClient, 0x47038E) || old.Known(ServerToClient, 0x47038E) {
		t.Error("s2c 0x47038e must exist in 70755 only")
	}
}

func rebaseMap(t *testing.T) map[uint32]struct{ old, code string } {
	t.Helper()
	raw, err := os.ReadFile("../../research/opcode_rebase_70755.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("the research inventories live in wow-forever:", err)
	}
	var doc struct {
		Opcodes []struct {
			Opcode string  `json:"opcode"`
			Old    *string `json:"old"`
			Code   string  `json:"code"`
		} `json:"opcodes"`
		VtableCheck map[string]struct {
			OK  int      `json:"ok"`
			Bad []string `json:"bad"`
		} `json:"vtable_check"`
		Unmapped []string `json:"unmapped_old"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for b, v := range doc.VtableCheck {
		if len(v.Bad) != 0 || v.OK < 1679 {
			t.Errorf("vtable check %s: %d ok, bad %v", b, v.OK, v.Bad)
		}
	}
	if len(doc.Unmapped) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("70707 opcodes with no 70755 counterpart: %v", doc.Unmapped)
	}
	m := map[uint32]struct{ old, code string }{}
	for _, o := range doc.Opcodes {
		n, _ := strconv.ParseUint(o.Opcode, 0, 32)
		old := ""
		if o.Old != nil {
			old = *o.Old
		}
		m[uint32(n)] = struct{ old, code string }{old, o.Code}
	}
	return m
}

// The client's own code decides where each 70707 message went. It agrees with
// the measured client shift (0x44: +2 from 70707 0x71) and disagrees with the
// measured server shift: the new server message is 0x4700EA, not 0x470125,
// and 70707 0x4700EA..0x470124 are one higher too.
func Test70755RebaseMap(t *testing.T) {
	m := rebaseMap(t)
	want := func(op uint32) uint32 {
		g, i := op>>16, op&0xFFFF
		switch {
		case g == 0x44 && i >= 0x73:
			return op - 2
		case g == 0x47 && i >= 0xEB:
			return op - 1
		}
		return op
	}
	for op, r := range m {
		if r.code == "new" {
			if op != 0x440072 && op != 0x4700EA {
				t.Errorf("unexpected new opcode %#08x", op)
			}
			continue
		}
		o, _ := strconv.ParseUint(r.old, 0, 32)
		if uint32(o) != want(op) {
			t.Errorf("70755 %#08x carries 70707 %s, want %#08x", op, r.old, want(op))
		}
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		op   uint32
		old  string
		code string
	}{
		{0x440014, "0x440014", "identical"},
		{0x440070, "0x440070", "identical-ambiguous"},
		{0x440073, "0x440071", "identical"},
		{0x470018, "0x470018", "changed"},
		{0x4700EC, "0x4700eb", "identical"},
		{0x470125, "0x470124", "identical"},
		{0x470126, "0x470125", "identical-ambiguous"},
	} {
		if r := m[c.op]; r.old != c.old || r.code != c.code {
			t.Errorf("%#08x: carries %q (%s), want %s (%s)", c.op, r.old, r.code, c.old, c.code)
		}
	}
}

func Test70755NameSpotChecks(t *testing.T) {
	old, err := NamesForBuild(70707)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cur, err := NamesForBuild(70755)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	name := func(n *Names, d Direction, op uint32) string {
		e, _ := n.Lookup(d, op)
		return e.Name
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		dir  Direction
		op   uint32
		name string
	}{
		{ClientToServer, 0x440014, "CMSG_ENUM_CHARACTERS"},
		{ClientToServer, 0x440070, "CMSG_CREATE_CHARACTER"},
		{ClientToServer, 0x440073, "CMSG_CHECK_CHARACTER_NAME_AVAILABILITY"},
		{ClientToServer, 0x4400B7, "CMSG_QUERY_REALM_NAME"},
		{ClientToServer, 0x4400CC, "CMSG_SERVER_TIME_OFFSET_REQUEST"},
		{ClientToServer, 0x460001, "CMSG_AUTH_SESSION"},
		{ServerToClient, 0x470018, "SMSG_ENUM_CHARACTERS_RESULT"},
		{ServerToClient, 0x4700ED, "SMSG_ADDON_LIST_REQUEST"},
		{ServerToClient, 0x4700EE, "SMSG_ACHIEVEMENT_EARNED"},
		{ServerToClient, 0x470125, "SMSG_SET_TIME_ZONE_INFORMATION"},
		{ServerToClient, 0x470126, "SMSG_BATTLE_PET_CAGE_DATE_ERROR"},
		{ServerToClient, 0x470316, "SMSG_LATENCY_REPORT_PING"},
		{ServerToClient, 0x4C0005, "SMSG_MOTD"},
	} {
		if got := name(cur, c.dir, c.op); got != c.name {
			t.Errorf("70755 %#08x = %q, want %s", c.op, got, c.name)
		}
	}
	// name check: 70755 0x440073 is 70707 0x440071's name, two higher
	if name(cur, ClientToServer, 0x440073) != name(old, ClientToServer, 0x440071) {
		t.Error("0x440073 must carry 70707 0x440071's name")
	}
	// 0x126 is 70707 0x125's name; 0x125 is 70707 0x124's (not new)
	if name(cur, ServerToClient, 0x470126) != name(old, ServerToClient, 0x470125) ||
		name(cur, ServerToClient, 0x470125) != name(old, ServerToClient, 0x470124) {
		t.Error("0x470125/0x470126 must carry 70707 0x470124/0x470125")
	}
	// the two new messages are unnamed
	for _, c := range []struct {
		dir Direction
		op  uint32
	}{{ClientToServer, 0x440072}, {ServerToClient, 0x4700EA}} {
		e := entryAt(cur, c.dir, c.op)
		if e == nil || e.Name != "" || e.Confidence != NameNone || e.RebaseCode != "new" {
			t.Errorf("%#08x: %+v, want an unnamed new entry", c.op, e)
		}
	}
}

// Every carried entry has the 70707 name of the opcode it carries, and keeps
// its grade unless it moved on a shared body (then capped at medium).
func Test70755NamesCarried(t *testing.T) {
	old, _ := NamesForBuild(70707)
	cur, err := NamesForBuild(70755)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := rebaseMap(t)
	tbl, _ := ForBuild(70755)
	for _, dir := range []Direction{ServerToClient, ClientToServer} {
		if got, want := len(entriesFor(cur, dir)), tbl.NumberedCount(dir); got != want {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d name records, want %d", dir, got, want)
		}
	}
	rank := map[NameConfidence]int{NameHigh: 3, NameMedium: 2, NameLow: 1, NameNone: 0}
	for i := range cur.Entries {
		e := &cur.Entries[i]
		if e.RebaseCode == "new" {
			continue
		}
		from, _ := strconv.ParseUint(e.RebaseFrom, 0, 32)
		o := entryAt(old, e.Direction, uint32(from))
		if o == nil || o.Name != e.Name {
			t.Errorf("%s %s: name %q, 70707 %s has %+v", e.Direction, e.Opcode, e.Name, e.RebaseFrom, o)
			continue
		}
		if r, ok := m[e.ID()]; ok && r.code != e.RebaseCode {
			t.Errorf("%s: rebase_code %s, map says %s", e.Opcode, e.RebaseCode, r.code)
		}
		moved := uint32(from) != e.ID()
		switch {
		case !moved || e.RebaseCode == "identical":
			if e.Confidence != o.Confidence {
				t.Errorf("%s: confidence %s, 70707 %s", e.Opcode, e.Confidence, o.Confidence)
			}
		case rank[o.Confidence] > rank[NameMedium]:
			if e.Confidence != NameMedium || e.Confidence70707 != o.Confidence {
				t.Errorf("%s moved on a shared body: confidence %s (70707 %s)", e.Opcode, e.Confidence, o.Confidence)
			}
		default:
			if e.Confidence != o.Confidence {
				t.Errorf("%s: confidence %s, 70707 %s", e.Opcode, e.Confidence, o.Confidence)
			}
		}
	}
}

func entryAt(n *Names, d Direction, op uint32) *PublicName {
	for i := range n.Entries {
		if n.Entries[i].Direction == d && n.Entries[i].ID() == op {
			return &n.Entries[i]
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// The session/world entries move with the rebase.
func Test70755SessionEntries(t *testing.T) {
	old, cur := bothTables(t)
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name     string
		old, new uint32
	}{
		{"CMSG_ENUM_CHARACTERS", 0x440014, 0x440014},
		{"SMSG_ENUM_CHARACTERS_RESULT", 0x470018, 0x470018},
		{"CMSG_AUTH_SESSION", 0x460001, 0x460001},
		{"SMSG_AUTH_CHALLENGE", 0x4E0000, 0x4E0000},
		{"CMSG_SERVER_TIME_OFFSET_REQUEST", 0x4400CA, 0x4400CC},
		{"CMSG_QUERY_REALM_NAME", 0x4400B5, 0x4400B7},
		{"CMSG_TUTORIAL", 0x44010C, 0x44010E},
		{"SMSG_LOGOUT_COMPLETE", 0x470131, 0x470132},
	} {
		for _, x := range []struct {
			tb   *Table
			want uint32
		}{{old, c.old}, {cur, c.new}} {
			_, id, err := x.tb.RequireID(c.name)
			if err != nil || id != x.want {
				t.Errorf("%s %s = %#08x, %v; want %#08x", x.tb.Protocol, c.name, id, err, x.want)
			}
		}
	}
}
```

`protocol/pktlog/pktlog.go`:

```go
// Package pktlog reads TrinityCore's PKT 3.1 packet log (PacketLogFile), the
// record the local fork writes of a real session: every frame the server
// logged, both directions, with the opcode number the server's own table gave
// it.
//
// The numbers are the *server's* enumeration, not the client's: the fork's
// SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT is 0x5c0000 where the client's is 0x5e0000. Bodies are
// the client's bytes unchanged, so a body is only meaningful next to the name
// it was logged under (tools/pktread.py in the server repo, or the table in
// protocol/opcodes for client numbers).
//
// See docs/EVIDENCE.md E38 (tools/worlddiff.py) for how the fork's log and the
// stock client's capture are compared.
package pktlog

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

// PKT 3.1 layout, as the fork writes it and tools/pktread.py reads it:
//
//	+0   [3]byte  magic "PKT"
//	+3   uint16   version 0x0301
//	+5   uint8    sniffer id
//	+6   uint32   build
//	+10  [4]byte  locale
//	+14  ...      forty bytes written as a struct with its own padding, skipped
//	+54  uint32   start unix seconds
//	+58  uint32   start tick milliseconds
//	+62  uint32   header option length, then that many bytes
//	..  packets
//
// Each packet is five little-endian uint32s (direction, connection id, tick
// milliseconds, option length, length), the option bytes, then the frame the
// server logged: uint32 opcode followed by the payload. direction is the
// ASCII tag "GSMC" (client to server) or "GSMS" (server to client) read as a
// little-endian uint32.
const (
	pktMagic     = "PKT"
	pktVersion   = 0x0301
	pktFixedHead = 3 + 2 + 1 + 4 + 4 + 40

	dirC2S = 0x47534D43 // "GSMC" as written by the logger
	dirS2C = 0x47534D53 // "GSMS"
)

// Dir is a packet's direction.
type Dir int

const (
	// C2S is client to server.
	C2S Dir = iota
	// S2C is server to client.
	S2C
)

// String returns "C2S" or "S2C".
func (d Dir) String() string {
	if d == C2S {
		return "C2S"
	}
	return "S2C"
}

// Packet is one logged frame.
type Packet struct {
	// Index is the packet's position in the log, from 0.
	Index int
	Dir   Dir
	// Conn is the connection id the server logged it on: 0 is the first
	// (realm) connection, 1 the instance connection CONNECT_TO names.
	Conn    int
	TicksMs uint32 // milliseconds, already rebased on the log's start ticks
	Opcode  uint32 // the number the server logged (its own core enumeration)
	Body    []byte
}

// TimeMs is the packet's timestamp relative to the log start.
func (p Packet) TimeMs() float64 { return float64(p.TicksMs) }

// Log is a parsed packet log.
type Log struct {
	Build  uint32
	Locale string
	Start  uint32 // unix seconds
	// StartTicks is the tick the log rebases on; packet timestamps are already
	// relative to it.
	StartTicks uint32
	Packets    []Packet
}

// ReadPKT parses a PKT 3.1 log.
func ReadPKT(raw []byte) (*Log, error) {
	if len(raw) < pktFixedHead+12 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pkt: %d bytes is shorter than the header", len(raw))
	}
	if string(raw[0:3]) != pktMagic {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pkt: magic is %q, want %q", raw[0:3], pktMagic)
	}
	if v := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(raw[3:5]); v != pktVersion {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pkt: version %#x, want %#x", v, pktVersion)
	}
	l := &Log{
		Build:  binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[6:10]),
		Locale: string(raw[10:14]),
	}
	off := pktFixedHead
	l.Start = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off:])
	l.StartTicks = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off+4:])
	opt := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off+8:])
	off += 12 + int(opt)
	if off > len(raw) {
		return nil, errors.New("pkt: header option runs past the file")
	}
	frame := 0
	for off+20 <= len(raw) {
		index := frame
		frame++
		dir := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off:])
		conn := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off+4:])
		ticks := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off+8:])
		optsize := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off+12:])
		length := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off+16:])
		off += 20
		off += int(optsize)
		if off+int(length) > len(raw) {
			break // a packet cut off by a live writer, as pktread.py says
		}
		if length < 4 {
			off += int(length)
			continue
		}
		op := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[off:])
		body := raw[off+4 : off+int(length)]
		off += int(length)
		var d Dir
		switch dir {
		case dirC2S:
			d = C2S
		case dirS2C:
			d = S2C
		default:
			continue
		}
		l.Packets = append(l.Packets, Packet{
			Index: index, Dir: d, Conn: int(conn), TicksMs: ticks - l.StartTicks, Opcode: op, Body: body,
		})
	}
	return l, nil
}

// ReadPKTFile parses a PKT file.
func ReadPKTFile(path string) (*Log, error) {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return ReadPKT(raw)
}

// LastLoginIndex is the index of the last CMSG_PLAYER_LOGIN in the log, given
// the name of an opcode number, or -1. A log usually holds more than one
// session (a character screen, a death, a logout and back in), and the live
// session is the last one.
func (l *Log) LastLoginIndex(name func(Dir, uint32) string) int {
	last := -1
	for i, p := range l.Packets {
		if p.Dir == C2S && name(p.Dir, p.Opcode) == "CMSG_PLAYER_LOGIN" {
			last = i
		}
	}
	return last
}

// Since returns the packets from index i on.
func (l *Log) Since(i int) []Packet {
	if i < 0 || i >= len(l.Packets) {
		return nil
	}
	return l.Packets[i:]
}

```

`protocol/pktlog/tail.go`:

```go
package pktlog

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
)

// Tail reads a PKT log the server is still writing: each Next returns the
// packets completed since the last call (the header is read on the first).
type Tail struct {
	f          *os.File
	buf        []byte
	header     bool
	startTicks uint32
	frame      int
}

// OpenTail opens a PKT log for tailing from its start.
func OpenTail(path string) (*Tail, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &Tail{f: f}, nil
}

// Close closes the file.
func (t *Tail) Close() error { return t.f.Close() }

// Next returns the packets that became complete.
func (t *Tail) Next() ([]Packet, error) {
	chunk := make([]byte, 1<<20)
	for {
		n, err := t.f.Read(chunk)
		t.buf = append(t.buf, chunk[:n]...)
		if err == io.EOF || n == 0 {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	off := 0
	if !t.header {
		if len(t.buf) < pktFixedHead+12 {
			return nil, nil
		}
		if string(t.buf[0:3]) != pktMagic {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pkt: magic is %q, want %q", t.buf[0:3], pktMagic)
		}
		opt := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(t.buf[pktFixedHead+8:])
		if len(t.buf) < pktFixedHead+12+int(opt) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		t.startTicks = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(t.buf[pktFixedHead+4:])
		off, t.header = pktFixedHead+12+int(opt), true
	}
	var out []Packet
	for off+20 <= len(t.buf) {
		le := binary.LittleEndian
		dir, conn, ticks := le.Uint32(t.buf[off:]), le.Uint32(t.buf[off+4:]), le.Uint32(t.buf[off+8:])
		optsize, length := le.Uint32(t.buf[off+12:]), le.Uint32(t.buf[off+16:])
		end := off + 20 + int(optsize) + int(length)
		if end > len(t.buf) {
			break
		}
		body := t.buf[off+20+int(optsize) : end]
		off = end
		index := t.frame
		t.frame++
		if length < 4 {
			continue
		}
		var d Dir
		switch dir {
		case dirC2S:
			d = C2S
		case dirS2C:
			d = S2C
		default:
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, Packet{Index: index, Dir: d, Conn: int(conn), TicksMs: ticks - t.startTicks,
			Opcode: le.Uint32(body), Body: append([]byte(nil), body[4:]...)})
	}
	t.buf = append(t.buf[:0], t.buf[off:]...)
	return out, nil
}
```

`protocol/pktlog/tail_test.go`:

```go
package pktlog

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// Tail over a file written in small pieces gives what ReadPKT gives at once.
func TestTailMatchesReadPKT(t *testing.T) {
	src := filepath.Join(os.Getenv("HOME"), "wow/server/wow-forever-tc/captures/2026-11-04-goldshire-70755.pkt")
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(src)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("no fork capture here:", err)
	}
	want, err := ReadPKT(raw)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "grow.pkt")
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer f.Close()
	tail, err := OpenTail(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var got []Packet
	for p := 0; p < len(raw); p += 777 {
		e := min(p+777, len(raw))
		f.Write(raw[p:e])
		pk, err := tail.Next()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		got = append(got, pk...)
	}
	if len(got) != len(want.Packets) {
		t.Fatalf("tail %d packets, ReadPKT %d", len(got), len(want.Packets))
	}
	for i := range got {
		if got[i].Opcode != want.Packets[i].Opcode || got[i].TicksMs != want.Packets[i].TicksMs || string(got[i].Body) != string(want.Packets[i].Body) {
			t.Fatalf("packet %d differs", i)
		}
	}
}
```

`protocol/spellstate/spellstate.go`:

```go
// Package spellstate tracks the player's cooldowns, charges, global cooldown
// and power from the world stream: what a rotation helper needs beside auras.
//
// The server does not send a cooldown per cast. Retail's capture of
// 2026-11-05 03:02 has 9 SMSG_SPELL_COOLDOWN against 1,363 casts: the client
// starts cooldowns itself from the spell's own data. So does this package:
// a cast of the player's (SPELL_GO) starts the spell's recovery, category
// recovery, charge and GCD from the game's tables (wago.tools CSV exports of
// SpellCooldowns, SpellCategories and SpellCategory), and the server's own
// messages correct it: forced cooldowns (SPELL_COOLDOWN), the login snapshot
// (SEND_SPELL_HISTORY, SEND_SPELL_CHARGES), charge state (SET_SPELL_CHARGES),
// clears, delta changes (MODIFY_COOLDOWN) and rate changes
// (UPDATE_CHARGE_CATEGORY_COOLDOWN, UPDATE_COOLDOWN). Haste is not known, so
// hasted cooldowns and the GCD run at their base length unless a rate
// message says otherwise.
//
// Power: SPELL_GO's remaining-power list for the player's casts sets it
// (authoritative), SPELL_ENERGIZE adds to it between casts.
package spellstate

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/codec"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/combatlog"
)

// SpellInfo is a spell's cooldown data.
type SpellInfo struct {
	Recovery    uint32 // ms, the spell's own cooldown
	CatRecovery uint32 // ms, its category's cooldown
	GCD         uint32 // ms, StartRecoveryTime
	Category    int32
	ChargeCat   int32
}

// Category is a cooldown or charge category.
type Category struct {
	Name           string
	MaxCharges     int
	ChargeRecovery uint32 // ms
}

// Data is the spell tables the tracker needs.
type Data struct {
	Spells     map[int32]SpellInfo
	Categories map[int32]Category
	Names      map[int32]string
	bycat      map[int32][]int32
}

// CategorySpells lists the spells of a cooldown or charge category (at most
// 20), so a consumer can tell which spells a category cooldown holds back.
func (d *Data) CategorySpells(c int32) []int32 {
	if d.bycat == nil {
		d.bycat = map[int32][]int32{}
		for id, s := range d.Spells {
			for i, k := range []int32{s.Category, s.ChargeCat} {
				if i == 1 && k == s.Category {
					continue
				}
				if k != 0 && len(d.bycat[k]) < 20 {
					d.bycat[k] = append(d.bycat[k], id)
				}
			}
		}
		for _, l := range d.bycat {
			sort.Slice(l, func(i, j int) bool { return l[i] < l[j] })
		}
	}
	return d.bycat[c]
}

// LoadWago reads SpellCooldowns.csv, SpellCategories.csv, SpellCategory.csv
// and (if present) SpellName.csv from dir: wago.tools exports, e.g.
// https://wago.tools/db2/SpellCooldowns/csv?build=12.1.5.70783. Rows for
// difficulty 0 win over others.
func LoadWago(dir string) (*Data, error) {
	d := &Data{Spells: map[int32]SpellInfo{}, Categories: map[int32]Category{}, Names: map[int32]string{}}
	cd, err := readCSV(filepath.Join(dir, "SpellCooldowns.csv"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, r := range cd.rows {
		if r.int("DifficultyID") != 0 {
			continue
		}
		id := int32(r.int("SpellID"))
		s := d.Spells[id]
		s.CatRecovery, s.Recovery, s.GCD = uint32(r.int("CategoryRecoveryTime")), uint32(r.int("RecoveryTime")), uint32(r.int("StartRecoveryTime"))
		d.Spells[id] = s
	}
	cats, err := readCSV(filepath.Join(dir, "SpellCategories.csv"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, r := range cats.rows {
		if r.int("DifficultyID") != 0 {
			continue
		}
		id := int32(r.int("SpellID"))
		s := d.Spells[id]
		s.Category, s.ChargeCat = int32(r.int("Category")), int32(r.int("ChargeCategory"))
		d.Spells[id] = s
	}
	cat, err := readCSV(filepath.Join(dir, "SpellCategory.csv"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	for _, r := range cat.rows {
		d.Categories[int32(r.int("ID"))] = Category{Name: r.str("Name_lang"), MaxCharges: r.int("MaxCharges"), ChargeRecovery: uint32(r.int("ChargeRecoveryTime"))}
	}
	if names, err := readCSV(filepath.Join(dir, "SpellName.csv")); err == nil {
		for _, r := range names.rows {
			d.Names[int32(r.int("ID"))] = r.str("Name_lang")
		}
	}
	return d, nil
}

type table struct{ rows []row }
type row struct {
	cols map[string]int
	v    []string
}

func (r row) str(c string) string {
	if i, ok := r.cols[c]; ok && i < len(r.v) {
		return r.v[i]
	}
	return ""
}
func (r row) int(c string) int { n, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.str(c)); return n }

func readCSV(path string) (*table, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	cr := csv.NewReader(f)
	cr.FieldsPerRecord = -1
	all, err := cr.ReadAll()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if len(all) == 0 {
		return &table{}, nil
	}
	cols := map[string]int{}
	for i, h := range all[0] {
		cols[h] = i
	}
	t := &table{}
	for _, v := range all[1:] {
		t.rows = append(t.rows, row{cols, v})
	}
	return t, nil
}

type charges struct {
	consumed int
	next     uint32 // log ms the next charge comes back (when consumed > 0)
}

// Tracker is the player's cooldown, charge, GCD and power state.
type Tracker struct {
	Data   *Data
	Player codec.GUID

	gcdEnd    uint32
	spell     map[int32]uint32 // spell -> ready at (log ms)
	cat       map[int32]uint32 // category -> ready at (for the casting spell's length)
	catStart  map[int32]uint32 // category -> when its cooldown started (from a cast)
	charge    map[int32]*charges
	rate      map[int32]float32 // charge category -> recovery length multiplier (1 = base, <1 faster)
	power     map[int8]int32
	maxPower  map[int8]int32
	powerSeen bool
}

// New returns a tracker over the spell tables (nil: server messages only).
func New(d *Data) *Tracker {
	if d == nil {
		d = &Data{Spells: map[int32]SpellInfo{}, Categories: map[int32]Category{}, Names: map[int32]string{}}
	}
	return &Tracker{Data: d, spell: map[int32]uint32{}, cat: map[int32]uint32{}, catStart: map[int32]uint32{}, charge: map[int32]*charges{},
		rate: map[int32]float32{}, power: map[int8]int32{}, maxPower: map[int8]int32{}}
}

// Event takes a combat log event; it returns whether the state changed.
func (tr *Tracker) Event(e combatlog.Event) bool {
	if tr.Player.IsEmpty() {
		return false
	}
	switch {
	case e.Sub == "SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS" && e.Source == tr.Player:
		for _, p := range e.Powers {
			tr.power[p.Type] = p.Amount
			tr.powerSeen = true
		}
		return tr.cast(e.SpellID, e.TimeMs) || len(e.Powers) > 0
	case (e.Sub == "SPELL_ENERGIZE" || e.Sub == "SPELL_PERIODIC_ENERGIZE") && e.Dest == tr.Player:
		// Amount is what was gained; Over is what was wasted past the cap,
		// so an overcap means the player is now at max: learn it from there.
		t := int8(e.School)
		tr.power[t] += int32(e.Amount)
		if e.Over > 0 {
			tr.maxPower[t] = tr.power[t]
		}
		if m := tr.maxPower[t]; m > 0 && tr.power[t] > m {
			tr.power[t] = m
		}
		tr.power[t] = max(tr.power[t], 0)
		tr.powerSeen = true
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func (tr *Tracker) chargeRecovery(c int32) uint32 {
	r := tr.Data.Categories[c].ChargeRecovery
	if f := tr.rate[c]; f > 0 {
		r = uint32(float32(r) * f)
	}
	return r
}

func (tr *Tracker) cast(id int32, t uint32) bool {
	s, ok := tr.Data.Spells[id]
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	if s.GCD > 0 {
		tr.gcdEnd = t + s.GCD
	}
	changed := s.GCD > 0
	if c := tr.Data.Categories[s.ChargeCat]; s.ChargeCat != 0 && c.MaxCharges > 0 {
		ch := tr.charges(s.ChargeCat, t)
		if ch.consumed == 0 {
			ch.next = t + tr.chargeRecovery(s.ChargeCat)
		}
		if ch.consumed < c.MaxCharges {
			ch.consumed++
		}
		changed = true
	} else if s.Recovery > 0 {
		tr.spell[id] = t + s.Recovery
		changed = true
	}
	if s.Category != 0 && s.CatRecovery > 0 && s.Category != s.ChargeCat {
		tr.cat[s.Category] = t + s.CatRecovery
		tr.catStart[s.Category] = t
		changed = true
	}
	return changed
}

// charges brings a charge category up to time t.
func (tr *Tracker) charges(c int32, t uint32) *charges {
	ch := tr.charge[c]
	if ch == nil {
		ch = &charges{}
		tr.charge[c] = ch
	}
	for ch.consumed > 0 && t >= ch.next {
		ch.consumed--
		if ch.consumed > 0 {
			ch.next += tr.chargeRecovery(c)
		}
	}
	return ch
}

// Message takes a server message (by its bare name); it returns whether it
// was a cooldown message and the state changed.
func (tr *Tracker) Message(name string, t uint32, body []byte) bool {
	r := codec.NewReader(body)
	u32 := func() uint32 { v, _ := r.Uint32(); return v }
	f32 := func() float32 { v, _ := r.Float32(); return v }
	switch name {
	case "SMSG_SPELL_COOLDOWN": // caster, u8 flags, n × {spell, forced ms, rate}
		g, err := r.GUID()
		if err != nil || g != tr.Player {
			return false
		}
		r.Uint8()
		n := u32()
		for i := uint32(0); i < n && r.Remaining() >= 12; i++ {
			id, forced := int32(u32()), u32()
			f32()
			if forced > 0 {
				tr.spell[id] = t + forced
			} else {
				tr.cast(id, t)
			}
		}
		return n > 0
	case "SMSG_SEND_SPELL_HISTORY": // n × {spell, item, category, recovery, cat recovery, rate, bits, offsets}
		n := u32()
		for i := uint32(0); i < n && r.Remaining() >= 25; i++ {
			id, _, cat := int32(u32()), u32(), int32(u32())
			rec, catRec := int32(u32()), int32(u32())
			f32()
			a, _ := r.Bit()
			b, _ := r.Bit()
			r.Bit()
			r.ResetBits()
			if a {
				u32()
			}
			if b {
				u32()
			}
			if rec > 0 {
				tr.spell[id] = t + uint32(rec)
			}
			if cat != 0 && catRec > 0 {
				tr.cat[cat] = t + uint32(catRec)
			}
		}
		return n > 0
	case "SMSG_SEND_SPELL_CHARGES": // n × {category, next recovery, rate, u8 consumed}
		n := u32()
		for i := uint32(0); i < n && r.Remaining() >= 13; i++ {
			c, next := int32(u32()), u32()
			rate := f32()
			used, _ := r.Uint8()
			tr.setCharges(c, t, next, int(used), rate)
		}
		return n > 0
	case "SMSG_SET_SPELL_CHARGES": // category, next recovery, u8 consumed, rate, bit
		if len(body) < 13 {
			return false
		}
		c, next := int32(u32()), u32()
		used, _ := r.Uint8()
		tr.setCharges(c, t, next, int(used), f32())
		return true
	case "SMSG_CLEAR_COOLDOWN":
		if len(body) >= 4 {
			id := int32(u32())
			delete(tr.spell, id)
			if s, ok := tr.Data.Spells[id]; ok && s.Category != 0 {
				delete(tr.cat, s.Category)
			}
			return true
		}
	case "SMSG_CLEAR_COOLDOWNS":
		n := u32()
		for i := uint32(0); i < n && r.Remaining() >= 4; i++ {
			delete(tr.spell, int32(u32()))
		}
		return n > 0
	case "SMSG_CLEAR_SPELL_CHARGES":
		if len(body) >= 4 {
			delete(tr.charge, int32(u32()))
			return true
		}
	case "SMSG_CLEAR_ALL_SPELL_CHARGES":
		tr.charge = map[int32]*charges{}
		return true
	case "SMSG_MODIFY_COOLDOWN":
		// retail's message under this name (by the group shift) is 13 bytes,
		// {category, float change, float rate, bit}: the charge-category rate
		// update (categories 1552/1553/1676 Fracture, Infernal Strike,
		// Immolation Aura in the 03:02 capture). The fork's is 9 bytes
		// {spell, i32 delta ms, bits}.
		switch len(body) {
		case 13:
			tr.speedUp(int32(u32()), f32(), t)
			return true
		case 9:
			id, delta := int32(u32()), int32(u32())
			if at, ok := tr.spell[id]; ok {
				tr.spell[id] = uint32(max(int64(at)+int64(delta), int64(t)))
			}
			return true
		}
	case "SMSG_UPDATE_CHARGE_CATEGORY_COOLDOWN":
		if len(body) >= 12 {
			tr.speedUp(int32(u32()), f32(), t)
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// speedUp applies a recovery speed change (ModChange: >1 faster, as haste
// rises; the capture's values sit between 0.94 and 1.04) to a charge
// category: the charge in flight and later ones.
func (tr *Tracker) speedUp(c int32, change float32, t uint32) {
	if change <= 0 {
		return
	}
	if ch := tr.charges(c, t); ch.consumed > 0 && ch.next > t {
		ch.next = t + uint32(float32(ch.next-t)/change)
	}
	m := tr.rate[c]
	if m == 0 {
		m = 1
	}
	tr.rate[c] = m / change
}

func (tr *Tracker) setCharges(c int32, t, next uint32, used int, rate float32) {
	ch := tr.charges(c, t)
	ch.consumed = used
	ch.next = t + next
	if rate > 0 {
		tr.rate[c] = rate
	}
}

// Cooldown is one spell or category that is not ready.
type Cooldown struct {
	Spell       int32   `json:"spell,omitempty"`
	Category    int32   `json:"category,omitempty"`
	Name        string  `json:"name,omitempty"`
	RemainingMs uint32  `json:"remaining_ms"`
	Charges     *int    `json:"charges,omitempty"`     // available now, for charge categories
	MaxCharges  int     `json:"max_charges,omitempty"` // for charge categories
	Spells      []int32 `json:"spells,omitempty"`      // for categories: the spells it holds back
}

// GCD returns the GCD left at t.
func (tr *Tracker) GCD(t uint32) uint32 {
	if tr.gcdEnd > t {
		return tr.gcdEnd - t
	}
	return 0
}

// Cooldowns returns everything still recovering at t: spells, categories
// (by one spell that uses them, for a name) and charge categories with a
// charge missing. Anything absent is ready.
func (tr *Tracker) Cooldowns(t uint32) []Cooldown {
	var out []Cooldown
	for id, at := range tr.spell {
		if at > t {
			out = append(out, Cooldown{Spell: id, Name: tr.Data.Names[id], RemainingMs: at - t})
		} else {
			delete(tr.spell, id)
		}
	}
	for c, at := range tr.cat {
		start, cast := tr.catStart[c]
		if !cast {
			if at > t {
				out = append(out, Cooldown{Category: c, Name: tr.Data.Categories[c].Name, RemainingMs: at - t, Spells: tr.Data.CategorySpells(c)})
			} else {
				delete(tr.cat, c)
			}
			continue
		}
		// One start, a length per spell: Blade Dance (15 s) and Death Sweep
		// (9 s) share category 1640, so Death Sweep is ready 9 s after either.
		byLen := map[uint32][]int32{}
		var longest uint32
		for _, id := range tr.Data.CategorySpells(c) {
			if l := tr.Data.Spells[id].CatRecovery; l > 0 {
				byLen[l] = append(byLen[l], id)
				longest = max(longest, l)
			}
		}
		if start+longest <= t {
			delete(tr.cat, c)
			delete(tr.catStart, c)
			continue
		}
		for l, ids := range byLen {
			if start+l <= t {
				continue
			}
			cd := Cooldown{Category: c, Name: tr.Data.Categories[c].Name, RemainingMs: start + l - t, Spells: ids}
			if len(byLen) > 1 && len(ids) == 1 {
				cd.Spell, cd.Name = ids[0], tr.Data.Names[ids[0]]
			}
			out = append(out, cd)
		}
	}
	for c := range tr.charge {
		ch := tr.charges(c, t)
		if ch.consumed == 0 {
			continue
		}
		maxc := tr.Data.Categories[c].MaxCharges
		left := max(maxc-ch.consumed, 0)
		out = append(out, Cooldown{Category: c, Name: tr.Data.Categories[c].Name, RemainingMs: ch.next - t,
			Charges: &left, MaxCharges: maxc, Spells: tr.Data.CategorySpells(c)})
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].RemainingMs < out[j].RemainingMs })
	return out
}

// Power returns the known power amounts by type, and whether any is known.
func (tr *Tracker) Power() (map[int8]int32, bool) {
	out := map[int8]int32{}
	for k, v := range tr.power {
		out[k] = v
	}
	return out, tr.powerSeen
}

// SpellCategories returns the cooldown and charge categories of a spell, so
// a consumer can tell a spell is not ready because its category is cooling.
func (tr *Tracker) SpellCategories(id int32) (cat, chargeCat int32) {
	s := tr.Data.Spells[id]
	return s.Category, s.ChargeCat
}

// PowerNames names the power types a rotation is likely to read.
var PowerNames = map[int8]string{0: "mana", 1: "rage", 2: "focus", 3: "energy", 4: "combo_points", 5: "runes",
	6: "runic_power", 7: "soul_shards", 8: "lunar_power", 9: "holy_power", 11: "maelstrom", 12: "chi",
	13: "insanity", 16: "arcane_charges", 17: "fury", 18: "pain", 19: "essence"}
```

```go
package spellstate

import (
	"encoding/hex"
	"testing"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/codec"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/combatlog"

// Retail 12.1.5.70783 data for three Vengeance spells (wago.tools CSVs):
// Fracture 263642 charge category 1552 (2 charges, 5.5 s), Spirit Bomb
// 247454 category 2455 (25 s), Soul Cleave 228477 (GCD only).
func data() *Data {
	return &Data{
		Spells: map[int32]SpellInfo{
			263642: {GCD: 1500, ChargeCat: 1552},
			247454: {GCD: 1500, Category: 2455, CatRecovery: 25000},
			228477: {GCD: 1500},
		},
		Categories: map[int32]Category{1552: {Name: "Demon Hunter - Fracture", MaxCharges: 2, ChargeRecovery: 5500}, 2455: {Name: "Demon Hunter - Spirit Bomb"}},
		Names:      map[int32]string{},
	}
}

func cast(tr *Tracker, spell int32, t uint32, fury int32) {
	tr.Event(combatlog.Event{TimeMs: t, Sub: "SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS", Source: tr.Player, SpellID: spell, Powers: []combatlog.Power{{Type: 17, Amount: fury}}})
}

func find(cds []Cooldown, cat int32) *Cooldown {
	for i := range cds {
		if cds[i].Category == cat {
			return &cds[i]
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func TestChargesGCDCategoryAndFury(t *testing.T) {
	tr := New(data())
	tr.Player = codec.GUID{Hi: 0x0801180000000000, Lo: 9}

	cast(tr, 263642, 0, 28)
	if g := tr.GCD(100); g != 1400 {
		t.Errorf("GCD at 100 ms: %d", g)
	}
	c := find(tr.Cooldowns(100), 1552)
	if c == nil || *c.Charges != 1 || c.RemainingMs != 5400 {
		t.Fatalf("one Fracture used: %+v", c)
	}
	cast(tr, 263642, 2000, 56)
	if c := find(tr.Cooldowns(2000), 1552); *c.Charges != 0 || c.RemainingMs != 3500 {
		t.Errorf("both used: %+v", c)
	}
	// the first charge returns at 5.5 s, the second 5.5 s after that
	if c := find(tr.Cooldowns(6000), 1552); *c.Charges != 1 || c.RemainingMs != 5000 {
		t.Errorf("one back: %+v", c)
	}
	if find(tr.Cooldowns(11000), 1552) != nil {
		t.Errorf("both back by 11 s")
	}

	cast(tr, 247454, 20000, 26)
	if c := find(tr.Cooldowns(21000), 2455); c == nil || c.RemainingMs != 24000 {
		t.Errorf("Spirit Bomb category: %+v", c)
	}
	if p, _ := tr.Power(); p[17] != 26 {
		t.Errorf("fury after Spirit Bomb: %v", p)
	}
	tr.Event(combatlog.Event{TimeMs: 21500, Sub: "SPELL_ENERGIZE", Dest: tr.Player, SpellID: 263642, School: 17, Amount: 28})
	if p, _ := tr.Power(); p[17] != 54 {
		t.Errorf("fury after +28: %v", p)
	}
	// Demon Blades at the cap, as retail logs it: 2 gained, 13 wasted. The
	// waste is not a spend: fury goes up by 2 and that is the max from now on.
	tr.Event(combatlog.Event{TimeMs: 22000, Sub: "SPELL_ENERGIZE", Dest: tr.Player, SpellID: 203796, School: 17, Amount: 2, Over: 13})
	if p, _ := tr.Power(); p[17] != 56 {
		t.Errorf("fury after an overcap: %v", p)
	}
	tr.Event(combatlog.Event{TimeMs: 22500, Sub: "SPELL_ENERGIZE", Dest: tr.Player, SpellID: 203796, School: 17, Amount: 0, Over: 15})
	tr.Event(combatlog.Event{TimeMs: 23000, Sub: "SPELL_ENERGIZE", Dest: tr.Player, SpellID: 263642, School: 17, Amount: 20})
	if p, _ := tr.Power(); p[17] != 56 {
		t.Errorf("fury past the learned cap: %v", p)
	}
}

// Server messages from the retail capture of 2026-11-05 03:02 (no GUIDs in
// these bodies): Metamorphosis's charge category 2469 with 106,292 ms to go
// and one charge used; a recovery speed change of 1.0104 for Fracture (1552).
func TestRetailServerMessages(t *testing.T) {
	d := data()
	d.Categories[2469] = Category{Name: "Demon Hunter - Metamorphosis (Vengeance)", MaxCharges: 1, ChargeRecovery: 120000}
	tr := New(d)
	tr.Player = codec.GUID{Lo: 1}

	set, _ := hex.DecodeString("a5090000349f0100010000803f00")
	if !tr.Message("SMSG_SET_SPELL_CHARGES", 1000, set) {
		t.Fatal("SET_SPELL_CHARGES not taken")
	}
	if c := find(tr.Cooldowns(1000), 2469); c == nil || c.RemainingMs != 106292 || *c.Charges != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Metamorphosis: %+v", c)
	}

	cast(tr, 263642, 0, 0)
	rate, _ := hex.DecodeString("11060000ae47813f0000803f00") // category 0x611 is Infernal Strike: no effect on 1552
	tr.Message("SMSG_MODIFY_COOLDOWN", 500, rate)
	if c := find(tr.Cooldowns(500), 1552); c.RemainingMs != 5000 {
		t.Errorf("another category's rate moved Fracture: %+v", c)
	}
	frac, _ := hex.DecodeString("10060000ae47813f0000803f00") // 0x610 = 1552, change 1.01
	tr.Message("SMSG_MODIFY_COOLDOWN", 500, frac)
	if c := find(tr.Cooldowns(500), 1552); c.RemainingMs != 4950 { // 5000 / 1.01
		t.Errorf("Fracture after a 1.01 speed-up: %+v", c)
	}
}

// Blade Dance and Death Sweep share category 1640 with lengths of 15 s and
// 9 s (retail tables): after a Blade Dance, Death Sweep is ready at 9 s.
func TestSharedCategoryLengths(t *testing.T) {
	d := data()
	d.Spells[188499] = SpellInfo{GCD: 1500, Category: 1640, CatRecovery: 15000}
	d.Spells[210152] = SpellInfo{GCD: 1500, Category: 1640, CatRecovery: 9000}
	d.Names[188499], d.Names[210152] = "Blade Dance", "Death Sweep"
	tr := New(d)
	tr.Player = codec.GUID{Lo: 1}
	cast(tr, 188499, 0, 0)
	got := map[int32]uint32{}
	for _, c := range tr.Cooldowns(5000) {
		got[c.Spell] = c.RemainingMs
	}
	if got[188499] != 10000 || got[210152] != 4000 {
		t.Fatalf("at 5 s: %v", got)
	}
	for _, c := range tr.Cooldowns(9500) {
		if c.Spell == 210152 {
			t.Fatalf("Death Sweep still listed at 9.5 s: %+v", c)
		}
	}
}
```

`protocol/updateobject/apply/apply.go`:

```go
// Package apply replays a decoded SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT into the world model
// (package state).
//
// Mapping (docs/STATE_SCHEMA.md): position and facing come from the create
// block's movement section; entry from ObjectData; class, race, level,
// health, max health and target from UnitData; name from PlayerData. A game
// object's display, type, state, flags, faction and level come from
// GameObjectData and its rotation from the create block; an item's owner,
// container, stack count and durability from ItemData. The client's
// ThisIsYou flag sets the session's self GUID.
//
// A values block whose later struct cannot be decoded (an unsupported
// PlayerData bit, say) still applies the structs before it: the client reads
// them in a fixed order, so they are exact. The block is reported in
// Result.Skipped and in Result.Updated.
//
// Not mapped, on purpose:
//   - power: UnitData.Power[i] is indexed by the class's power slot, and the
//     slot -> power type table (ChrClassesXPowerTypes) is client data this
//     package does not have; state keys power by type name. The raw slots
//     are kept in updateobject.UnitData.
//   - auras: they are not update fields in this client (SMSG_AURA_UPDATE
//     carries them), so an update leaves an object's auras as they were.
//
// Objects are keyed by the full 128-bit wire GUID. The low half alone is not
// unique: players and creatures number their low halves independently, and
// in the 70755 Goldshire capture the player and a creature both have low
// half 3.
package apply

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/updateobject"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/state"
)

// Skip is a block (or part of one) that was not applied, and why.
type Skip struct {
	GUID updateobject.GUID
	Type updateobject.BlockType
	Err  error
}

func (s Skip) Error() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%v block for %v: %v", s.Type, s.GUID, s.Err) }

// Result reports what Apply did.
type Result struct {
	Created []state.GUID
	Updated []state.GUID
	Removed []state.GUID
	Skipped []Skip
}

// GUIDOf maps a wire GUID to the state key.
func GUIDOf(g updateobject.GUID) state.GUID { return state.GUID{Hi: g.Hi, Lo: g.Lo} }

var kinds = map[updateobject.ObjectType]state.Kind{
	updateobject.TypeItem:                 state.KindItem,
	updateobject.TypeContainer:            state.KindContainer,
	updateobject.TypeAzeriteEmpoweredItem: state.KindItem,
	updateobject.TypeAzeriteItem:          state.KindItem,
	updateobject.TypeUnit:                 state.KindUnit,
	updateobject.TypePlayer:               state.KindPlayer,
	updateobject.TypeActivePlayer:         state.KindPlayer,
	updateobject.TypeGameObject:           state.KindGameObject,
	updateobject.TypeDynamicObject:        state.KindDynamicObject,
	updateobject.TypeCorpse:               state.KindCorpse,
	updateobject.TypeAreaTrigger:          state.KindAreaTrigger,
	updateobject.TypeSceneObject:          state.KindSceneObject,
	updateobject.TypeConversation:         state.KindConversation,
}

// ErrNoKind marks an object type the state model has no kind for.
var ErrNoKind = errors.New("apply: object type has no state kind")

// ErrUnknownObject marks a values block for an object the state does not
// hold (the client skips these by their size too).
var ErrUnknownObject = errors.New("apply: values for an unknown object")

// Apply applies u to s. Blocks that cannot be applied are reported in
// Result.Skipped; the rest still apply.
func Apply(s *state.State, u *updateobject.UpdateObject) Result {
	var res Result
	if rm := u.Removed; rm != nil {
		self := s.Self()
		for _, list := range [][]updateobject.GUID{rm.Destroyed, rm.OutOfRange} {
			for _, g := range list {
				// The client never removes its own player this way
				// (0x102cd627c skips the active player's GUID).
				if k := GUIDOf(g); k != self && s.Remove(k) {
					res.Removed = append(res.Removed, k)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	for _, b := range u.Blocks {
		switch {
		case b.Create != nil:
			applyCreate(s, b, &res)
		case b.Values != nil:
			applyValues(s, b, &res)
		}
	}
	return res
}

func applyCreate(s *state.State, b updateobject.Block, res *Result) {
	c := b.Create
	kind, ok := kinds[c.ObjectType]
	if !ok {
		res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, Skip{b.GUID, b.Type, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d", ErrNoKind, c.ObjectType)})
		return
	}
	key := GUIDOf(b.GUID)
	o, existed := s.Object(key)
	o.GUID, o.Kind = key, kind
	if m := c.Movement; m != nil {
		var p *updateobject.Pos4
		switch {
		case m.Movement != nil:
			p = &m.Movement.Info.Position
		case m.Stationary != nil:
			p = m.Stationary
		}
		if p != nil {
			o.Position = state.Vec3{X: p.X, Y: p.Y, Z: p.Z}
			o.Facing = p.O
		}
	}
	of, err := c.DecodeFields()
	if err != nil {
		res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, Skip{b.GUID, b.Type, err})
	} else {
		applyFields(&o, of)
	}
	if kind == state.KindGameObject && c.Movement != nil && c.Movement.Rotation != nil {
		if o.GameObject == nil {
			o.GameObject = &state.GameObjectInfo{}
		}
		q := updateobject.UnpackRotation(*c.Movement.Rotation)
		o.GameObject.Rotation = state.Quat{X: q.X, Y: q.Y, Z: q.Z, W: q.W}
	}
	o.Updated = time.Time{} // Upsert stamps it
	s.Upsert(o)
	if c.Movement != nil && c.Movement.ThisIsYou {
		s.SetSelf(key)
	}
	if existed {
		res.Updated = append(res.Updated, key)
	} else {
		res.Created = append(res.Created, key)
	}
}

func applyFields(o *state.Object, of *updateobject.ObjectFields) {
	if of.Object != nil {
		o.Entry = uint32(of.Object.EntryID)
	}
	if of.Unit != nil {
		applyUnit(o, of.Unit.Fields)
	}
	if of.Player != nil && of.Player.Name != "" {
		o.Name = of.Player.Name
	}
	if of.Player != nil {
		applyPlayer(o, of.Player.Fields)
	}
	if of.GameObject != nil {
		if o.GameObject == nil {
			o.GameObject = &state.GameObjectInfo{}
		}
		applyGameObject(o.GameObject, of.GameObject.Fields)
	}
	if of.Item != nil {
		if o.Item == nil {
			o.Item = &state.ItemInfo{}
		}
		applyItem(o.Item, of.Item.Fields)
	}
}

func applyGameObject(g *state.GameObjectInfo, fields []updateobject.Field) {
	for _, f := range fields {
		switch f.Name {
		case "DisplayID":
			g.Display = uint32(f.Value.(int32))
		case "TypeID":
			g.Type = f.Value.(int8)
		case "State":
			g.State = f.Value.(int8)
		case "Flags":
			g.Flags = f.Value.(uint32)
		case "FactionTemplate":
			g.Faction = uint32(f.Value.(int32))
		case "Level":
			g.Level = f.Value.(int32)
		case "ArtKit":
			g.ArtKit = f.Value.(uint32)
		case "PercentHealth":
			g.PercentHealth = f.Value.(uint8)
		case "CreatedBy":
			g.CreatedBy = GUIDOf(f.Value.(updateobject.GUID))
		}
	}
}

func applyItem(it *state.ItemInfo, fields []updateobject.Field) {
	for _, f := range fields {
		switch f.Name {
		case "Owner":
			it.Owner = GUIDOf(f.Value.(updateobject.GUID))
		case "ContainedIn":
			it.ContainedIn = GUIDOf(f.Value.(updateobject.GUID))
		case "StackCount":
			it.StackCount = f.Value.(uint32)
		case "Durability":
			it.Durability = f.Value.(uint32)
		case "MaxDurability":
			it.MaxDurability = f.Value.(uint32)
		case "DynamicFlags":
			it.DynamicFlags = f.Value.(uint32)
		}
	}
}

// applyUnit copies the UnitData fields state models.
func applyUnit(o *state.Object, fields []updateobject.Field) {
	for _, f := range fields {
		switch f.Name {
		case "Health":
			o.Health = f.Value.(int64)
		case "MaxHealth":
			o.MaxHealth = f.Value.(int64)
		case "Level":
			if l := f.Value.(int32); l >= 0 && l <= 255 {
				o.Level = uint8(l)
			}
		case "ClassId":
			o.Class = f.Value.(uint8)
		case "Race":
			o.Race = f.Value.(uint8)
		case "Target":
			o.Target = GUIDOf(f.Value.(updateobject.GUID))
		case "NpcFlags":
			o.NpcFlags = f.Value.(uint32)
		}
	}
}

// valuesType is the object type a values block is decoded as. The state
// keeps the kind, not the create's object type; the kinds with more than
// one type are told apart by the self GUID (players) or default to the
// plain type (items).
func valuesType(s *state.State, key state.GUID, k state.Kind) (updateobject.ObjectType, bool) {
	switch k {
	case state.KindPlayer:
		if key == s.Self() {
			return updateobject.TypeActivePlayer, true
		}
		return updateobject.TypePlayer, true
	case state.KindUnit:
		return updateobject.TypeUnit, true
	case state.KindGameObject:
		return updateobject.TypeGameObject, true
	case state.KindItem:
		return updateobject.TypeItem, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

func applyValues(s *state.State, b updateobject.Block, res *Result) {
	key := GUIDOf(b.GUID)
	o, ok := s.Object(key)
	if !ok {
		res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, Skip{b.GUID, b.Type, ErrUnknownObject})
		return
	}
	t, ok := valuesType(s, key, o.Kind)
	if !ok {
		res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, Skip{b.GUID, b.Type, fmt.Errorf("%w: values for a %s", updateobject.ErrUnsupported, o.Kind)})
		return
	}
	d, err := updateobject.DecodeValues(t, b.Values)
	if err != nil {
		res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, Skip{b.GUID, b.Type, err})
		if d == nil || (d.Object == nil && d.Unit == nil && d.GameObject == nil && d.Item == nil) {
			return
		}
	}
	if err := s.Mutate(key, func(o *state.Object) {
		for _, f := range d.Object {
			if f.Name == "EntryID" {
				o.Entry = uint32(f.Value.(int32))
			}
		}
		applyUnit(o, d.Unit)
		applyPlayer(o, d.Player)
		if d.GameObject != nil {
			if o.GameObject == nil {
				o.GameObject = &state.GameObjectInfo{}
			}
			applyGameObject(o.GameObject, d.GameObject)
		}
		if d.Item != nil {
			if o.Item == nil {
				o.Item = &state.ItemInfo{}
			}
			applyItem(o.Item, d.Item)
		}
	}); err != nil {
		res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, Skip{b.GUID, b.Type, err})
		return
	}
	res.Updated = append(res.Updated, key)
}

// applyPlayer copies the PlayerData fields state models: the item id in each
// visible equipment slot ("VisibleItems.ItemID[n]").
func applyPlayer(o *state.Object, fields []updateobject.Field) {
	const pre = "VisibleItems.ItemID["
	for _, f := range fields {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(f.Name, pre) || !strings.HasSuffix(f.Name, "]") {
			continue
		}
		slot, err := strconv.Atoi(f.Name[len(pre) : len(f.Name)-1])
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		id, _ := f.Value.(int32)
		if id == 0 {
			delete(o.Equipment, slot)
			continue
		}
		if o.Equipment == nil {
			o.Equipment = map[int]int32{}
		}
		o.Equipment[slot] = id
	}
}

```

`protocol/updateobject/apply/apply_test.go`:

```go
package apply

import (
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"flag"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/updateobject"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/state"
)

var update = flag.Bool("update", false, "rewrite testdata/*.hex")

// Wire GUIDs: a player (high type 0x08) and a creature.
var (
	selfGUID     = updateobject.GUID{Lo: 0x2A, Hi: 0x0800000000000000}
	creatureGUID = updateobject.GUID{Lo: 0x00000000000F4A11, Hi: 0x2040000000000000}
)

// selfCreate is a synthetic create of the player's own character with the
// client's real layouts: the movement section of TestActivePlayerGolden,
// field flags Owner|PartyMember (what the fork sends a player about
// itself), fragments CGObject + Tag_Unit + Tag_Player, and the
// Object/Unit/Player chain. ActivePlayerData, which is not decoded, is an
// opaque tail.
func selfCreate(t *testing.T) *updateobject.UpdateObject {
	speeds := [9]float32{2.5, 7, 4.5, 4.722222, 2.5, 7, 4.5, 3.141594, 3.141594}
	mv := &updateobject.CreateMovement{
		ThisIsYou: true,
		Movement: &updateobject.MovementUpdate{
			Info: updateobject.MovementInfo{
				Mover:           selfGUID,
				MoveTime:        1000,
				Position:        updateobject.Pos4{X: -8949.95, Y: -132.493, Z: 83.5312, O: 0.5},
				MoveIndex:       7,
				GravityModifier: 1,
			},
			Speeds:       speeds,
			ForcesModMag: 1,
		},
		ActivePlayer: &updateobject.ActivePlayerCreate{},
	}
	data, err := updateobject.BuildFragmentData(updateobject.TypeActivePlayer, updateobject.FlagOwner|updateobject.FlagPartyMember, updateobject.Fields{
		Object: map[string]any{"EntryID": int32(0), "DynamicFlags": uint32(0), "Scale": float32(1)},
		Unit: map[string]any{
			"DisplayID": int32(49), "NativeDisplayID": int32(49),
			"Race": uint8(1), "ClassId": uint8(1), "PlayerClassId": uint8(1), "Sex": uint8(0), "DisplayPower": uint8(1),
			"Health": int64(250), "MaxHealth": int64(300), "Level": int32(12), "EffectiveLevel": int32(12),
			"FactionTemplate": int32(1), "MaxPower[1]": int32(1000),
			"BoundingRadius": float32(0.389), "CombatReach": float32(1.5), "DisplayScale": float32(1),
			"NativeXDisplayScale": float32(1), "ModCastingSpeed": float32(1), "ModCastingSpeedNeg": float32(1),
			"ModHaste": float32(1), "ModSpellHaste": float32(1), "ModRangedHaste": float32(1), "ModHasteRegen": float32(1),
			"ModTimeRate": float32(1), "MaxHealthModifier": float32(1), "HoverHeight": float32(1),
			"AttackRoundBaseTime[0]": uint32(2000), "AttackRoundBaseTime[1]": uint32(2000),
			"Target": creatureGUID,
		},
		Player: map[string]any{
			"WowAccount":                     updateobject.GUID{Lo: 0x1001, Hi: 0x0C00000000000000},
			"PlayerFlags":                    uint32(0x8),
			"Name.len":                       uint64(4),
			"Name":                           "Jack",
			"SuperDistrict.SuperDistrictID":  uint32(2),
			"SuperDistrict2.SuperDistrictID": uint32(2),
		},
		ActivePlayerRaw: make([]byte, 64),
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return &updateobject.UpdateObject{MapID: 0, Flag7: true, Blocks: []updateobject.Block{{
		Type: updateobject.BlockCreateObject2,
		GUID: selfGUID,
		Create: &updateobject.CreateBlock{
			ObjectType:   updateobject.TypeActivePlayer,
			Movement:     mv,
			FieldFlags:   updateobject.FlagOwner | updateobject.FlagPartyMember,
			Fragments:    []uint8{updateobject.FragmentCGObject, updateobject.FragmentTagUnit, updateobject.FragmentTagPlayer},
			FragmentData: data,
		},
	}}}
}

// golden checks b against testdata/name (or rewrites it with -update) and
// returns the stored bytes, so the regression runs on the recorded message.
func golden(t *testing.T, name string, b []byte) []byte {
	path := "testdata/" + name
	if *update {
		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(hex.EncodeToString(b)+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	h, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want, err := hex.DecodeString(strings.TrimSpace(string(h)))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if hex.EncodeToString(b) != hex.EncodeToString(want) {
		t.Fatalf("%s: encoder output changed; rerun with -update if intended", name)
	}
	return want
}

func mustApply(t *testing.T, s *state.State, msg []byte) Result {
	t.Helper()
	u, err := updateobject.Decode(msg)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return Apply(s, u)
}

// TestActivePlayerPipeline is the pipeline regression test: bytes ->
// updateobject.Decode -> Apply -> state snapshot.
func TestActivePlayerPipeline(t *testing.T) {
	s := state.New()
	msg := golden(t, "active_player_create.hex", updateobject.Encode(selfCreate(t)))
	res := mustApply(t, s, msg)
	if len(res.Skipped) != 0 || len(res.Created) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("result %+v", res)
	}
	snap := s.Snapshot()
	if snap.Self != GUIDOf(selfGUID) {
		t.Fatalf("self %v", snap.Self)
	}
	if len(snap.Objects) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d objects", len(snap.Objects))
	}
	o := snap.Objects[0]
	want := state.Object{
		GUID: GUIDOf(selfGUID), Kind: state.KindPlayer, Name: "Jack", Level: 12, Class: 1, Race: 1,
		Position: state.Vec3{X: -8949.95, Y: -132.493, Z: 83.5312}, Facing: 0.5,
		Health: 250, MaxHealth: 300, Target: GUIDOf(creatureGUID),
	}
	o.Updated = want.Updated
	if o.Auras != nil || o.Power != nil {
		t.Fatalf("auras/power invented: %+v", o)
	}
	o.Auras, o.Power = nil, nil
	if !equalObject(o, want) {
		t.Fatalf("snapshot object\n got %+v\nwant %+v", o, want)
	}

	// Auras come from elsewhere (SMSG_AURA_UPDATE); an update must keep them.
	if err := s.Mutate(GUIDOf(selfGUID), func(o *state.Object) { o.Auras = []string{"Battle Shout"} }); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// A values update: health and level.
	vals, err := updateobject.BuildValues(nil, map[string]any{"Health": int64(180), "Level": int32(13)}, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	upd := golden(t, "active_player_values.hex", updateobject.Encode(&updateobject.UpdateObject{Flag7: true, Blocks: []updateobject.Block{
		{Type: updateobject.BlockValues, GUID: selfGUID, Values: &updateobject.ValuesBlock{Data: vals}},
	}}))
	res = mustApply(t, s, upd)
	if len(res.Skipped) != 0 || len(res.Updated) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("update result %+v", res)
	}
	o, _ = s.Object(GUIDOf(selfGUID))
	if o.Health != 180 || o.Level != 13 || o.MaxHealth != 300 || len(o.Auras) != 1 || o.Auras[0] != "Battle Shout" {
		t.Fatalf("after update %+v", o)
	}
}

func equalObject(a, b state.Object) bool {
	return a.GUID == b.GUID && a.Kind == b.Kind && a.Name == b.Name && a.Level == b.Level && a.Class == b.Class &&
		a.Race == b.Race && a.Position == b.Position && a.Facing == b.Facing && a.Health == b.Health &&
		a.MaxHealth == b.MaxHealth && a.Target == b.Target && a.Entry == b.Entry
}

// TestCreateUpdateRemove runs a creature through create -> update -> remove.
func TestCreateUpdateRemove(t *testing.T) {
	s := state.New()
	data, err := updateobject.BuildFragmentData(updateobject.TypeUnit, 0, updateobject.Fields{
		Object: map[string]any{"EntryID": int32(299), "Scale": float32(1)},
		Unit:   map[string]any{"Health": int64(42), "MaxHealth": int64(42), "Level": int32(2), "ClassId": uint8(1)},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	create := &updateobject.UpdateObject{Blocks: []updateobject.Block{{
		Type: updateobject.BlockCreateObject2, GUID: creatureGUID,
		Create: &updateobject.CreateBlock{
			ObjectType:   updateobject.TypeUnit,
			Movement:     &updateobject.CreateMovement{Stationary: &updateobject.Pos4{X: 10, Y: 20, Z: 30, O: 1}},
			Fragments:    []uint8{updateobject.FragmentCGObject, updateobject.FragmentTagUnit},
			FragmentData: data,
		},
	}}}
	res := mustApply(t, s, updateobject.Encode(create))
	key := GUIDOf(creatureGUID)
	if len(res.Created) != 1 || res.Created[0] != key || len(res.Skipped) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("create %+v", res)
	}
	o, _ := s.Object(key)
	if o.Kind != state.KindUnit || o.Entry != 299 || o.Health != 42 || o.Position != (state.Vec3{X: 10, Y: 20, Z: 30}) {
		t.Fatalf("created %+v", o)
	}

	vals, err := updateobject.BuildValues(nil, map[string]any{"Health": int64(0), "Target": selfGUID}, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res = mustApply(t, s, updateobject.Encode(&updateobject.UpdateObject{Blocks: []updateobject.Block{
		{Type: updateobject.BlockValues, GUID: creatureGUID, Values: &updateobject.ValuesBlock{Data: vals}},
		{Type: updateobject.BlockValues, GUID: updateobject.GUID{Lo: 999}, Values: &updateobject.ValuesBlock{Data: vals}},
	}}))
	if len(res.Updated) != 1 || len(res.Skipped) != 1 || !errors.Is(res.Skipped[0].Err, ErrUnknownObject) {
		t.Fatalf("update %+v", res)
	}
	o, _ = s.Object(key)
	if o.Health != 0 || o.MaxHealth != 42 || o.Target != GUIDOf(selfGUID) {
		t.Fatalf("updated %+v", o)
	}

	res = mustApply(t, s, updateobject.Encode(&updateobject.UpdateObject{Removed: &updateobject.RemovedObjects{Destroyed: []updateobject.GUID{creatureGUID}}}))
	if len(res.Removed) != 1 || s.Len() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("remove %+v, %d objects left", res, s.Len())
	}
}

// TestUnsupportedBlocksAreReported checks that a block we cannot decode is
// skipped with ErrUnsupported while the rest of the message applies.
func TestUnsupportedBlocksAreReported(t *testing.T) {
	s := state.New()
	u := &updateobject.UpdateObject{Blocks: []updateobject.Block{
		{Type: updateobject.BlockCreateObject, GUID: updateobject.GUID{Lo: 7}, Create: &updateobject.CreateBlock{
			ObjectType:   updateobject.TypeCorpse,
			Movement:     &updateobject.CreateMovement{Stationary: &updateobject.Pos4{X: 1}},
			Fragments:    []uint8{updateobject.FragmentCGObject, 208},
			FragmentData: []byte{1, 0, 0, 0, 0},
		}},
	}}
	res := mustApply(t, s, updateobject.Encode(u))
	if len(res.Skipped) != 1 || !errors.Is(res.Skipped[0].Err, updateobject.ErrUnsupported) {
		t.Fatalf("result %+v", res)
	}
	if o, ok := s.Object(state.LowGUID(7)); !ok || o.Kind != state.KindCorpse || o.Position.X != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("object %+v %v", o, ok)
	}
}
```

`protocol/updateobject/apply/real70755_test.go`:

```go
package apply

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"testing"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/state"
)

// TestReal70755Session replays every SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT of the 70755
// Goldshire capture (private local server; ../testdata/real70755/README.md)
// into a fresh state, in capture order, and checks the world it ends with.
func TestReal70755Session(t *testing.T) {
	files, err := filepath.Glob("../testdata/real70755/*_SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT.bin")
	if err != nil || len(files) != 88 {
		t.Fatalf("%d packets (%v)", len(files), err)
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	s := state.New()
	var skipped []Skip
	for _, f := range files {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(f)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		skipped = append(skipped, mustApply(t, s, b).Skipped...)
	}
	// Every block applies, the quest log and equipment deltas included.
	if len(skipped) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("skipped %+v", skipped)
	}

	snap := s.Snapshot()
	kinds := map[state.Kind]int{}
	for _, o := range snap.Objects {
		kinds[o.Kind]++
	}
	want := map[state.Kind]int{state.KindGameObject: 70, state.KindItem: 19, state.KindPlayer: 1, state.KindUnit: 51}
	if len(snap.Objects) != 141 || len(kinds) != len(want) {
		t.Errorf("%d objects %v, want 141 %v", len(snap.Objects), kinds, want)
	}
	for k, n := range want {
		if kinds[k] != n {
			t.Errorf("%d %s, want %d", kinds[k], k, n)
		}
	}

	// Self: the level-61 dwarf shaman, at full health after the fight; the
	// maximum went 2260 -> 2430 when an item was equipped (packet 1403).
	selfGUID := state.GUID{Hi: 0x0801180000000000, Lo: 3}
	if snap.Self != selfGUID {
		t.Fatalf("self %v", snap.Self)
	}
	me, _ := s.Object(selfGUID)
	if me.Kind != state.KindPlayer || me.Name != "Qweqwee" || me.Level != 61 || me.Race != 3 || me.Class != 7 ||
		me.Health != 2430 || me.MaxHealth != 2430 {
		t.Errorf("self %+v", me)
	}
	// The item equipped in packet 1403 (VisibleItems[14], a nested delta).
	if me.Equipment[14] != 21710 || me.Equipment[15] != 36 {
		t.Errorf("equipment %v", me.Equipment)
	}

	byEntry := map[uint32][]state.Object{}
	for _, o := range snap.Objects {
		byEntry[o.Entry] = append(byEntry[o.Entry], o)
	}
	near := func(a, b float32) bool { return a-b < 0.01 && b-a < 0.01 }
	for _, w := range []struct {
		entry   uint32
		level   uint8
		health  int64
		max     int64
		x, y, z float32
	}{
		{240, 25, 713, 713, -9465.52, 74.01, 56.78},    // Marshal Dughan
		{295, 30, 1003, 1003, -9462.66, 16.19, 57.05},  // Innkeeper Farley
		{54, 10, 198, 198, -9464.87, 93.99, 58.53},     // Corina Steele (a vendor: FVendor_C)
		{113, 5, 0, 102, -9574.88, 121.39, 59.56},      // a Stonetusk Boar, killed
		{6749, 30, 1003, 1003, -9465.95, 48.14, 56.97}, // Erma
	} {
		cands := byEntry[w.entry]
		found := false
		for _, o := range cands {
			if o.Kind == state.KindUnit && o.Level == w.level && o.Health == w.health && o.MaxHealth == w.max &&
				near(o.Position.X, w.x) && near(o.Position.Y, w.y) && near(o.Position.Z, w.z) {
				found = true
			}
		}
		if !found {
			t.Errorf("no unit %d level %d %d/%d at (%.2f, %.2f, %.2f); have %+v", w.entry, w.level, w.health, w.max, w.x, w.y, w.z, cands)
		}
	}

	mailbox := byEntry[142075]
	if len(mailbox) != 1 || mailbox[0].GameObject == nil || mailbox[0].GameObject.Type != 19 || mailbox[0].GameObject.Display != 1907 ||
		!near(mailbox[0].Position.X, -9456.0) {
		t.Errorf("mailbox %+v", mailbox)
	}
	worn := byEntry[36] // Worn Mace
	if len(worn) != 1 || worn[0].Item == nil || worn[0].Item.Owner != selfGUID || worn[0].Item.Durability != 32 || worn[0].Item.MaxDurability != 35 {
		t.Errorf("item 36 %+v", worn)
	}
}
```

`protocol/updateobject/build.go`:

```go
package updateobject

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/codec"
)

// Builders for fixtures: the inverse of DecodeFields and DecodeValues. Field
// values are given by name (as decoded: "Health", "Power[0]", ...); missing
// fields are zero, and counts and presence bits are fields too.

// Fields gives create field values per struct.
type Fields struct {
	Object, Unit, Player map[string]any
	// ActivePlayerRaw is appended verbatim for TypeActivePlayer.
	ActivePlayerRaw []byte
}

// BuildFragmentData encodes CGObject create data (with its active byte) for
// a create block of type t with visibility flags.
func BuildFragmentData(t ObjectType, flags uint8, f Fields) ([]byte, error) {
	w := codec.NewWriter()
	w.Uint8(1) // IndirectFragmentActive
	parts := []struct {
		prog []op
		vals map[string]any
	}{{objectDataCreate, f.Object}, {unitDataCreate, f.Unit}}
	switch t {
	case TypeActivePlayer, TypePlayer:
		parts = append(parts, struct {
			prog []op
			vals map[string]any
		}{playerDataCreate, f.Player})
	case TypeUnit:
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: update fields of object type %d", ErrUnsupported, t)
	}
	for _, p := range parts {
		if err := writeLayout(w, p.prog, flags, mapValues(p.vals)); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		w.FlushBits()
	}
	if t == TypeActivePlayer {
		w.RawBytes(f.ActivePlayerRaw)
	}
	return w.Bytes(), nil
}

// BuildValues encodes a CGObject values block that changes the given fields.
func BuildValues(object, unit, player map[string]any) ([]byte, error) {
	w := codec.NewWriter()
	w.Uint8(0) // owner
	w.Uint8(0) // fragment ids unchanged
	w.Uint8(3) // CGObject active, contents changed
	var typeMask uint32
	if len(object) > 0 {
		typeMask |= 1 << 0
	}
	if len(unit) > 0 {
		typeMask |= 1 << 5
	}
	if len(player) > 0 {
		typeMask |= 1 << 6
	}
	w.Uint32(typeMask)
	for _, p := range []struct {
		l    *deltaLayout
		vals map[string]any
	}{{&objectDataDelta, object}, {&unitDataDelta, unit}, {&playerDataDelta, player}} {
		if len(p.vals) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if err := writeDelta(w, p.l, deltaValues(p.vals)); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		w.FlushBits()
	}
	return w.Bytes(), nil
}
```
