`protocol/updateobject/real70755_test.go`:

```go
package updateobject

import (
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// Real bytes: every SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT of the 70755 Goldshire capture (88
// packets), recorded on a private local TrinityCore server
// (testdata/real70755/README.md). File names keep the capture's packet
// sequence numbers.

type realPacket struct {
	name string
	b    []byte
}

func realPackets(t *testing.T) []realPacket {
	t.Helper()
	files, err := filepath.Glob("testdata/real70755/*_SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	if len(files) != 88 {
		t.Fatalf("%d packets in testdata/real70755, want 88", len(files))
	}
	out := make([]realPacket, len(files))
	for i, f := range files {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(f)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		out[i] = realPacket{strings.SplitN(filepath.Base(f), "_", 2)[0], b}
	}
	return out
}

func fieldMap(fs []Field) map[string]any {
	m := map[string]any{}
	for _, f := range fs {
		m[f.Name] = f.Value
	}
	return m
}

// TestReal70755Decode decodes every packet, every create's fields and every
// values block, and checks the totals and the known gaps.
func TestReal70755Decode(t *testing.T) {
	types := map[GUID]ObjectType{}
	var blocks, creates, values int
	createsByType := map[ObjectType]int{}
	vendors := 0
	type gap struct{ pkt, why string }
	var gaps []gap
	for _, p := range realPackets(t) {
		u, err := Decode(p.b)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("packet %s: %v", p.name, err)
		}
		if u.MapID != 0 {
			t.Errorf("packet %s: map %d, want 0 (Eastern Kingdoms)", p.name, u.MapID)
		}
		// The framing and movement encoders reproduce the server's bytes.
		if string(Encode(u)) != string(p.b) {
			t.Errorf("packet %s: re-encoded bytes differ", p.name)
		}
		for _, bl := range u.Blocks {
			blocks++
			switch {
			case bl.Create != nil:
				creates++
				c := bl.Create
				types[bl.GUID] = c.ObjectType
				createsByType[c.ObjectType]++
				of, err := c.DecodeFields()
				if err != nil {
					t.Errorf("packet %s: create %v (type %d): %v", p.name, bl.GUID, c.ObjectType, err)
					continue
				}
				if of.Vendor != nil {
					vendors++
				}
			case bl.Values != nil:
				values++
				_, err := DecodeValues(types[bl.GUID], bl.Values)
				if err != nil {
					gaps = append(gaps, gap{p.name, err.Error()})
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if blocks != 333 || creates != 251 || values != 82 {
		t.Errorf("%d blocks (%d creates, %d values), want 333 (251, 82)", blocks, creates, values)
	}
	want := map[ObjectType]int{TypeGameObject: 132, TypeUnit: 97, TypeItem: 21, TypeActivePlayer: 1}
	for k, n := range want {
		if createsByType[k] != n {
			t.Errorf("%d creates of type %d, want %d", createsByType[k], k, n)
		}
	}
	if vendors != 18 {
		t.Errorf("%d creates with FVendor_C, want 18", vendors)
	}
	// Every values block decodes, the quest log (packet 1350) and the item
	// equipped (1403) included.
	if len(gaps) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("values gaps %+v", gaps)
	}
}

func realBlock(t *testing.T, pkt string, i int) Block {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/real70755/" + pkt + "_SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	u, err := Decode(b)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return u.Blocks[i]
}

func TestReal70755ActivePlayerCreate(t *testing.T) {
	bl := realBlock(t, "0275", 19)
	c := bl.Create
	if c == nil || c.ObjectType != TypeActivePlayer || !c.Movement.ThisIsYou || c.FieldFlags != FlagOwner|FlagPartyMember {
		t.Fatalf("block: %+v", bl)
	}
	if bl.GUID != (GUID{Hi: 0x0801180000000000, Lo: 3}) {
		t.Errorf("guid %v", bl.GUID)
	}
	of, err := c.DecodeFields()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	u := of.Unit
	if u.Level != 61 || u.Health != 2260 || u.MaxHealth != 2260 || u.Race != 3 || u.ClassID != 7 {
		t.Errorf("unit: level %d health %d/%d race %d class %d", u.Level, u.Health, u.MaxHealth, u.Race, u.ClassID)
	}
	if of.Player.Name != "Qweqwee" || of.ActivePlayer == nil || len(of.ActivePlayer.Raw) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("player %q, active player %d raw bytes", of.Player.Name, len(of.ActivePlayer.Raw))
	}
	p := c.Movement.Movement.Info.Position
	if p.X < -9488.3 || p.X > -9488.2 || p.Y < 63.8 || p.Y > 63.9 {
		t.Errorf("position %+v", p)
	}
}

// TestReal70755NestedValues: packet 1403 equips an item (VisibleItems[14],
// a nested VisibleItem delta) and raises the maximum health 2260 -> 2430;
// packet 1350 accepts quest 47 into quest log slot 0 (a
// QuestLogQuestIdToIndex change and a QuestLog nested delta).
func TestReal70755NestedValues(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := DecodeValues(TypeActivePlayer, realBlock(t, "1403", 1).Values)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if v := fieldMap(d.Unit)["MaxHealth"]; v != int64(2430) {
		t.Errorf("MaxHealth = %v, want 2430", v)
	}
	of, err := realBlock(t, "0275", 19).Create.DecodeFields()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	p := of.Player
	if p.VisibleItems[15].ItemID != 36 || p.VisibleItems[14].ItemID != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("create: visible items %+v", p.VisibleItems)
	}
	p.ApplyTo(d.Player)
	if v := p.VisibleItems[14]; v.ItemID != 21710 || v.ItemModifiedAppearanceID != 164745 {
		t.Errorf("VisibleItems[14] = %+v", v)
	}
	if p.VisibleItems[15].ItemID != 36 {
		t.Errorf("VisibleItems[15] = %+v", p.VisibleItems[15])
	}

	d, err = DecodeValues(TypeActivePlayer, realBlock(t, "1350", 0).Values)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	p.ApplyTo(d.Player)
	if p.QuestLogQuestIDToIndex[47] != 0 || len(p.QuestLogQuestIDToIndex) != 1 || p.QuestLog[0].QuestID != 47 {
		t.Errorf("quest log: map %v, slot 0 %+v", p.QuestLogQuestIDToIndex, p.QuestLog[0])
	}

	// A plain health tick of the active player, with the ActivePlayerData
	// delta kept raw after it.
	d, err = DecodeValues(TypeActivePlayer, realBlock(t, "1049", 0).Values)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if v := fieldMap(d.Unit)["Health"]; v != int64(2244) || len(d.ActivePlayerRaw) != 23 {
		t.Errorf("Health = %v, %d raw bytes", v, len(d.ActivePlayerRaw))
	}
}

func TestReal70755GameObjectAndItem(t *testing.T) {
	gos := map[int32]*GameObjectData{}
	var item *ItemData
	for _, p := range realPackets(t) {
		u, _ := Decode(p.b)
		for _, bl := range u.Blocks {
			if bl.Create == nil {
				continue
			}
			of, err := bl.Create.DecodeFields()
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if of.GameObject != nil {
				gos[of.Object.EntryID] = of.GameObject
			}
			if of.Item != nil && of.Object.EntryID == 36 {
				item = of.Item
			}
		}
	}
	for _, w := range []struct {
		entry   int32
		display int32
		typ     int8
		faction int32
	}{
		{176495, 3031, 15, 0},  // a transport (MO_TRANSPORT)
		{142075, 1907, 19, 12}, // the Goldshire mailbox
		{22772, 199, 8, 0},     // a spell focus (brazier) at the inn
		{177494, 39, 7, 0},     // a chair (GAMEOBJECT_TYPE_CHAIR)
	} {
		g := gos[w.entry]
		if g == nil || g.DisplayID != w.display || g.TypeID != w.typ || g.FactionTemplate != w.faction || g.State != 1 {
			t.Errorf("game object %d: %+v", w.entry, g)
		}
	}
	// A worn item of the player's (owner flags: stack count and durability).
	self := GUID{Hi: 0x0801180000000000, Lo: 3}
	if item == nil || item.Owner != self || item.ContainedIn != self || item.StackCount != 1 || item.Durability != 32 || item.MaxDurability != 35 {
		t.Errorf("item 36: %+v", item)
	}
}

// TestReal70755Rotation checks UnpackRotation against the stationary facing
// the same create carries: every object here turns about the vertical, so
// the quaternion is (0, 0, sin(o/2), cos(o/2)) up to sign.
func TestReal70755Rotation(t *testing.T) {
	n := 0
	for _, p := range realPackets(t) {
		u, _ := Decode(p.b)
		for _, bl := range u.Blocks {
			c := bl.Create
			if c == nil || c.Movement.Rotation == nil || c.Movement.Stationary == nil {
				continue
			}
			q := UnpackRotation(*c.Movement.Rotation)
			o := float64(c.Movement.Stationary.O)
			// q and -q are the same rotation: compare |<q, (0,0,z,w)>| with 1.
			dot := float64(q.Z)*math.Sin(o/2) + float64(q.W)*math.Cos(o/2)
			if q.X != 0 || q.Y != 0 || math.Abs(math.Abs(dot)-1) > 1e-5 {
				t.Errorf("packet %s %v: rotation %+v, facing %.3f", p.name, bl.GUID, q, o)
			}
			n++
		}
	}
	if n != 132 {
		t.Errorf("%d rotations checked, want 132", n)
	}
}

# Two SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT bodies from the live 70755 session

Cut from `~/wow/server/wow-forever-tc/captures/2026-11-05-live-goldshire-70755.pkt`
(29 minutes of the stock 70755 client in Goldshire on the private local
TrinityCore fork; the log itself is not committed). File names are the
log's packet indices; each file is the message body, without the opcode:

    go run ./tools/worldreplay -dump-op 0x5c0000 -dump-to /tmp/dump <log>
    tail -c +5 /tmp/dump/9968-conn1-*.bin > 09968_SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT.bin

- `09968` (268.5 s): quest 179 accepted into quest log slot 1 — PlayerData
  bit 26 (`QuestLogQuestIdToIndex` change) and bit 59 (QuestLog[1]).
- `18314` (455.9 s): QuestLog[1] objective 4 progress → 2 (bit 59).

These were the session's last two kinds of skipped block.

`protocol/updateobject/testdata/real70755/README.md`:

```md
# Real 70755 update-object bytes

Every `SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT` payload (88 packets) of one session of the stock
WoW Forever 1.60.1.**70755** client, recorded on **a private local
TrinityCore server** (the `forever` fork, run on the owner's machine), not
on Blizzard's servers. Nothing here came from Blizzard's infrastructure.

- Source: `~/wow/server/wow-forever-tc/captures/2026-11-04-goldshire-70755.pkt`
  (TrinityCore PKT 3.1, 1,614 packets, 135 s, sha256
  `814696211609d3047e783e6e4729a67697d5d18b7551584727c544bd8af0a057`).
- Session: login, character list, world entry in Goldshire (Elwynn Forest,
  map 0), walking, a quest giver, combat with a few mobs, chat, logout. The
  character is Qweqwee, a level-61 dwarf shaman, GUID
  `0801180000000000:0000000000000003`; the account's characters are made-up
  test names.
- Exported with `~/wow/server/wow-forever-tc/tools/pktread.py <pkt> --export DIR`:
  one file per packet, payload only (no opcode, no frame header), named by
  the capture's packet sequence number. The server logs a packet before it
  compresses or encrypts it, so these are the plain bodies the client's
  readers see after `SMSG_COMPRESSED_PACKET` is inflated.

Tests: `../../real70755_test.go` (decode, re-encode, fields, values,
rotation) and `../../apply/real70755_test.go` (the whole session applied
into `state`). Findings: `docs/EVIDENCE.md` E31.

`protocol/updateobject/ufemu_test.go`:

```go
package updateobject

import (
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/codec"
)

// The client's update-field readers, run in an emulator by tools/ufemu.py
// over bytes this package encodes. The recorded runs live in
// testdata/ufemu/results.json. Regenerate with:
//
//	UFEMU_CASES=/tmp/cases.json go test ./protocol/updateobject -run TestWriteUfemuCases
//	python3 tools/ufemu.py artifacts/WoWForever-arm64.decrypted \
//	    --cases /tmp/cases.json --out protocol/updateobject/testdata/ufemu/results.json

type ufemuCase struct {
	Name   string            `json:"name"`
	Reader string            `json:"reader"`
	Flags  string            `json:"flags"`
	Hex    string            `json:"hex"`
	Delta  bool              `json:"delta,omitempty"`
	Init   map[string]uint64 `json:"init,omitempty"`
}

type ufemuRead struct {
	Pos int  `json:"pos"`
	W   any  `json:"w"`
	N   *int `json:"n,omitempty"`
}

type ufemuResult struct {
	ufemuCase
	Consumed int         `json:"consumed"`
	Total    int         `json:"total"`
	Error    *string     `json:"error"`
	Reads    []ufemuRead `json:"reads"`
}

// layoutCase is one create layout under one flag set and one value filler.
type layoutCase struct {
	name   string
	reader string
	prog   []op
	flags  uint8
	vals   valueSource
}

// filler gives every field a distinct non-zero value, and counts and
// presence bits from over.
func filler(over map[string]any) valueSource {
	n := 0
	return func(name string, w Width) any {
		if v, ok := over[name]; ok {
			return v
		}
		base := name
		if i := strings.IndexByte(base, '['); i >= 0 {
			base = base[:i]
		}
		if v, ok := over[base]; ok {
			return v
		}
		if strings.HasSuffix(base, ".size") || strings.HasSuffix(base, ".len") || strings.HasPrefix(base, "Has") ||
			strings.Contains(base, ".Has") {
			return nil
		}
		n++
		switch w {
		case WGUID:
			return GUID{Lo: uint64(n)<<8 | 0x11, Hi: uint64(n) << 48}
		case WF32:
			return float32(n) + 0.5
		case WBit:
			return n%2 == 0
		}
		return uint64(n)
	}
}

// readerInit sets members of the (zeroed) destination struct that a reader
// dereferences: optional sub-structs are tagged pointers, 1 = absent.
var readerInit = map[string]map[string]uint64{
	"0x1008e3fa0": {"0x3c0": 1, "0x380": 0x3f800000},             // AssistActionData; the +0x368 map's max load factor (1.0f)
	"0x1008d2130": {"0x108": 0x3f800000, "0x400": 1, "0x408": 1}, // the +0xF0 map's max load factor; the two name sets
}

var visFlagSets = []uint8{0, FlagOwner, FlagPartyMember, FlagUnitAll, FlagEmpath, FlagOwner | FlagPartyMember | FlagUnitAll | FlagEmpath}

// deltaCase is one delta layout with a set of changed fields.
type deltaCase struct {
	name   string
	reader string
	layout *deltaLayout
	vals   deltaValues
}

func deltaPrelude(l *deltaLayout) func(*rd, mask, *fieldSet) {
	if l == &unitDataDelta {
		return unitDataPrelude
	}
	return nil
}

// allDeltaValues sets every supported field of l to a distinct value.
func allDeltaValues(l *deltaLayout) deltaValues {
	v := deltaValues{}
	n := 0
	for _, f := range l.fields {
		if f.trailer || f.read != nil {
			continue
		}
		n++
		switch f.width {
		case WGUID:
			v[f.name] = GUID{Lo: uint64(n)<<8 | 0x22, Hi: uint64(n) << 40}
		case WF32:
			v[f.name] = float32(n) + 0.25
		default:
			v[f.name] = uint64(n)
		}
	}
	return v
}

func deltaCases() []deltaCase {
	return []deltaCase{
		{"ObjectData/delta/all", "0x1008ce4bc", &objectDataDelta, allDeltaValues(&objectDataDelta)},
		{"UnitData/delta/all", "0x1008e93e0", &unitDataDelta, func() deltaValues {
			v := allDeltaValues(&unitDataDelta)
			v["Field_314"] = true
			return v
		}()},
		{"UnitData/delta/health", "0x1008e93e0", &unitDataDelta, deltaValues{
			"Health": uint64(77), "Power[0]": uint64(5), "MaxPower[0]": uint64(100), "Target": GUID{Lo: 0x99},
		}},
		{"PlayerData/delta/all", "0x1008d4e40", &playerDataDelta, allDeltaValues(&playerDataDelta)},
		{"GameObjectData/delta/all", "0x1008b6b60", &gameObjectDataDelta, allDeltaValues(&gameObjectDataDelta)},
		{"GameObjectData/delta/state", "0x1008b6b60", &gameObjectDataDelta, deltaValues{"State": uint64(0), "Flags": uint64(32)}},
		{"ItemData/delta/all", "0x1008c9ec0", &itemDataDelta, allDeltaValues(&itemDataDelta)},
		{"ItemData/delta/stack", "0x1008c9ec0", &itemDataDelta, deltaValues{"StackCount": uint64(5), "Durability": uint64(30)}},
	}
}

func (c deltaCase) bytes(t *testing.T) []byte {
	w := codec.NewWriter()
	if err := writeDelta(w, c.layout, c.vals); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", c.name, err)
	}
	return w.Bytes()
}

func (c layoutCase) bytes(t *testing.T) []byte {
	w := codec.NewWriter()
	if err := writeLayout(w, c.prog, c.flags, c.vals); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", c.name, err)
	}
	return w.Bytes()
}

func TestWriteUfemuCases(t *testing.T) {
	path := os.Getenv("UFEMU_CASES")
	if path == "" {
		t.Skip("set UFEMU_CASES to write the emulator cases")
	}
	var out []ufemuCase
	for _, c := range layoutCases() {
		out = append(out, ufemuCase{Name: c.name, Reader: c.reader, Flags: fmt.Sprintf("%#x", c.flags|flagCreate), Hex: hex.EncodeToString(c.bytes(t)), Init: readerInit[c.reader]})
	}
	for _, c := range deltaCases() {
		out = append(out, ufemuCase{Name: c.name, Reader: c.reader, Flags: "0", Hex: hex.EncodeToString(c.bytes(t)), Delta: true, Init: readerInit[createReaderOf[c.reader]]})
	}
	b, _ := json.MarshalIndent(out, "", " ")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, b, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// createReaderOf maps a delta reader to its struct's create reader (whose
// destination init it shares).
var createReaderOf = map[string]string{"0x1008ce4bc": "0x1008ce2b8", "0x1008e93e0": "0x1008e3fa0", "0x1008d4e40": "0x1008d2130",
	"0x1008b6b60": "0x1008b5fe8", "0x1008c9ec0": "0x1008c8c98"}

// TestDeltasAgainstClient is TestLayoutsAgainstClient for the delta readers.
func TestDeltasAgainstClient(t *testing.T) {
	res := loadUfemu(t)
	for _, c := range deltaCases() {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			r, ok := res[c.name]
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("no recorded client run; regenerate testdata/ufemu")
			}
			b := c.bytes(t)
			if hex.EncodeToString(b) != r.Hex {
				t.Fatalf("encoded bytes differ from the recorded run; regenerate testdata/ufemu")
			}
			if r.Error != nil {
				t.Fatalf("client run failed: %s", *r.Error)
			}
			var tr []traceEnt
			d := &rd{r: codec.NewReader(b), trace: &tr}
			fs := d.readDelta(c.layout, deltaPrelude(c.layout))
			if d.err != nil {
				t.Fatal(d.err)
			}
			if len(fs) == 0 {
				t.Fatal("no fields decoded")
			}
			got := map[string]any{}
			for _, f := range fs {
				got[f.Name] = f.Value
			}
			for name, v := range c.vals {
				if fmt.Sprint(got[name]) != fmt.Sprint(v) {
					t.Errorf("%s = %v, want %v", name, got[name], v)
				}
			}
			want := normClient(r.Reads)
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(tr, want) {
				for i := range want {
					if i >= len(tr) || tr[i] != want[i] {
						lo := max(0, i-3)
						t.Fatalf("read %d differs: client %v, ours %v (from %d: client %v ours %v)", i, want[i], at(tr, i), lo, want[lo:min(len(want), i+3)], tr[lo:min(len(tr), i+3)])
					}
				}
				t.Fatalf("we made %d reads, client %d", len(tr), len(want))
			}
			if r.Consumed != len(b) || d.r.Remaining() != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("client consumed %d, we left %d, of %d bytes", r.Consumed, d.r.Remaining(), len(b))
			}
		})
	}
}

func loadUfemu(t *testing.T) map[string]ufemuResult {
	b, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/ufemu/results.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var rs []ufemuResult
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &rs); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := map[string]ufemuResult{}
	for _, r := range rs {
		m[r.Name] = r
	}
	return m
}

func normClient(rs []ufemuRead) []traceEnt {
	out := make([]traceEnt, 0, len(rs))
	for _, r := range rs {
		e := traceEnt{Pos: r.Pos, W: fmt.Sprint(r.W)}
		if e.W == "D" && r.N != nil {
			e.N = *r.N
		}
		out = append(out, e)
	}
	return out
}

// TestLayoutsAgainstClient checks that, for every case, the client's reader
// consumed exactly the bytes we encoded and made the same reads, in the same
// order and at the same offsets, as our decoder.
func TestLayoutsAgainstClient(t *testing.T) {
	res := loadUfemu(t)
	for _, c := range layoutCases() {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			r, ok := res[c.name]
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("no recorded client run; regenerate testdata/ufemu (see ufemu_test.go)")
			}
			b := c.bytes(t)
			if hex.EncodeToString(b) != r.Hex {
				t.Fatalf("encoded bytes differ from the recorded run; regenerate testdata/ufemu")
			}
			if r.Error != nil {
				t.Fatalf("client run failed: %s", *r.Error)
			}
			var tr []traceEnt
			d := &rd{r: codec.NewReader(b), trace: &tr}
			var fs fieldSet
			d.readLayout(c.prog, c.flags, &fs)
			if d.err != nil {
				t.Fatal(d.err)
			}
			left := d.r.Remaining()
			defer func() {
				if left != 0 && !t.Failed() {
					t.Fatalf("decoder left %d bytes", left)
				}
			}()
			want := normClient(r.Reads)
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(tr, want) {
				for i := range want {
					if i >= len(tr) || tr[i] != want[i] {
						lo := max(0, i-3)
						t.Fatalf("read %d differs: client %v, ours %v (from %d: client %v ours %v)", i, want[i], at(tr, i), lo, want[lo:min(len(want), i+3)], tr[lo:min(len(tr), i+3)])
					}
				}
				t.Fatalf("we made %d reads, client %d", len(tr), len(want))
			}
			if r.Consumed != len(b) {
				t.Fatalf("client consumed %d of %d bytes", r.Consumed, len(b))
			}
		})
	}
}

func at(tr []traceEnt, i int) any {
	if i < len(tr) {
		return tr[i]
	}
	return "nothing"
}

// TestDumpCreateNames writes each create layout's field names in read order
// (owner and party-member visibility, no counts), for tools/ufdelta.py.
func TestDumpCreateNames(t *testing.T) {
	path := os.Getenv("UFNAMES")
	if path == "" {
		t.Skip("set UFNAMES to write the create field names")
	}
	out := map[string][][2]string{}
	for name, prog := range map[string][]op{"ObjectData": objectDataCreate, "UnitData": unitDataCreate, "PlayerData": playerDataCreate,
		"GameObjectData": gameObjectDataCreate, "ItemData": itemDataCreate} {
		flags := FlagOwner | FlagPartyMember
		w := codec.NewWriter()
		if err := writeLayout(w, prog, flags, mapValues(nil)); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var fs fieldSet
		d := &rd{r: codec.NewReader(w.Bytes())}
		d.readLayout(prog, flags, &fs)
		for _, f := range fs.list {
			out[name] = append(out[name], [2]string{f.Name, f.Width.String()})
		}
	}
	b, _ := json.Marshal(out)
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, b, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

`protocol/version/version.go`:

```go
// Package version carries the protocol identity of the shipped game client and
// the rules that decide when recorded traffic, an opcode table, or a struct
// layout may be reused.
//
// Everything in this package is a *declared* fact taken from the shipped
// artifact. See docs/EVIDENCE.md for the source of each value.
package version

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// ID identifies one shipped build. Two builds that differ in Build may share a
// version string but never share an opcode numbering.
type ID struct {
	Product  string // product flavor, e.g. "wowf" (World of Warcraft: Forever)
	Branch   string // .build.info Branch column
	Major    int
	Minor    int
	Patch    int
	Build    int
	BuildKey string // .build.info "Build Key" (CASC build config key)
	CDNKey   string // .build.info "CDN Key"
}

// Known builds. Each has its own opcode numbering (protocol/opcodes) and its
// own per-build auth key (world.BuildAuthKey); nothing recorded against one
// is valid for the other without a check.
var (
	// Build70707 is CFBundleVersion 1.60.1.70707, the build everything was
	// first decoded against (artifacts/WoWForever-arm64.decrypted).
	Build70707 = ID{
		Product: "wowf", Branch: "us", Major: 1, Minor: 60, Patch: 1, Build: 70707,
		BuildKey: "7feb61f3c994bcb168526b8db521514a",
		CDNKey:   "aced69cc895b8fbb802f35e442ebe6fc",
	}
	// Build70755 is CFBundleVersion 1.60.1.70755, shipped by Battle.net on
	// 2026-11-03/04 and installed since. It renumbers two opcode groups
	// against 70707 (docs/EVIDENCE.md E31).
	Build70755 = ID{
		Product: "wowf", Branch: "us", Major: 1, Minor: 60, Patch: 1, Build: 70755,
		BuildKey: "9d9888f2d89a2dcc9eacc68a2d7cb3dc",
		CDNKey:   "483baa37d48c06ae7d14c83a591c469e",
	}
)

// Forever returns the identity of the reference target, the installed client:
// /Applications/World of Warcraft/_forever_/World of Warcraft.app,
// CFBundleVersion 1.60.1.70755, product flavor "wowf". Build70707 stays known
// and selectable through ByBuild.
func Forever() ID { return Build70755 }

// Known lists every build this client has tables for, oldest first.
func Known() []ID { return []ID{Build70707, Build70755} }

// ByBuild returns the known identity with that build number.
func ByBuild(build int) (ID, bool) {
	for _, v := range Known() {
		if v.Build == build {
			return v, true
		}
	}
	return ID{}, false
}

// Parse resolves a protocol string ("wowf 1.60.1.70707", as v.String()
// renders it) to a known identity.
func Parse(protocol string) (ID, bool) {
	for _, v := range Known() {
		if v.String() == protocol {
			return v, true
		}
	}
	return ID{}, false
}

// ErrUnknownBuild is returned for a build this client has no tables for.
var ErrUnknownBuild = errors.New("unknown protocol build")

// VersionString renders the marketing version ("1.60.1").
func (v ID) VersionString() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d.%d.%d", v.Major, v.Minor, v.Patch) }

// String renders the full identity ("wowf 1.60.1.70707").
func (v ID) String() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s.%d", v.Product, v.VersionString(), v.Build) }

// ErrBuildMismatch is returned when two identities disagree on the exact build.
var ErrBuildMismatch = errors.New("protocol build mismatch")

// Check reports whether a recorded artifact (opcode table, fixture, capture) is
// usable against v. Only an exact build match is accepted: opcode numbering is
// rebuilt every patch and there is no public stability guarantee (70755 moved
// two groups against 70707 without changing the version string), and v itself
// must be a known build.
func (v ID) Check(want ID) error {
	if v.Product != want.Product || v.Major != want.Major || v.Minor != want.Minor ||
		v.Patch != want.Patch || v.Build != want.Build {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: have %s, want %s", ErrBuildMismatch, v, want)
	}
	if _, ok := ByBuild(v.Build); !ok || v.Product != Forever().Product {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrUnknownBuild, v)
	}
	return nil
}

// Compatible reports whether both identities can share a protocol table.
func (v ID) Compatible(other ID) bool { return v.Check(other) == nil }

// All returns every known build, oldest build number first.
func All() []ID { return Known() }

// Lookup returns the identity of a known build.
func Lookup(build int) (ID, bool) { return ByBuild(build) }

// Latest returns the newest known build by build number.
func Latest() ID {
	all := All()
	if len(all) == 0 {
		panic("version: no known builds")
	}
	return all[len(all)-1]
}

`protocol/version/version_test.go`:

```go
package version

import (
	"errors"
	"testing"
)

func TestForeverIdentity(t *testing.T) {
	v := Forever()
	if got, want := v.VersionString(), "1.60.1"; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("VersionString() = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := v.String(), "wowf 1.60.1.70755"; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("String() = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestKnownBuilds(t *testing.T) {
	for _, b := range []int{70707, 70755} {
		v, ok := ByBuild(b)
		if !ok || v.Build != b || v.Product != "wowf" {
			t.Fatalf("ByBuild(%d) = %+v, %v", b, v, ok)
		}
		if p, ok := Parse(v.String()); !ok || p != v {
			t.Fatalf("Parse(%q) = %+v, %v", v.String(), p, ok)
		}
		if err := v.Check(v); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s self check: %v", v, err)
		}
	}
	if Build70707.String() != "wowf 1.60.1.70707" || Build70707.BuildKey != "7feb61f3c994bcb168526b8db521514a" {
		t.Fatalf("70707 identity changed: %+v", Build70707)
	}
	if _, ok := ByBuild(70658); ok {
		t.Fatal("70658 is not a known build")
	}
}

func TestCheckRequiresExactBuild(t *testing.T) {
	v := Forever()
	if err := v.Check(Forever()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("self check failed: %v", err)
	}
	if err := v.Check(Build70707); !errors.Is(err, ErrBuildMismatch) {
		t.Fatalf("70755 vs 70707: expected ErrBuildMismatch, got %v", err)
	}
	other := Forever()
	other.Build++
	if err := v.Check(other); !errors.Is(err, ErrBuildMismatch) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrBuildMismatch, got %v", err)
	}
	if err := other.Check(other); !errors.Is(err, ErrUnknownBuild) {
		t.Fatalf("unknown build self check: expected ErrUnknownBuild, got %v", err)
	}
	if v.Compatible(other) {
		t.Fatal("different builds must not be compatible")
	}
}

func TestRegistryLookup(t *testing.T) {
	all := All()
	if len(all) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("All() is empty")
	}
	if got := Latest(); got.Build != all[len(all)-1].Build {
		t.Fatalf("Latest() = %s, want newest of %v", got, all)
	}
	ref := Forever()
	got, ok := Lookup(ref.Build)
	if !ok || got != ref {
		t.Fatalf("Lookup(%d) = %v, %v; want %v", ref.Build, got, ok, ref)
	}
	if _, ok := Lookup(-1); ok {
		t.Fatal("Lookup(-1) should fail")
	}
}

`protocol/worldstream/pcap.go`:

```go
package worldstream

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"time"
)

// Tail reads TCP segments from a pcapng file, including one tcpdump is still
// writing (`tcpdump -U -w`): each Next returns the segments in the blocks
// completed since the last call and keeps a partial block for later.
type Tail struct {
	f     *os.File
	buf   []byte
	links []uint16
}

// OpenTail opens a pcapng capture for tailing.
func OpenTail(path string) (*Tail, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &Tail{f: f}, nil
}

// Close closes the file.
func (t *Tail) Close() error { return t.f.Close() }

// Next returns the segments that became complete.
func (t *Tail) Next() ([]Segment, error) {
	chunk := make([]byte, 1<<20)
	for {
		n, err := t.f.Read(chunk)
		t.buf = append(t.buf, chunk[:n]...)
		if err == io.EOF || n == 0 {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	var segs []Segment
	le := binary.LittleEndian
	p := 0
	for p+12 <= len(t.buf) {
		typ, blen := le.Uint32(t.buf[p:]), int(le.Uint32(t.buf[p+4:]))
		if blen < 12 {
			return segs, fmt.Errorf("pcapng: block of %d bytes at %d (not pcapng?)", blen, p)
		}
		if p+blen > len(t.buf) {
			break
		}
		b := t.buf[p+8 : p+blen-4]
		switch typ {
		case 1: // interface description
			t.links = append(t.links, le.Uint16(b))
		case 6: // enhanced packet
			iface := le.Uint32(b)
			ts := uint64(le.Uint32(b[4:]))<<32 | uint64(le.Uint32(b[8:]))
			capLen := int(le.Uint32(b[12:]))
			if 20+capLen <= len(b) {
				link := uint16(1)
				if int(iface) < len(t.links) {
					link = t.links[iface]
				}
				if s, ok := parsePacket(link, b[20:20+capLen]); ok {
					s.T = time.UnixMicro(int64(ts))
					segs = append(segs, s)
				}
			}
		}
		p += blen
	}
	t.buf = append(t.buf[:0], t.buf[p:]...)
	return segs, nil
}

func parsePacket(link uint16, d []byte) (Segment, bool) {
	var s Segment
	switch link {
	case 258: // PKTAP: its own header, then the inner link
		if len(d) < 8 {
			return s, false
		}
		hl := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(d))
		inner := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(d[4:])
		if hl > len(d) {
			return s, false
		}
		return parsePacket(uint16(inner), d[hl:])
	case 1: // Ethernet
		if len(d) < 14 {
			return s, false
		}
		d = d[14:]
	case 0: // BSD loopback
		if len(d) < 4 {
			return s, false
		}
		d = d[4:]
	case 12, 101: // raw IP
	default:
		return s, false
	}
	if len(d) < 20 {
		return s, false
	}
	var tcp []byte
	switch d[0] >> 4 {
	case 4:
		ihl := int(d[0]&0xf) * 4
		total := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(d[2:]))
		if d[9] != 6 || total > len(d) || ihl > total {
			return s, false
		}
		s.Src = fmt.Sprintf("%d.%d.%d.%d", d[12], d[13], d[14], d[15])
		s.Dst = fmt.Sprintf("%d.%d.%d.%d", d[16], d[17], d[18], d[19])
		tcp = d[ihl:total]
	case 6:
		if len(d) < 40 || d[6] != 6 {
			return s, false
		}
		plen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(d[4:]))
		s.Src, s.Dst = hex.EncodeToString(d[8:24]), hex.EncodeToString(d[24:40])
		if 40+plen > len(d) {
			return s, false
		}
		tcp = d[40 : 40+plen]
	default:
		return s, false
	}
	if len(tcp) < 20 {
		return s, false
	}
	s.SPort, s.DPort = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(tcp), binary.BigEndian.Uint16(tcp[2:])
	s.Seq = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(tcp[4:])
	off := int(tcp[12]>>4) * 4
	flags := tcp[13]
	s.SYN, s.FIN = flags&0x02 != 0, flags&0x01 != 0
	if off > len(tcp) {
		return s, false
	}
	s.Payload = append([]byte(nil), tcp[off:]...)
	return s, true
}

```

`protocol/worldstream/worldstream.go`:

```go
// Package worldstream decrypts world connections as they are captured: the
// incremental form of tools/worlddecrypt (E45). Feed it TCP segments in
// capture order (Tail reads them from a pcapng file tcpdump is still
// writing) and it hands back each message the moment its frame is complete:
// TCP reassembly per direction, framing, the session's AES-GCM key (found
// from bnetrelay's secrets.jsonl, re-read until a key opens the connection),
// the persistent deflate stream, SMSG_COMPRESSED_PACKET and
// SMSG_MULTIPLE_PACKETS unpacked.
package worldstream

import (
	"bytes"
	"compress/flate"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/framing"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/opcodes"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/world"
)

// WorldPort is the world server's TCP port.
const WorldPort = 3724

// Segment is one TCP segment of a world connection.
type Segment struct {
	T            time.Time
	Src, Dst     string
	SPort, DPort uint16
	Seq          uint32
	SYN, FIN     bool
	Payload      []byte
}

// Msg is one decrypted world message.
type Msg struct {
	T      time.Time
	Port   uint16 // the client's port: one per connection
	Dir    opcodes.Direction
	Opcode uint32
	Name   string // opcodes.DescribeBuild's text, "Group/0xN ~SMSG_NAME (confidence)"
	Body   []byte
	Note   string // "decrypt failed", "inflate: ..." when something went wrong
}

var shortName = regexp.MustCompile(`~?([CS]MSG_\w+)`)

// Short is the message's bare name (SMSG_SPELL_GO), or "" when unnamed.
func (m Msg) Short() string {
	if s := shortName.FindStringSubmatch(m.Name); s != nil {
		return s[1]
	}
	return ""
}

// Builds the decoder names messages for. Retail 12.1.5.70783 has no table
// yet; its numbers are Forever 70755's with the group (high 16 bits) two
// lower (the sibling branch's worlddecrypt -build 70783, RETAIL.md), so its
// names come from the 70755 table by that shift.
const (
	BuildForever = 70755
	BuildRetail  = 70783
)

// Decoder follows every world connection in a capture.
type Decoder struct {
	// Build names the messages: BuildForever, BuildRetail, or 0 to tell
	// from the first SMSG_AUTH_CHALLENGE (0x4E0000 Forever, 0x4C0000 retail).
	Build       int
	SecretsPath string

	conns       map[string]*conn
	sessionKeys [][]byte
}

// New returns a decoder that reads keys from bnetrelay's secrets.jsonl.
func New(build int, secretsPath string) *Decoder {
	return &Decoder{Build: build, SecretsPath: secretsPath, conns: map[string]*conn{}}
}

type frame struct {
	t     time.Time
	index uint64 // the frame's position in its direction: the GCM nonce counter
	tag   [framing.TagLen]byte
	clear bool
	op    uint32
	body  []byte
}

type dirState struct {
	next    uint32
	started bool
	pending map[uint32]Segment // out-of-order segments by seq
	buf     []byte             // in-order bytes not yet framed
	bufT    time.Time          // arrival of the newest bytes in buf
	hs      bool               // handshake line consumed
	count   uint64
	held    []frame // frames waiting for the key
	inf     *inflater
}

type conn struct {
	port     uint16
	c2s, s2c dirState
	key      *[world.EncryptionKeyLen]byte
	first    *frame // first client frame: AUTH_SESSION or AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION
	chal     []byte // server challenge from SMSG_AUTH_CHALLENGE
	sk       []byte // this connection's session key, once found
	dead     bool
}

// Feed takes one segment and returns the messages it completed.
func (d *Decoder) Feed(s Segment) []Msg {
	var key string
	var c2s bool
	switch {
	case s.DPort == WorldPort:
		key, c2s = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Dst, s.SPort), true
	case s.SPort == WorldPort:
		key = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Src, s.DPort)
	default:
		return nil
	}
	c := d.conns[key]
	if c == nil {
		port := s.DPort
		if c2s {
			port = s.SPort
		}
		c = &conn{port: port}
		d.conns[key] = c
	}
	if c.dead {
		return nil
	}
	ds := &c.s2c
	if c2s {
		ds = &c.c2s
	}
	var fresh []frame
	for _, chunk := range ds.reassemble(s) {
		fresh = append(fresh, ds.frames(chunk)...)
	}
	if len(fresh) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return d.handle(c, c2s, fresh)
}

// reassemble returns in-order bytes the segment makes available.
func (ds *dirState) reassemble(s Segment) [][]byte {
	if ds.pending == nil {
		ds.pending = map[uint32]Segment{}
	}
	if s.SYN {
		ds.next, ds.started = s.Seq+1, true
		return nil
	}
	if !ds.started {
		ds.next, ds.started = s.Seq, true // capture began mid-stream
	}
	if len(s.Payload) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	ds.pending[s.Seq] = s
	var out [][]byte
	for progressed := true; progressed; {
		progressed = false
		for seq, p := range ds.pending {
			off := int32(ds.next - seq) // bytes of p already delivered
			if off < 0 {
				continue
			}
			delete(ds.pending, seq)
			if int(off) < len(p.Payload) {
				out = append(out, p.Payload[off:])
				ds.next += uint32(len(p.Payload) - int(off))
				ds.bufT = p.T
				progressed = true
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// frames appends bytes and cuts every complete frame.
func (ds *dirState) frames(b []byte) []frame {
	ds.buf = append(ds.buf, b...)
	if !ds.hs {
		nl := bytes.IndexByte(ds.buf, '\n')
		if nl < 0 {
			return nil
		}
		ds.buf, ds.hs = ds.buf[nl+1:], true
	}
	var out []frame
	for len(ds.buf) >= 4+framing.TagLen {
		size := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ds.buf))
		end := 4 + framing.TagLen + size
		if size < 4 || size > 1<<20 {
			ds.buf = nil // lost framing; nothing after this can be trusted
			break
		}
		if len(ds.buf) < end {
			break
		}
		f := frame{t: ds.bufT, index: ds.count}
		ds.count++
		copy(f.tag[:], ds.buf[4:])
		f.clear = f.tag == [framing.TagLen]byte{}
		payload := append([]byte(nil), ds.buf[4+framing.TagLen:end]...)
		if f.clear {
			f.op, f.body = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(payload), payload[4:]
		} else {
			f.body = payload
		}
		out = append(out, f)
		ds.buf = ds.buf[end:]
	}
	return out
}

func (d *Decoder) handle(c *conn, c2s bool, fresh []frame) []Msg {
	ds := &c.s2c
	if c2s {
		ds = &c.c2s
	}
	if c.key == nil {
		for i := range fresh {
			f := fresh[i]
			if f.index == 0 && f.clear {
				if c2s {
					c.first = &f
				} else if len(f.body) >= 64 {
					c.chal = append([]byte(nil), f.body[32:64]...)
				}
			}
		}
		ds.held = append(ds.held, fresh...)
		if d.Build == 0 && !c2s {
			for _, f := range fresh {
				if f.index == 0 && f.clear {
					switch f.op {
					case 0x4E0000:
						d.Build = BuildForever
					case 0x4C0000:
						d.Build = BuildRetail
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if !d.findKey(c) {
			return nil
		}
		var out []Msg
		out = append(out, d.open(c, false, c.s2c.held)...)
		out = append(out, d.open(c, true, c.c2s.held)...)
		c.s2c.held, c.c2s.held = nil, nil
		return out
	}
	return d.open(c, c2s, fresh)
}

// findKey tries every key the secrets allow on the first encrypted server
// frame. It is called again on every new frame until one works.
func (d *Decoder) findKey(c *conn) bool {
	if c.first == nil || c.chal == nil {
		return false
	}
	var probe *frame
	for i := range c.s2c.held {
		if !c.s2c.held[i].clear {
			probe = &c.s2c.held[i]
			break
		}
	}
	if probe == nil {
		return false
	}
	first := d.name(opcodes.ClientToServer, c.first.op)
	if len(c.first.body) == world.AuthContinuedSessionLen {
		first = "CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION" // retail moved even the auth numbers
	}
	type cand struct {
		key [world.EncryptionKeyLen]byte
		sk  []byte
	}
	var cands []cand
	if strings.Contains(first, "CONTINUED") {
		a, err := world.DecodeAuthContinuedSession(c.first.body)
		if err != nil {
			c.dead = true
			return false
		}
		for _, sk := range d.sessionKeys {
			if k, err := world.EncryptionKey(sk, a.LocalChallenge[:], c.chal); err == nil {
				cands = append(cands, cand{k, nil})
			}
		}
	} else {
		a, err := world.DecodeAuthSessionBody(c.first.body)
		if err != nil {
			c.dead = true
			return false
		}
		clients, joins, err := ReadSecrets(d.SecretsPath)
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		for _, cs := range clients {
			for _, js := range joins {
				kd := append(append([]byte(nil), cs...), js...)
				sk, err := world.SessionKey(kd, a.LocalChallenge[:], c.chal)
				if err != nil {
					continue
				}
				if k, err := world.EncryptionKey(sk[:], a.LocalChallenge[:], c.chal); err == nil {
					cands = append(cands, cand{k, append([]byte(nil), sk[:]...)})
				}
			}
		}
	}
	for _, k := range cands {
		ci, err := world.NewCipherAt(k.key[:], world.Recv, probe.index)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		if _, err := ci.Open(nil, probe.body, probe.tag[:]); err == nil {
			key := k.key
			c.key = &key
			if k.sk != nil {
				c.sk = k.sk
				d.sessionKeys = append(d.sessionKeys, k.sk)
			}
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (d *Decoder) open(c *conn, c2s bool, fs []frame) []Msg {
	ds, wdir, odir := &c.s2c, world.Recv, opcodes.ServerToClient
	if c2s {
		ds, wdir, odir = &c.c2s, world.Send, opcodes.ClientToServer
	}
	if ds.inf == nil {
		ds.inf = newInflater()
	}
	var out []Msg
	for _, f := range fs {
		op, body := f.op, f.body
		if !f.clear {
			ci, err := world.NewCipherAt(c.key[:], wdir, f.index)
			if err != nil {
				continue
			}
			plain, err := ci.Open(nil, f.body, f.tag[:])
			if err != nil || len(plain) < 4 {
				out = append(out, Msg{T: f.t, Port: c.port, Dir: odir, Note: "decrypt failed"})
				continue
			}
			op, body = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(plain), plain[4:]
		}
		var expand func(op uint32, body []byte, depth int)
		expand = func(op uint32, body []byte, depth int) {
			n := d.name(odir, op)
			switch {
			case depth < 3 && strings.Contains(n, "COMPRESSED_PACKET") && len(body) >= 12:
				plain, err := ds.inf.inflate(body)
				if err == nil && len(plain) >= 4 {
					expand(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(plain), plain[4:], depth+1)
					return
				}
				out = append(out, Msg{T: f.t, Port: c.port, Dir: odir, Opcode: op, Name: n, Body: body, Note: fmt.Sprintf("inflate: %v", err)})
				return
			case depth < 3 && strings.Contains(n, "MULTIPLE_PACKETS"):
				b := body
				for len(b) >= 6 {
					sz := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b))
					if len(b) < 6+sz {
						break
					}
					expand(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[2:]), b[6:6+sz], depth+1)
					b = b[6+sz:]
				}
				return
			}
			out = append(out, Msg{T: f.t, Port: c.port, Dir: odir, Opcode: op, Name: n, Body: body})
		}
		expand(op, body, 0)
	}
	return out
}

// retailC2S names the retail client messages the combat feed needs, read off
// the retail capture of 2026-11-05 03:02 (C2S does not follow the S2C group
// shift): 0x430016 carries the character's GUID, then 600.0 (the far clip)
// and a bit, once, before world entry, as CMSG_PLAYER_LOGIN (Forever
// 0x440016) does; 0x3E00CA carries one GUID, later an empty one, and the
// player's next 44 hits went to that GUID.
var retailC2S = map[uint32]string{
	0x430016: "CMSG_PLAYER_LOGIN",
	0x3E00CA: "CMSG_SET_SELECTION",
}

// name describes a message number for the decoder's build.
func (d *Decoder) name(dir opcodes.Direction, op uint32) string {
	switch d.Build {
	case BuildRetail:
		if dir == opcodes.ClientToServer {
			if n, ok := retailC2S[op]; ok {
				return n + "~"
			}
		}
		if n := opcodes.DescribeBuild(BuildForever, dir, op+0x20000); !strings.HasPrefix(n, "0x") {
			return n + "~" // named by the group shift: a guess per message
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("%#08x", op)
	case 0:
		return opcodes.DescribeBuild(BuildForever, dir, op)
	}
	return opcodes.DescribeBuild(d.Build, dir, op)
}

// ReadSecrets reads bnetrelay's secrets.jsonl: every client secret
// (Param_ClientInfo) and join secret (Param_JoinSecret) it has logged.
func ReadSecrets(path string) (clients, joins [][]byte, err error) {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	secretRE := regexp.MustCompile(`"secret":\[([0-9, ]+)\]`)
	for _, line := range bytes.Split(raw, []byte("\n")) {
		if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		var r struct {
			ClientInfo string `json:"client_info"`
			JoinSecret string `json:"join_secret"`
		}
		if json.Unmarshal(line, &r) != nil {
			continue // a line still being written
		}
		if m := secretRE.FindStringSubmatch(r.ClientInfo); m != nil {
			var b []byte
			for _, s := range strings.Split(m[1], ",") {
				var v int
				fmt.Sscan(strings.TrimSpace(s), &v)
				b = append(b, byte(v))
			}
			clients = append(clients, b)
		}
		if r.JoinSecret != "" {
			if b, err := hex.DecodeString(r.JoinSecret); err == nil {
				joins = append(joins, b)
			}
		}
	}
	if len(clients) == 0 || len(joins) == 0 {
		return nil, nil, errors.New("secrets: need a client secret and a join secret")
	}
	return clients, joins, nil
}

// inflater is one direction's persistent raw-deflate stream
// (SMSG_COMPRESSED_PACKET: u32 size, u32 plain adler, u32 compressed adler,
// deflate bytes).
type inflater struct {
	feed *feeder
	r    io.ReadCloser
}

type feeder struct{ buf []byte }

func (f *feeder) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if len(f.buf) == 0 {
		return 0, io.ErrNoProgress
	}
	n := copy(p, f.buf)
	f.buf = f.buf[n:]
	return n, nil
}

func (f *feeder) ReadByte() (byte, error) {
	if len(f.buf) == 0 {
		return 0, io.ErrNoProgress
	}
	b := f.buf[0]
	f.buf = f.buf[1:]
	return b, nil
}

func newInflater() *inflater {
	fd := &feeder{}
	return &inflater{feed: fd, r: flate.NewReader(fd)}
}

func (in *inflater) inflate(body []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	size := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body)
	if size > 1<<20 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("claims %d bytes", size)
	}
	in.feed.buf = append(in.feed.buf, body[12:]...)
	plain := make([]byte, size)
	_, err := io.ReadFull(in.r, plain)
	return plain, err
}

```

`radar/README.md`:

```md
# wow-radar

The world around your character in WoW, from the server's own positions: every player, creature
and game object the server tells the client about, where moving mobs are heading, and you in the
middle. Nothing touches the game process: the input is the world connection's traffic, recorded and
decrypted by `tools/capture-live` (repo root), or a local TrinityCore fork's `World.pkt`.

```bash
go run . -run ../captures/<stamp> -follow               # retail, live
go run . -run <capture-live --game forever run> -follow -build 70755           # Forever, live
go run . -pkt <fork>/logs/World.pkt -follow                      # the local fork
go run . -jsonl conn-1.jsonl,conn-2.jsonl -speed 1                             # replay worlddecrypt output
python3 overlay.py                                                             # over the game window
python3 tools/nodes-export.py                                                  # once: herb and ore spawns -> nodes.json
```

Then http://127.0.0.1:8791 for the 3D view (three.js), or the overlay over the game.

## MCP

The running radar is also an MCP server at `http://127.0.0.1:8791/mcp` (JSON-RPC over HTTP,
read-only), so Claude Code can ask what's around the character while you play:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http wow-radar http://127.0.0.1:8791/mcp
```

| tool | what |
|---|---|
| `radar_self` | map, position, level, health, the quest log (names, objectives, progress), enemy players closing in |
| `radar_around` | everything within `radius` yards, nearest first: name, level, health %, dead, moving with destination and ETA, quest-giver icon |
| `radar_find` | tracked objects by name, nearest first |
| `radar_quest_givers` | NPCs nearby with a ! or ? |
| `radar_nodes` | herb and ore spots with up/empty/gone and respawn estimates |
| `radar_status` | is the stream live: clock, object count, message counters |

On Forever (`-pkt`, or `-build` other than retail's 70783) names come from the Forever names db (`WOW_FOREVER_DB`)
(`-db`), read once with the `sqlite3` command line, since Forever's WDB caches start empty.

## What it reads

| Message | What for |
|---|---|
| `SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT` | every object's position and kind (create blocks); on Forever also level, health, NPC flags and our quest log |
| `SMSG_ON_MONSTER_MOVE` | mob splines: where a unit goes and when it gets there |
| `SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE*` | other players; they coast at their measured speed between updates |
| client `CMSG_MOVE_*` | us |
| `SMSG_QUEST_GIVER_STATUS(_MULTIPLE)` | the ! and ? over each NPC |
| `creaturecache.wdb`, query responses, `forever.db` | names |

## The overlay

A click-through window over the game (shown while WoW is in front), heading-up:

- **Forever: levelling.** Creatures in con colours, gold rings on your quest targets with their
  counts ("Tough Wolf Meat 3/8"): mobs to kill, mobs that drop a quest item, objects to loot or use,
  from the Forever names db (`WOW_FOREVER_DB`). Quest givers' ! and ?, and a list of the nearest objectives.
- **Retail: players.** Everyone within ~200 yd, which way they face, distance and height.
- **Herbs and ore (both modes).** Every node spot, whatever your tracking: green diamonds for
  herbs, copper squares for ore. Filled when the server shows the node up; hollow with a timer once
  it is gathered (a countdown when the respawn has been measured at that spot, else time since);
  faint when you have been close enough to see it was empty, or saw it up from afar. The nearest
  up ones are listed under the radar and pinned on its edge when beyond it.
- **Enemy players (Forever).** The other faction in red with level and class. Anyone inside 60 yd,
  or inside 120 yd and closing faster than 3 yd/s, gets a warning line above the radar and a chime
  the first time (`--no-chime` to mute).
- `--heads` (experimental): arrows over players' heads with a fixed chase camera. The network
  carries your facing, not the camera, so it only lines up while the camera sits where the flags say.

`python3 overlay.py --help` for the flags.

## Node spots

`tools/nodes-export.py` reads every herb and ore spawn in the Forever names db (`WOW_FOREVER_DB`)
(Questie and Wowhead, as zone-map fractions), fits each zone's map to world coordinates from the
NPC spawns that have both (exact: 49/49 zones at 0.0 yd), and writes `nodes.json`: about 15,000
spots. A live Peacebloom in Elwynn lands 0.1 yd from its exported spawn. Forever's own starter-zone
nodes (Wilted Peacebloom, Stunted Silverleaf, Poor Copper Vein) are not in the db; the radar learns
those as you see them.

A node that is destroyed, or leaves view while you stand inside 0.6 × `-vis` (90 yd) of it, was
gathered; when it is back at the same spot the time is one respawn measurement. Gathered and empty
times and the measurements are kept in `~/.config/wow-radar/seen.json` (live runs only, `-seen ""`
to disable), so the next session starts knowing which spots were cleared and when.

## Layout

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `main.go` | the radar: inputs, the world model, `/state`, the page |
| `web/index.html` | the 3D view |
| `overlay.py` | the overlay (PyObjC) |
| `nodes.go` | herb and ore spots: up, gone, empty, last seen; respawn timers |
| `pvp.go` | enemy players: faction from race, closing speed, warnings |
| `tools/nodes-export.py` | forever.db's node spawns to world coordinates (`nodes.json`) |

The decoders are the repo's own `protocol/updateobject`, `worldstream`, `pktlog` and `state`.
Herb and ore nodes, and Forever names, need a Forever names db (`WOW_FOREVER_DB`); without one the
radar still runs, with fewer names and no nodes.

```

`radar/foreverdb.go`:

```go
package main

// Names from a Forever names db (WOW_FOREVER_DB) for Forever sessions, where the client's
// WDB caches start empty: creature and game-object names by entry, and quest
// names with their objectives for the MCP's quest log. Read once at start
// through the sqlite3 command line, so the radar needs no SQLite driver.

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"os/exec"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

type questInfo struct {
	Name       string      `json:"name"`
	Level      int         `json:"level,omitempty"`
	Objectives []objective `json:"objectives,omitempty"`
}

type objective struct {
	Text  string `json:"text"`
	Count int    `json:"count,omitempty"`
}

// questNames is filled by loadForeverDB; empty without a database.
var questNames = map[int32]*questInfo{}

func sqliteRows(db, query string, each func([]string)) error {
	out, err := exec.Command("sqlite3", "-readonly", "-separator", "\t", db, query).Output()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("sqlite3 %s: %w", db, err)
	}
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(bytes.NewReader(out))
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 1<<20), 1<<20)
	for sc.Scan() {
		each(strings.Split(sc.Text(), "\t"))
	}
	return sc.Err()
}

// loadForeverDB fills names the caches don't have; it returns how many of each it read.
func loadForeverDB(db string, w *world) (npcs, objects, quests int, err error) {
	clean := func(s string) string { return strings.ReplaceAll(s, `\n`, " ") }
	fill := func(table string, into map[uint32]string, n *int) error {
		return sqliteRows(db, "select id, name from "+table+" where name is not null and name != ''", func(f []string) {
			if len(f) < 2 {
				return
			}
			id, e := strconv.ParseUint(f[0], 10, 32)
			if e != nil {
				return
			}
			if _, ok := into[uint32(id)]; !ok {
				into[uint32(id)] = f[1]
			}
			*n++
		})
	}
	if err = fill("npcs", w.names, &npcs); err != nil {
		return
	}
	if err = fill("objects", w.goNames, &objects); err != nil {
		return
	}
	err = sqliteRows(db, "select id, name, coalesce(level, 0) from quests where name is not null", func(f []string) {
		if len(f) < 3 {
			return
		}
		id, e := strconv.Atoi(f[0])
		if e != nil {
			return
		}
		lvl, _ := strconv.Atoi(f[2])
		questNames[int32(id)] = &questInfo{Name: f[1], Level: lvl}
		quests++
	})
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	err = sqliteRows(db, "select quest, coalesce(text, ''), coalesce(count, 0) from objectives order by quest, n", func(f []string) {
		if len(f) < 3 {
			return
		}
		id, e := strconv.Atoi(f[0])
		if e != nil {
			return
		}
		if q := questNames[int32(id)]; q != nil {
			c, _ := strconv.Atoi(f[2])
			q.Objectives = append(q.Objectives, objective{Text: clean(f[1]), Count: c})
		}
	})
	return
}

```

`radar/main.go`:

```go
// Command radar is a live 3D radar of the world around the player, drawn
// from the positions the server sends: players, creatures and game objects,
// where moving mobs are heading, and ourselves at the centre.
//
//	go run . -run captures/<stamp> -follow   # live, with capture-live
//	go run . -jsonl conn-1.jsonl,conn-2.jsonl -speed 1                   # replay worlddecrypt output
//	go run . -pkt <fork>/logs/World.pkt -follow             # the local fork's packet log
//	go run . -run <capture-live --game forever run> -follow -build 70755   # Forever live
//
// Then open http://localhost:8791. Nothing touches the game process: the
// input is the world connection's own traffic (tcpdump + the relay's keys).
//
// Sources: SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT creates (movement block: every object's
// position), SMSG_ON_MONSTER_MOVE (splines: where a unit is going and how
// long it takes), SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE (other players), the client's own
// movement messages (us), and the client's creature/game-object name caches
// plus the query responses that arrive while it runs.
//
// On Forever (70755) the update fields decode too: levels, health, NPC flags
// and our quest log (QuestLog.QuestID / ObjectiveProgress), and
// SMSG_QUEST_GIVER_STATUS(_MULTIPLE) gives each NPC's quest icon. The
// overlay's levelling mode joins those with a Forever names db (WOW_FOREVER_DB).
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"embed"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"log"
	"math"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/codec"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/opcodes"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/pktlog"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/updateobject"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/updateobject/apply"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/worldstream"
	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/state"
)

//go:embed web
var web embed.FS

type msg struct {
	T    time.Time
	C2S  bool
	Op   uint32
	Name string // bare name, SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT, or ""
	Body []byte
}

type ent struct {
	GUID  string  `json:"g"`
	Kind  string  `json:"k"`
	Entry uint32  `json:"e,omitempty"`
	Name  string  `json:"n,omitempty"`
	X     float32 `json:"x"`
	Y     float32 `json:"y"`
	Z     float32 `json:"z"`
	O     float32 `json:"o"`
	// The active spline, if any: from Pos at T0 to Dest at T1.
	DX, DY, DZ float32   `json:"-"`
	T0, T1     time.Time `json:"-"`
	Moving     bool      `json:"m,omitempty"`
	ToX        float32   `json:"tx,omitempty"`
	ToY        float32   `json:"ty,omitempty"`
	ToZ        float32   `json:"tz,omitempty"`
	ETA        float64   `json:"eta,omitempty"` // seconds to the destination
	// From the update fields (Forever: they decode; retail: not yet).
	Level   uint8     `json:"lvl,omitempty"`
	HP      int64     `json:"hp,omitempty"`
	MaxHP   int64     `json:"mhp,omitempty"`
	Dead    bool      `json:"dead,omitempty"`
	NPC     uint32    `json:"npcf,omitempty"`
	QGiver  string    `json:"qs,omitempty"` // quest giver status: turnin, available, trivial, future
	Race    uint8     `json:"race,omitempty"`
	Class   uint8     `json:"cls,omitempty"`
	Hostile bool      `json:"hostile,omitempty"` // a player of the other faction
	spot    *spot     // a herb or ore node: its spot
	Seen    time.Time `json:"-"`
	// Between a player's movement messages: the velocity measured from the
	// last two (yards per second), while its flags say it is moving.
	VX, VY, VZ float32 `json:"-"`
	MT         uint32  `json:"-"` // the mover's clock at the last message (ms)
	Coast      bool    `json:"-"`
}

// moving flags: forward, backward, strafe left/right, falling, ascending, descending.
const movingFlags = 0x0F | 0x800 | 0x200000 | 0x400000

// moveTo applies a MovementInfo and measures the velocity since the last one.
func moveTo(e *ent, mi *updateobject.MovementInfo, t time.Time) {
	p := mi.Position
	if e.MT != 0 && mi.MoveTime > e.MT && mi.MoveTime-e.MT < 3000 {
		dt := float32(mi.MoveTime-e.MT) / 1000
		vx, vy, vz := (p.X-e.X)/dt, (p.Y-e.Y)/dt, (p.Z-e.Z)/dt
		if math.Hypot(float64(vx), float64(vy)) < 120 { // not a teleport
			e.VX, e.VY, e.VZ = vx, vy, vz
		}
	}
	e.Coast = mi.Flags&movingFlags != 0
	if !e.Coast {
		e.VX, e.VY, e.VZ = 0, 0, 0
	}
	e.X, e.Y, e.Z, e.O = p.X, p.Y, p.Z, p.O
	e.MT = mi.MoveTime
	e.Moving = false
	e.Seen = t
}

// coast moves e on by its velocity for the time since its last message (at most 1.5 s).
func coast(e *ent, now time.Time) {
	if !e.Coast {
		return
	}
	dt := float32(math.Min(now.Sub(e.Seen).Seconds(), 1.5))
	if dt <= 0 {
		return
	}
	e.X += e.VX * dt
	e.Y += e.VY * dt
	e.Z += e.VZ * dt
}

type world struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	ents     map[codec.GUID]*ent
	self     codec.GUID
	mapID    uint16
	clock    time.Time // stream time of the last message
	wall     time.Time // wall time it arrived
	speed    float64
	names    map[uint32]string // creature entry -> name
	goNames  map[uint32]string
	players  map[codec.GUID]string
	stats    map[string]int
	lastMove time.Time
	// The full update-field model (Forever's fields decode) and our quest log.
	st      *state.State
	quests  map[int]*quest // quest log slot -> quest
	qstatus map[codec.GUID]uint64
	nodes   *nodes
	vis     float64 // yards inside which the server always shows a node that is up
}

type quest struct {
	ID       int32     `json:"id"`
	Progress [24]int32 `json:"-"`
	P        []int32   `json:"p"`
}

func newWorld(speed float64) *world {
	return &world{ents: map[codec.GUID]*ent{}, names: map[uint32]string{}, goNames: map[uint32]string{},
		players: map[codec.GUID]string{}, stats: map[string]int{}, speed: speed,
		st: state.New(), quests: map[int]*quest{}, qstatus: map[codec.GUID]uint64{},
		nodes: newNodes(), vis: 90}
}

// now is the stream's clock: the last message's time plus the wall time
// since (scaled in replay), so splines keep moving between messages.
func (w *world) now() time.Time {
	if w.clock.IsZero() {
		return time.Now()
	}
	d := time.Since(w.wall)
	if d > 5*time.Second {
		d = 5 * time.Second
	}
	return w.clock.Add(time.Duration(float64(d) * w.speed))
}

func guidType(g codec.GUID) uint64  { return g.Hi >> 58 }
func guidEntry(g codec.GUID) uint32 { return uint32((g.Hi >> 6) & 0x7FFFFF) }

var kinds = map[updateobject.ObjectType]string{
	updateobject.TypeUnit: "unit", updateobject.TypePlayer: "player", updateobject.TypeActivePlayer: "player",
	updateobject.TypeGameObject: "gameobject", updateobject.TypeCorpse: "corpse",
	updateobject.TypeAreaTrigger: "areatrigger", updateobject.TypeDynamicObject: "dynamic",
}

func (w *world) get(g codec.GUID, kind string) *ent {
	e := w.ents[g]
	if e == nil {
		e = &ent{GUID: fmt.Sprintf("%016x%016x", g.Hi, g.Lo), Kind: kind}
		if kind == "unit" || kind == "gameobject" {
			e.Entry = guidEntry(g)
		}
		w.ents[g] = e
	}
	return e
}

func (w *world) handle(m msg) {
	w.mu.Lock()
	defer w.mu.Unlock()
	w.clock, w.wall = m.T, time.Now()
	if m.C2S {
		w.c2s(m)
		return
	}
	switch m.Name {
	case "SMSG_LOGIN_VERIFY_WORLD", "SMSG_NEW_WORLD", "SMSG_LOGOUT_COMPLETE":
		// The client drops every object here and the server sends them all again with new creates.
		// Without this a relog (or a World.pkt holding several sessions) leaves a stale copy of each.
		w.ents = map[codec.GUID]*ent{}
		w.qstatus = map[codec.GUID]uint64{}
		if m.Name == "SMSG_LOGOUT_COMPLETE" {
			w.self, w.quests = codec.GUID{}, map[int]*quest{}
		}
		w.stats["world reset"]++
	case "SMSG_UPDATE_OBJECT":
		u, err := updateobject.Decode(m.Body)
		if err != nil {
			w.stats["update_object failed"]++
			return
		}
		w.stats["update_object"]++
		w.mapID = u.MapID
		if r := apply.Apply(w.st, u); len(r.Skipped) == 0 {
			w.stats["fields applied"]++
		}
		for _, b := range u.Blocks {
			if b.Create != nil && b.Create.Movement != nil && b.Create.Movement.ThisIsYou {
				w.self = b.GUID
			}
			if b.GUID != w.self || w.self == (codec.GUID{}) {
				continue
			}
			var fs []updateobject.Field
			switch {
			case b.Create != nil:
				if of, err := b.Create.DecodeFields(); err == nil && of.Player != nil {
					fs = of.Player.Fields
				}
			case b.Values != nil:
				if d, err := updateobject.DecodeValues(updateobject.TypeActivePlayer, b.Values); d != nil && (err == nil || d.Player != nil) {
					fs = d.Player
				}
			}
			w.questFields(fs)
		}
		if rm := u.Removed; rm != nil {
			for i, l := range [][]codec.GUID{rm.Destroyed, rm.OutOfRange} {
				for _, g := range l {
					if g == w.self {
						continue
					}
					if e := w.ents[g]; e != nil && e.spot != nil {
						// out of range while we stand well inside view range: it went
						gathered := i == 0 || w.distSelf(e) < w.vis*0.6
						w.nodes.down(e.spot, e.GUID, gathered, m.T)
					}
					delete(w.ents, g)
				}
			}
		}
		for _, b := range u.Blocks {
			c := b.Create
			if c == nil {
				continue
			}
			kind, ok := kinds[c.ObjectType]
			if !ok || c.Movement == nil {
				continue
			}
			var p *updateobject.Pos4
			switch mv := c.Movement; {
			case mv.Movement != nil:
				p = &mv.Movement.Info.Position
			case mv.Stationary != nil:
				p = mv.Stationary
			}
			if p == nil {
				continue
			}
			e := w.get(b.GUID, kind)
			e.X, e.Y, e.Z, e.O = p.X, p.Y, p.Z, p.O
			e.Moving = false
			e.Seen = m.T
			if c.Movement.ThisIsYou {
				w.self = b.GUID
			}
			if kind == "gameobject" {
				if name := w.goName(e.Entry); nodeKind(name) != "" {
					e.spot = w.nodes.up(e.GUID, u.MapID, name, e.X, e.Y, e.Z, m.T)
				}
			}
		}
	case "SMSG_ON_MONSTER_MOVE":
		mm, err := updateobject.DecodeMonsterMove(m.Body)
		if err != nil {
			w.stats["monster_move failed"]++
			return
		}
		w.stats["monster_move"]++
		e := w.get(mm.Mover, "unit")
		d := mm.Dest()
		e.X, e.Y, e.Z = mm.Start.X, mm.Start.Y, mm.Start.Z
		e.DX, e.DY, e.DZ = d.X, d.Y, d.Z
		left := time.Duration(int64(mm.MoveTime)-int64(mm.Elapsed)) * time.Millisecond
		e.T0, e.T1 = m.T, m.T.Add(left)
		e.Moving = len(mm.Points) > 0 && left > 0
		if e.Moving && (d.X != e.X || d.Y != e.Y) {
			e.O = float32(math.Atan2(float64(d.Y-e.Y), float64(d.X-e.X)))
		}
		e.Seen = m.T
	case "SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE", "SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE_RUN_SPEED", "SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE_FLIGHT_SPEED",
		"SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE_SWIM_SPEED", "SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE_COLLISION_HEIGHT", "SMSG_MOVE_UPDATE_KNOCK_BACK":
		// all start with the mover's MovementInfo (checked: every one decodes, 2026-11-05)
		mi, err := updateobject.DecodeMoveUpdate(m.Body)
		if err != nil || !sane(mi.Position) {
			w.stats["move_update failed"]++
			return
		}
		w.stats["move_update"]++
		kind := "unit"
		if guidType(mi.Mover) == 2 {
			kind = "player"
		}
		moveTo(w.get(mi.Mover, kind), mi, m.T)
	case "SMSG_QUEST_GIVER_STATUS":
		r := codec.NewReader(m.Body)
		if g, err := r.GUID(); err == nil {
			if v, err := r.Uint64(); err == nil {
				w.qstatus[g] = v
			}
		}
	case "SMSG_QUEST_GIVER_STATUS_MULTIPLE":
		r := codec.NewReader(m.Body)
		n, _ := r.Uint32()
		for i := 0; i < int(n) && i < 4096; i++ {
			g, err := r.GUID()
			if err != nil {
				break
			}
			v, err := r.Uint64()
			if err != nil {
				break
			}
			w.qstatus[g] = v
		}
	case "SMSG_QUERY_CREATURE_RESPONSE":
		if id, n := cacheName(m.Body); id != 0 && n != "" {
			w.names[id] = n
		}
	case "SMSG_QUERY_GAME_OBJECT_RESPONSE":
		if id, n := cacheName(m.Body); id != 0 && n != "" {
			w.goNames[id] = n
		}
	case "SMSG_QUERY_PLAYER_NAMES_RESPONSE":
		for g, n := range playerNames(m.Body) {
			w.players[g] = n
		}
	}
}

func (w *world) goName(entry uint32) string {
	if n := w.goNames[entry]; n != "" {
		return n
	}
	return w.nodes.entries[entry]
}

func (w *world) distSelf(e *ent) float64 {
	me := w.ents[w.self]
	if me == nil {
		return math.Inf(1)
	}
	return math.Hypot(float64(e.X-me.X), float64(e.Y-me.Y))
}

// c2s: the client's own movement messages carry our MovementInfo. On
// 70783 they are the 0x41 group (CMSG_MOVE_*, unnamed in our table).
func (w *world) c2s(m msg) {
	if m.Op>>16 != 0x41 && !strings.HasPrefix(m.Name, "CMSG_MOVE") {
		return
	}
	mi, err := updateobject.DecodeMoveUpdate(m.Body)
	if err != nil || guidType(mi.Mover) != 2 || !sane(mi.Position) {
		return
	}
	if w.self != mi.Mover {
		w.self = mi.Mover
	}
	w.stats["self_move"]++
	moveTo(w.get(mi.Mover, "player"), mi, m.T)
	w.lastMove = m.T
}

func sane(p updateobject.Pos4) bool {
	return math.Abs(float64(p.X)) < 20000 && math.Abs(float64(p.Y)) < 20000 && math.Abs(float64(p.Z)) < 10000 && !math.IsNaN(float64(p.X))
}

var questField = regexp.MustCompile(`^QuestLog\.(QuestID|ObjectiveProgress)\[(\d+)\](?:\[(\d+)\])?$`)

// questFields applies our PlayerData quest log fields (QuestLog.QuestID[i],
// QuestLog.ObjectiveProgress[i][j]).
func (w *world) questFields(fs []updateobject.Field) {
	for _, f := range fs {
		m := questField.FindStringSubmatch(f.Name)
		if m == nil {
			continue
		}
		i, _ := strconv.Atoi(m[2])
		q := w.quests[i]
		if q == nil {
			q = &quest{}
			w.quests[i] = q
		}
		v := toI32(f.Value)
		if m[1] == "QuestID" {
			if v != q.ID {
				q.Progress = [24]int32{}
			}
			q.ID = v
		} else if j, _ := strconv.Atoi(m[3]); j < 24 {
			q.Progress[j] = v
		}
	}
}

func toI32(v any) int32 {
	switch x := v.(type) {
	case int32:
		return x
	case uint32:
		return int32(x)
	case int16:
		return int32(x)
	case uint16:
		return int32(x)
	case int8:
		return int32(x)
	case uint8:
		return int32(x)
	case int64:
		return int32(x)
	}
	return 0
}

// giverStatus names the quest-giver icon the client would draw (QuestGiverStatus bits).
func giverStatus(v uint64) string {
	switch {
	case v&0x0000000FE000 != 0 || v&0xFFFE00000000 != 0: // Reward..ImportantReward, *RewardComplete*
		return "turnin"
	case v&(0x400000|0x800000|0x1000000|0x2000000|0x10000000|0x40000000|0x100000000) != 0:
		return "available"
	case v&0x1FE0 != 0:
		return "trivial"
	case v&0x1E != 0:
		return "future"
	}
	return ""
}

type snapshot struct {
	Map     uint16         `json:"map"`
	Self    *ent           `json:"self"`
	Objects []ent          `json:"objects"`
	Clock   string         `json:"clock"`
	Stats   map[string]int `json:"stats"`
	Level   uint8          `json:"level,omitempty"`
	Race    uint8          `json:"race,omitempty"`
	Quests  []quest        `json:"quests,omitempty"`
	Nodes   []nodeOut      `json:"nodes,omitempty"`
	Threats []threat       `json:"threats,omitempty"`
}

// fill copies what the field model knows about e's object.
func (w *world) fill(g codec.GUID, c *ent) {
	if o, ok := w.st.Object(state.GUID{Hi: g.Hi, Lo: g.Lo}); ok {
		c.Level, c.HP, c.MaxHP, c.NPC = o.Level, o.Health, o.MaxHealth, o.NpcFlags
		c.Dead = o.MaxHealth > 0 && o.Health == 0
		c.Race, c.Class = o.Race, o.Class
		if c.Entry == 0 {
			c.Entry = o.Entry
		}
	}
	if v, ok := w.qstatus[g]; ok {
		c.QGiver = giverStatus(v)
	}
}

func (w *world) snapshot(radius, nodeRadius float64) snapshot {
	w.mu.Lock()
	defer w.mu.Unlock()
	now := w.now()
	s := snapshot{Map: w.mapID, Clock: now.Format("15:04:05.0"), Stats: map[string]int{}}
	for k, v := range w.stats {
		s.Stats[k] = v
	}
	var sx, sy float32
	if me := w.ents[w.self]; me != nil {
		c := *me
		coast(&c, now)
		w.fill(w.self, &c)
		c.Kind = "self"
		if o, ok := w.st.Object(state.GUID{Hi: w.self.Hi, Lo: w.self.Lo}); ok {
			s.Level, s.Race = o.Level, o.Race
		}
		for i := 0; i < 175; i++ {
			if q := w.quests[i]; q != nil && q.ID > 0 {
				qq := *q
				n := 24
				for n > 0 && q.Progress[n-1] == 0 {
					n--
				}
				qq.P = append([]int32{}, q.Progress[:n]...)
				s.Quests = append(s.Quests, qq)
			}
		}
		c.Name = w.players[w.self]
		s.Self = &c
		sx, sy = c.X, c.Y
	}
	for g, e := range w.ents {
		if g == w.self {
			continue
		}
		c := *e
		coast(&c, now)
		w.fill(g, &c)
		if c.Moving {
			c.ToX, c.ToY, c.ToZ = c.DX, c.DY, c.DZ
			span := c.T1.Sub(c.T0).Seconds()
			f := 1.0
			if span > 0 {
				f = now.Sub(c.T0).Seconds() / span
			}
			if f >= 1 {
				c.X, c.Y, c.Z, c.Moving = c.DX, c.DY, c.DZ, false
				e.X, e.Y, e.Z, e.Moving = c.DX, c.DY, c.DZ, false // arrived
			} else {
				if f < 0 {
					f = 0
				}
				c.X += float32(f) * (c.DX - c.X)
				c.Y += float32(f) * (c.DY - c.Y)
				c.Z += float32(f) * (c.DZ - c.Z)
				c.ETA = c.T1.Sub(now).Seconds()
			}
		}
		if s.Self != nil && math.Hypot(float64(c.X-sx), float64(c.Y-sy)) > radius {
			continue
		}
		switch c.Kind {
		case "unit":
			c.Name = w.names[c.Entry]
		case "gameobject":
			c.Name = w.goName(c.Entry)
		case "player":
			c.Name = w.players[g]
		}
		s.Objects = append(s.Objects, c)
	}
	sort.Slice(s.Objects, func(i, j int) bool { return s.Objects[i].GUID < s.Objects[j].GUID })
	if s.Self != nil {
		s.Threats = threats(s.Self, s.Objects)
		s.Nodes = w.nodes.view(w.mapID, sx, sy, nodeRadius, w.vis, now)
	}
	return s
}

// cacheName pulls (entry, name) out of a creature or game-object record:
// the WDB cache's record body or a query response (u32 entry, then the
// stats with the name as the first printable run).
func cacheName(b []byte) (uint32, string) {
	if len(b) < 8 {
		return 0, ""
	}
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b), firstText(b[4:])
}

func firstText(b []byte) string {
	start := -1
	for i := 0; i <= len(b); i++ {
		ok := i < len(b) && b[i] >= 0x20 && b[i] < 0x7f
		if ok && start < 0 {
			start = i
		}
		if !ok && start >= 0 {
			if i-start >= 3 && strings.ContainsAny(string(b[start:i]), "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz") {
				return string(b[start:i])
			}
			start = -1
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// playerNames: each entry of the response names a player GUID; take the
// player GUIDs in order and the printable runs after each.
func playerNames(b []byte) map[codec.GUID]string {
	out := map[codec.GUID]string{}
	for i := 0; i+18 < len(b); i++ {
		r := codec.NewReader(b[i:])
		g, err := r.GUID()
		if err != nil || guidType(g) != 2 || g.Lo == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if n := firstText(b[i+2 : min(len(b), i+80)]); n != "" && !strings.Contains(n, " ") && len(n) <= 12 {
			out[g] = n
		}
	}
	return out
}

// loadWDB reads a client cache file (creaturecache.wdb / gameobjectcache.wdb):
// a 24-byte header, then records of u32 entry, u32 size, size bytes.
func loadWDB(path string, into map[uint32]string) int {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil || len(b) < 24 {
		return 0
	}
	n := 0
	for p := 24; p+8 <= len(b); {
		id := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[p:])
		sz := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[p+4:]))
		if id == 0 && sz == 0 || p+8+sz > len(b) {
			break
		}
		if name := firstText(b[p+8 : p+8+sz]); name != "" {
			into[id] = name
			n++
		}
		p += 8 + sz
	}
	return n
}

func main() {
	run := flag.String("run", "", "a tools/capture-live run directory (its world.pcap and bnet/*/secrets.jsonl)")
	pcap := flag.String("pcap", "", "the world-port capture")
	secrets := flag.String("secrets", "", "bnetrelay's secrets.jsonl")
