`tools/feedhub/hub.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
)

// streamOnly are the types that are moments, not state: a client that joins
// late is not sent the last one.
var streamOnly = map[string]bool{"event": true}

// resetType starts a new session (a login or relog): the state saved before it
// belongs to the last character, so it is dropped.
const resetType = "player"

// hub holds the latest line of each kind of state and the connected clients.
// Every line gets a sequence number; a client is sent the state it missed,
// then every line after it, in order, with nothing skipped: a client that
// cannot keep up is dropped rather than slowing the feed.
type hub struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	seq     uint64
	state   map[string]stamped // "type" or "type/unit" → its latest line
	clients map[*client]struct{}
	queue   int  // per-client buffer, in lines
	closed  bool // the feed has ended: new clients get the state, then are closed
}

type stamped struct {
	seq  uint64
	typ  string
	line []byte // with "v" and "seq" spliced in
}

type client struct {
	types map[string]bool // nil: every type
	out   chan []byte
	gone  chan struct{} // closed when the hub drops it for being too slow
	once  sync.Once
}

func newHub(queue int) *hub {
	return &hub{state: map[string]stamped{}, clients: map[*client]struct{}{}, queue: queue}
}

// head is the part of a line the hub looks at.
type head struct {
	Type string `json:"type"`
	Unit string `json:"unit"`
}

// publish stamps one feed line and sends it on. Lines that are not JSON
// objects are ignored (they still went to stdout).
func (h *hub) publish(line []byte) {
	if len(line) < 2 || line[0] != '{' {
		return
	}
	var hd head
	if json.Unmarshal(line, &hd) != nil {
		return
	}
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	h.seq++
	s := stamp(h.seq, line)
	if hd.Type == resetType {
		clear(h.state)
	}
	if hd.Type != "" && !streamOnly[hd.Type] {
		k := hd.Type
		if hd.Unit != "" {
			k += "/" + hd.Unit
		}
		h.state[k] = stamped{h.seq, hd.Type, s}
	}
	for c := range h.clients {
		if c.wants(hd.Type) {
			h.send(c, s)
		}
	}
}

// stamp splices {"v":1,"seq":N, in front of the line's own fields.
func stamp(seq uint64, line []byte) []byte {
	b := make([]byte, 0, len(line)+32)
	b = append(b, `{"v":1,"seq":`...)
	b = strconv.AppendUint(b, seq, 10)
	if rest := line[1:]; len(rest) > 0 && rest[0] != '}' {
		b = append(b, ',')
	}
	return append(b, line[1:]...)
}

func (c *client) wants(t string) bool { return c.types == nil || c.types[t] }

// send hands a line to a client, or drops the client if its buffer is full.
// Called with h.mu held.
func (h *hub) send(c *client, line []byte) {
	select {
	case c.out <- line:
	default:
		delete(h.clients, c)
		c.once.Do(func() { close(c.gone) })
	}
}

// join registers a client and queues the current state for it, oldest first,
// then a {"type":"hub","live":true} line carrying the latest seq, all under
// the same lock as publish so no line falls between them.
func (h *hub) join(types map[string]bool) *client {
	c := &client{types: types, out: make(chan []byte, h.queue), gone: make(chan struct{})}
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	for _, s := range h.snapshotLocked() {
		if c.wants(s.typ) {
			h.send(c, s.line)
		}
	}
	// the end of the catch-up: seq from here on rises by one per line
	h.send(c, stamp(h.seq, []byte(`{"type":"hub","live":true}`)))
	select {
	case <-c.gone: // the state alone overflowed its buffer
	default:
		if h.closed {
			close(c.out) // the feed already ended: nothing more will come
		} else {
			h.clients[c] = struct{}{}
		}
	}
	return c
}

func (h *hub) leave(c *client) {
	h.mu.Lock()
	delete(h.clients, c)
	h.mu.Unlock()
}

// snapshot is the current state, oldest first.
func (h *hub) snapshot() []stamped {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	return h.snapshotLocked()
}

func (h *hub) snapshotLocked() []stamped {
	out := make([]stamped, 0, len(h.state))
	for _, s := range h.state {
		out = append(out, s)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].seq < out[j].seq })
	return out
}

// closeAll drops every client, for the end of the feed.
func (h *hub) closeAll() {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	h.closed = true
	for c := range h.clients {
		delete(h.clients, c)
		close(c.out)
	}
}
```

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/coder/websocket"
)

func TestStamp(t *testing.T) {
	for in, want := range map[string]string{
		`{"type":"player","guid":"x"}`: `{"v":1,"seq":7,"type":"player","guid":"x"}`,
		`{}`:                           `{"v":1,"seq":7}`,
	} {
		got := string(stamp(7, []byte(in)))
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("stamp(%s) = %s, want %s", in, got, want)
		}
		if !json.Valid([]byte(got)) {
			t.Errorf("stamp(%s) is not JSON", in)
		}
	}
}

type msg struct {
	V    int    `json:"v"`
	Seq  uint64 `json:"seq"`
	Type string `json:"type"`
	Unit string `json:"unit"`
	N    int    `json:"n"`
}

func dial(t *testing.T, url string) *websocket.Conn {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	c, _, err := websocket.Dial(ctx, url, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return c
}

func read(t *testing.T, c *websocket.Conn) msg {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	_, b, err := c.Read(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var m msg
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &m); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", b, err)
	}
	return m
}

func server(t *testing.T, h *hub, token string) (*httptest.Server, string) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(handler(h, []string{"localhost:*"}, token))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	return srv, "ws" + strings.TrimPrefix(srv.URL, "http")
}

// A late client gets the latest state per type and unit, oldest first, never
// old events, then the live marker and the stream with no gaps.
func TestCatchUpThenStream(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHub(64)
	for _, l := range []string{
		`{"type":"player","guid":"a"}`,
		`{"type":"auras","unit":"player","n":1}`,
		`{"type":"event","sub":"SPELL_DAMAGE"}`,
		`{"type":"auras","unit":"target","n":2}`,
		`{"type":"auras","unit":"player","n":3}`,
		`not json`,
	} {
		h.publish([]byte(l))
	}
	_, url := server(t, h, "")
	c := dial(t, url+"/feed")
	defer c.CloseNow()

	want := []msg{
		{1, 1, "player", "", 0},
		{1, 4, "auras", "target", 2},
		{1, 5, "auras", "player", 3},
		{1, 5, "hub", "", 0},
	}
	for _, w := range want {
		if m := read(t, c); m != w {
			t.Fatalf("got %+v, want %+v", m, w)
		}
	}
	h.publish([]byte(`{"type":"event","n":9}`))
	if m := read(t, c); m.Seq != 6 || m.Type != "event" || m.N != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("stream: got %+v", m)
	}
}

func TestTypesFilter(t *testing.T) {

		t.Fatalf("got %+v", m)
	}
}

// A client that stops reading is dropped with 1008; the feed is not held up.
func TestSlowClientDropped(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHub(4)
	_, url := server(t, h, "")
	c := dial(t, url+"/feed")
	defer c.CloseNow()
	c.SetReadLimit(-1)
	read(t, c) // the hub line
	big := `{"type":"event","pad":"` + strings.Repeat("x", 256<<10) + `"}`
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
			h.publish([]byte(big))
		}
		close(done)
	}()
	select {
	case <-done:
	// A real block never finishes; 15s leaves room for -race on a slow CI runner,
	// where parsing these 50 MB alone takes several seconds.
	case <-time.After(15 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("publish blocked on a slow client")
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	for {
		if _, _, err := c.Read(ctx); err != nil {
			if websocket.CloseStatus(err) != websocket.StatusPolicyViolation {
				t.Fatalf("closed with %v, want 1008", err)
			}
			return
		}
	}
}

func TestOriginAndToken(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHub(64)
	srv, url := server(t, h, "s3cret")
	ctx := context.Background()

	if _, _, err := websocket.Dial(ctx, url+"/feed", nil); err == nil {
		t.Error("no token: connected")
	}
	evil := &websocket.DialOptions{HTTPHeader: http.Header{"Origin": {"https://evil.example"}}}
	if _, _, err := websocket.Dial(ctx, url+"/feed?token=s3cret", evil); err == nil {
		t.Error("foreign origin: connected")
	}
	local := &websocket.DialOptions{HTTPHeader: http.Header{"Origin": {"http://localhost:5173"}}}
	c, _, err := websocket.Dial(ctx, url+"/feed?token=s3cret", local)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("local dev origin: %v", err)
	}

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	if r.StatusCode != http.StatusUnauthorized {
		t.Errorf("/state without token: %d", r.StatusCode)
	}
}
```

`tools/feedhub/main.go`:

```go
// feedhub: the feed as a local WebSocket server. It sits at the end of a feed
// pipe, passes every line through to stdout unchanged, and serves the same
// lines to any number of WebSocket clients: overlays, dashboards, bots.
//
//	combatfeed -run <run> -follow ... | wow-rotation <toml> --feed | feedhub | auraoverlay.py --rotation
//
// Endpoints (default 127.0.0.1:7373):
//
//	ws://…/feed            every line as one text message, as {"v":1,"seq":N,...the line...}.
//	                       A new client first gets the current state (the latest line of each
//	                       type, per unit where a line has one; never "event"; a "player"
//	                       line, a login or relog, starts it afresh), then
//	                       {"v":1,"seq":N,"type":"hub","live":true} with the latest seq, then the stream.
//	ws://…/feed?types=auras,next   only those types
//	http://…/state         the current state as JSON lines
//	http://…/              a live view of the state in the browser
//
// After the "hub" line seq rises by one per line, so a client with no types
// filter that sees a gap knows it missed one. A client whose buffer fills is closed with
// 1008 "too slow" rather than slowing the feed. Browser pages may connect
// only from the hub's own origin or one matching -origin; -token, if set,
// must be passed as ?token=. When stdin ends, clients are closed with 1000
// "feed ended" and feedhub exits.
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	_ "embed"
	"errors"
	"flag"
	"io"
	"log"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/coder/websocket"
)

//go:embed viewer.html
var viewer []byte

func main() {
	addr := flag.String("ws", "127.0.0.1:7373", "where to listen")
	origins := flag.String("origin", "localhost:*,127.0.0.1:*", "comma-separated host patterns browser pages may connect from (besides the hub's own)")
	token := flag.String("token", "", "if set, clients must pass ?token=<this>")
	queue := flag.Int("queue", 4096, "lines buffered per client before it is dropped as too slow")
	quiet := flag.Bool("no-stdout", false, "do not pass lines through to stdout")
	flag.Parse()
	log.SetPrefix("feedhub: ")
	log.SetFlags(0)

	// a closed stdout (the overlay quit) is an error to report, not the end:
	// the socket keeps serving
	signal.Ignore(syscall.SIGPIPE)

	h := newHub(*queue)
	srv := &http.Server{Handler: handler(h, splitList(*origins), *token)}
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", *addr)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	log.Printf("serving ws://%s/feed (live view http://%s/)", ln.Addr(), ln.Addr())
	go func() {
		if err := srv.Serve(ln); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}()

	var out io.Writer = os.Stdout
	if *quiet {
		out = io.Discard
	}
	if err := pump(os.Stdin, out, h); err != nil {
		log.Print(err)
	}
	h.closeAll()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	_ = srv.Shutdown(ctx)
}

// pump copies stdin to out line by line (one write per line, so the next tool
// in the pipe sees each line as it comes) and publishes each line.
func pump(in io.Reader, out io.Writer, h *hub) error {
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(in)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 64<<10), 16<<20)
	stdoutOK := true
	for sc.Scan() {
		line := sc.Bytes()
		if stdoutOK {
			buf := make([]byte, len(line)+1)
			copy(buf, line)
			buf[len(line)] = '\n'
			if _, err := out.Write(buf); err != nil {
				// the reader went away (the overlay closed): keep serving the socket
				log.Printf("stdout: %v; serving the socket only", err)
				stdoutOK = false
			}
		}
		h.publish(append([]byte(nil), line...))
	}
	return sc.Err()
}

func handler(h *hub, origins []string, token string) http.Handler {
	authed := func(r *http.Request) bool { return token == "" || r.URL.Query().Get("token") == token }
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/feed", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if !authed(r) {
			http.Error(w, "bad token", http.StatusUnauthorized)
			return
		}
		conn, err := websocket.Accept(w, r, &websocket.AcceptOptions{OriginPatterns: origins})
		if err != nil {
			return // Accept has written the response
		}
		serve(r.Context(), conn, h, parseTypes(r.URL.Query().Get("types")))
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/state", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if !authed(r) {
			http.Error(w, "bad token", http.StatusUnauthorized)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/x-ndjson")
		types := parseTypes(r.URL.Query().Get("types"))
		for _, s := range h.snapshot() {
			if types == nil || types[s.typ] {
				w.Write(s.line)
				w.Write([]byte{'\n'})
			}
		}
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/{$}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
		w.Write(viewer)
	})
	return mux
}

// serve writes the client's lines to its socket until the feed ends, the
// client is dropped, or it goes away. Reads are discarded (CloseRead), which
// also notices the client closing.
func serve(ctx context.Context, conn *websocket.Conn, h *hub, types map[string]bool) {
	c := h.join(types)
	defer h.leave(c)
	ctx = conn.CloseRead(ctx)
	for {
		select {
		case line, ok := <-c.out:
			if !ok {
				conn.Close(websocket.StatusNormalClosure, "feed ended")
				return
			}
			wctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
			err := conn.Write(wctx, websocket.MessageText, line)
			cancel()
			if err != nil {
				conn.CloseNow()
				return
			}
		case <-c.gone:
			conn.Close(websocket.StatusPolicyViolation, "too slow")
			return
		case <-ctx.Done():
			conn.CloseNow()
			return
		}
	}
}

func parseTypes(s string) map[string]bool {
	list := splitList(s)
	if len(list) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	m := map[string]bool{}
	for _, t := range list {
		m[t] = true
	}
	return m
}

func splitList(s string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, p := range strings.Split(s, ",") {
		if p = strings.TrimSpace(p); p != "" {
			out = append(out, p)
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

```html
<script>
const cards = document.getElementById('cards'), evlist = document.getElementById('evlist');
const stat = document.getElementById('stat'), dot = document.getElementById('dot'), rate = document.getElementById('rate');
let lines = 0, lastSeq = null, gaps = 0, evTimes = [];

function el(tag, cls, text) { const e = document.createElement(tag); if (cls) e.className = cls; if (text != null) e.textContent = text; return e; }
function short(v) {
  if (v == null) return '';
  if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.map(x => typeof x === 'object' ? (x.name || x.spell || x.id || JSON.stringify(x)) : x).join(', ') || '(none)';
  if (typeof v === 'object') return JSON.stringify(v);
  return String(v);
}
// one row per item of the line's main list, or per field
function rows(m) {
  const list = m.queue || m.auras || m.cooldowns || m.powers;
  if (Array.isArray(list)) {
    if (!list.length) return [['(none)', '']];
    return list.map(x => [x.name || x.spell || x.id || '', Object.entries(x)
      .filter(([k]) => !['name', 'spell', 'id'].includes(k)).map(([k, v]) => k + ' ' + short(v)).join(' · ')]);
  }
  return Object.entries(m).filter(([k]) => !['v', 'seq', 'type', 'unit'].includes(k)).map(([k, v]) => [k, short(v)]);
}
function show(m) {
  const key = m.type + (m.unit ? '/' + m.unit : '');
  let card = document.getElementById('c-' + key);
  if (!card) {
    card = el('section', 'card'); card.id = 'c-' + key;
    cards.insertBefore(card, document.getElementById('events'));
  }
  card.replaceChildren();
  const h = el('h2', null, key); h.append(el('span', null, '#' + m.seq)); card.append(h);
  for (const [k, v] of rows(m)) { const r = el('div', 'row'); r.append(el('b', null, k), el('i', null, v)); card.append(r); }
}
function event(m) {
  const d = el('div', 'ev'); d.append(el('b', null, m.sub || 'event'), ' ' + [m.src_name || m.src, '→', m.dst_name || m.dst, m.spell_name || m.spell || '', m.amount ?? ''].filter(x => x !== '' && x != null).join(' '));
  evlist.prepend(d); while (evlist.childElementCount > 30) evlist.lastChild.remove();
  const now = performance.now(); evTimes.push(now); while (evTimes.length && now - evTimes[0] > 5000) evTimes.shift();
  rate.textContent = (evTimes.length / 5).toFixed(1) + '/s';
}
function connect() {
  const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('token');
  const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://${location.host}/feed` + (q ? '?token=' + encodeURIComponent(q) : ''));
  ws.onopen = () => { dot.classList.add('on'); lastSeq = null; };
  ws.onmessage = e => {
    const m = JSON.parse(e.data);
    if (m.type === 'hub') { lastSeq = m.seq; return; }
    lines++;
    if (lastSeq !== null) { if (m.seq > lastSeq + 1) gaps++; lastSeq = m.seq; }
    if (m.type === 'event') event(m); else show(m);
    stat.textContent = `${lines} lines · seq ${m.seq}` + (gaps ? ` · ${gaps} gaps` : '');
  };
  ws.onclose = e => { dot.classList.remove('on'); stat.textContent = `closed: ${e.reason || e.code} · retrying`; setTimeout(connect, 1500); };
}
connect();
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

`tools/worlddecrypt/main.go`:

```go
// Package main is worlddecrypt: the stock client's world connections,
// decrypted from a packet capture with the secrets tools/bnetrelay recorded.
//
// The world keys come from two Battle.net values (EVIDENCE E27, E34): the
// client secret the client puts in Param_ClientInfo, and Param_JoinSecret
// from the realm join. KeyData is client secret ‖ join secret; with the
// challenges each side sends in the clear (SMSG_AUTH_CHALLENGE's server
// challenge, CMSG_AUTH_SESSION's local challenge) that gives the session key
// and the GCM key (world.SessionKey, world.EncryptionKey). An instance
// connection (CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION) keys from the realm connection's
// session key and its own challenges. A frame's nonce is its index in its
// direction, cleartext frames included.
//
//	sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -U -w world.pcap 'tcp port 3724'   # while the client plays
//	go run ./tools/worlddecrypt -pcap world.pcap -secrets <relay run>/secrets.jsonl -out <dir>
//
// It writes <dir>/conn-<port>.jsonl per connection: every message with its
// time, direction, opcode, name and body in hex, compressed packets inflated.
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"compress/flate"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/framing"

)

// build names the opcodes; -build 70783 for a retail capture (no table yet: numbers only).
var build = 70755

func main() {
	pcap := flag.String("pcap", "", "tcpdump capture of the world port")
	secrets := flag.String("secrets", "", "bnetrelay's secrets.jsonl")
	out := flag.String("out", "", "output directory (default: next to the capture)")
	flag.IntVar(&build, "build", build, "client build the opcode names come from")
	flag.Parse()
	if *pcap == "" || *secrets == "" {
		log.Fatal("worlddecrypt: need -pcap and -secrets")
	}
	if *out == "" {
		*out = strings.TrimSuffix(*pcap, filepath.Ext(*pcap)) + "-decrypted"
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(*out, 0o700); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	clientSecrets, joinSecrets, err := readSecrets(*secrets)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	segs, err := readPcapng(*pcap)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	conns := assemble(segs)
	log.Printf("%d TCP connections; %d client secret(s), %d join secret(s)", len(conns), len(clientSecrets), len(joinSecrets))

	// Realm connections first: an instance connection needs their session key.
	sort.SliceStable(conns, func(i, j int) bool { return conns[i].start.Before(conns[j].start) })
	var sessionKeys [][]byte
	for pass := 0; pass < 2; pass++ {
		for _, c := range conns {
			if c.done {
				continue
			}
			if err := decrypt(c, clientSecrets, joinSecrets, &sessionKeys, *out); err != nil {
				if pass == 1 {
					log.Printf("port %d: %v", c.clientPort, err)
				}
				continue
			}
			c.done = true
		}
	}
}

func readSecrets(path string) (clients, joins [][]byte, err error) {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	secretRE := regexp.MustCompile(`"secret":\[([0-9, ]+)\]`)
	for _, line := range bytes.Split(raw, []byte("\n")) {
		if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		var r struct {
			ClientInfo string `json:"client_info"`
			JoinSecret string `json:"join_secret"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(line, &r); err != nil {
			return nil, nil, err
		}
		if m := secretRE.FindStringSubmatch(r.ClientInfo); m != nil {
			var b []byte
			for _, s := range strings.Split(m[1], ",") {
				var v int
				fmt.Sscan(strings.TrimSpace(s), &v)
				b = append(b, byte(v))
			}
			clients = append(clients, b)
		}
		if r.JoinSecret != "" {
			b, err := hex.DecodeString(r.JoinSecret)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, err
			}
			joins = append(joins, b)
		}
	}
	if len(clients) == 0 || len(joins) == 0 {
		return nil, nil, errors.New("secrets: need a client secret and a join secret")
	}
	return clients, joins, nil
}

// ---- pcapng and TCP ----

type segment struct {
	t            time.Time
	src, dst     string
	sport, dport uint16
	seq          uint32
	syn, fin     bool
	payload      []byte
}

func readPcapng(path string) ([]segment, error) {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var segs []segment
	var links []uint16
	le := binary.LittleEndian
	for p := 0; p+12 <= len(raw); {
		typ, blen := le.Uint32(raw[p:]), int(le.Uint32(raw[p+4:]))
		if blen < 12 || p+blen > len(raw) {
			break
		}
		b := raw[p+8 : p+blen-4]
		switch typ {
		case 1: // interface description
			links = append(links, le.Uint16(b))
		case 6: // enhanced packet
			iface := le.Uint32(b)
			ts := uint64(le.Uint32(b[4:]))<<32 | uint64(le.Uint32(b[8:]))
			capLen := int(le.Uint32(b[12:]))
			data := b[20 : 20+capLen]
			link := uint16(1)
			if int(iface) < len(links) {
				link = links[iface]
			}
			if s, ok := parsePacket(link, data); ok {
				s.t = time.UnixMicro(int64(ts))
				segs = append(segs, s)
			}
		}
		p += blen
	}
	if len(segs) == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("pcap: no TCP segments (is it pcapng?)")
	}
	return segs, nil
}

func parsePacket(link uint16, d []byte) (segment, bool) {
	var s segment
	switch link {
	case 258: // PKTAP: its own header, then the inner link
		if len(d) < 8 {
			return s, false
		}
		hl := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(d))
		inner := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(d[4:])
		if hl > len(d) {
			return s, false
		}
		return parsePacket(uint16(inner), d[hl:])
	case 1: // Ethernet
		if len(d) < 14 {
			return s, false
		}
		d = d[14:]
	case 0: // BSD loopback
		if len(d) < 4 {
			return s, false
		}
		d = d[4:]
	case 12, 101: // raw IP
	default:
		return s, false
	}
	if len(d) < 20 {
		return s, false
	}
	var tcp []byte
	switch d[0] >> 4 {
	case 4:
		ihl := int(d[0]&0xf) * 4
		total := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(d[2:]))
		if d[9] != 6 || total > len(d) || ihl > total {
			return s, false
		}
		s.src = fmt.Sprintf("%d.%d.%d.%d", d[12], d[13], d[14], d[15])
		s.dst = fmt.Sprintf("%d.%d.%d.%d", d[16], d[17], d[18], d[19])
		tcp = d[ihl:total]
	case 6:
		if len(d) < 40 || d[6] != 6 {
			return s, false
		}
		plen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(d[4:]))
		s.src, s.dst = hex.EncodeToString(d[8:24]), hex.EncodeToString(d[24:40])
		if 40+plen > len(d) {
			return s, false
		}
		tcp = d[40 : 40+plen]
	default:
		return s, false
	}
	if len(tcp) < 20 {
		return s, false
	}
	s.sport, s.dport = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(tcp), binary.BigEndian.Uint16(tcp[2:])
	s.seq = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(tcp[4:])
	off := int(tcp[12]>>4) * 4
	flags := tcp[13]
	s.syn, s.fin = flags&0x02 != 0, flags&0x01 != 0
	if off > len(tcp) {
		return s, false
	}
	s.payload = append([]byte(nil), tcp[off:]...)
	return s, true
}

type stream struct {
	isn     uint32
	haveISN bool
	parts   map[uint32][]byte // relative seq -> bytes
	times   map[uint32]time.Time
}

type conn struct {
	clientPort uint16
	server     string
	start      time.Time
	c2s, s2c   *stream
	done       bool
}

func assemble(segs []segment) []*conn {
	byKey := map[string]*conn{}
	var order []*conn
	for _, s := range segs {
		var c *conn
		var st **stream
		if s.dport == 3724 {
			key := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.dst, s.sport)
			if c = byKey[key]; c == nil {
				c = &conn{clientPort: s.sport, server: s.dst, start: s.t}
				byKey[key] = c
				order = append(order, c)
			}
			st = &c.c2s
		} else if s.sport == 3724 {
			key := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.src, s.dport)
			if c = byKey[key]; c == nil {
				c = &conn{clientPort: s.dport, server: s.src, start: s.t}
				byKey[key] = c
				order = append(order, c)
			}
			st = &c.s2c
		} else {
			continue
		}
		if *st == nil {
			*st = &stream{parts: map[uint32][]byte{}, times: map[uint32]time.Time{}}
		}
		x := *st
		if s.syn {
			x.isn, x.haveISN = s.seq+1, true
			continue
		}
		if !x.haveISN {
			// capture started mid-stream: take the first seen seq as the origin
			x.isn, x.haveISN = s.seq, true
		}
		if len(s.payload) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		rel := s.seq - x.isn
		if old, ok := x.parts[rel]; !ok || len(s.payload) > len(old) {
			x.parts[rel] = s.payload
			x.times[rel] = s.t
		}
	}
	return order
}

// bytes returns the stream in order, with the time each offset arrived.
func (x *stream) bytes() ([]byte, []int, []time.Time) {
	if x == nil {
		return nil, nil, nil
	}
	keys := make([]uint32, 0, len(x.parts))
	for k := range x.parts {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Slice(keys, func(i, j int) bool { return keys[i] < keys[j] })
	var out []byte
	var offs []int
	var ts []time.Time
	for _, k := range keys {
		p := x.parts[k]
		if int(k) > len(out) {
			log.Printf("gap of %d bytes at %d", int(k)-len(out), len(out))
			break
		}
		if int(k)+len(p) <= len(out) {
			continue
		}
		offs = append(offs, len(out))
		ts = append(ts, x.times[k])
		out = append(out, p[len(out)-int(k):]...)
	}
	return out, offs, ts
}

func timeAt(offs []int, ts []time.Time, pos int) time.Time {
	i := sort.Search(len(offs), func(i int) bool { return offs[i] > pos }) - 1
	if i < 0 {
		i = 0
	}
	if len(ts) == 0 {
		return time.Time{}
	}
	return ts[i]
}

// ---- world frames ----

type frame struct {
	t      time.Time
	tag    [framing.TagLen]byte
	clear  bool
	opcode uint32
	body   []byte // cleartext: the payload; encrypted: ciphertext (opcode included)
}

// frames splits one direction after its handshake line.
func frames(b []byte, offs []int, ts []time.Time) ([]frame, error) {
	nl := bytes.IndexByte(b, '\n')
	if nl < 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("no handshake line")
	}
	var fs []frame
	for p := nl + 1; p+4+framing.TagLen <= len(b); {
		size := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[p:]))
		if size < 4 || size > 1<<20 {
			return fs, fmt.Errorf("frame at %d: size %d", p, size)
		}
		end := p + 4 + framing.TagLen + size
		if end > len(b) {
			break
		}
		var f frame
		f.t = timeAt(offs, ts, p)
		copy(f.tag[:], b[p+4:])
		f.clear = f.tag == [framing.TagLen]byte{}
		payload := b[p+4+framing.TagLen : end]
		if f.clear {
			f.opcode = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(payload)
			f.body = payload[4:]
		} else {
			f.body = payload
		}
		fs = append(fs, f)
		p = end
	}
	return fs, nil
}

func name(dir opcodes.Direction, op uint32) string {
	if build == 70783 {
		// Retail 12.1.5.70783 has no table yet. Its opcodes look like Forever
		// 70755's with the group (high 16 bits) two lower: 0x4E000E
		// COMPRESSED_PACKET is 0x4C000E there, AUTH_SESSION 0x460001 is
		// 0x440001. Names found that way end in "~" (a guess, see RETAIL.md).
		if n := opcodes.DescribeBuild(70755, dir, op+0x20000); !strings.HasPrefix(n, "0x") {
			return n + "~"
		}
	}
	return opcodes.DescribeBuild(build, dir, op)
}

func decrypt(c *conn, clientSecrets, joinSecrets [][]byte, sessionKeys *[][]byte, outDir string) error {
	cb, coffs, cts := c.c2s.bytes()
	sb, soffs, sts := c.s2c.bytes()
	cf, err := frames(cb, coffs, cts)
	if err != nil && len(cf) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("client side: %w", err)
	}
	sf, err := frames(sb, soffs, sts)
	if err != nil && len(sf) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("server side: %w", err)
	}
	if len(cf) == 0 || len(sf) == 0 || !sf[0].clear || !cf[0].clear {
		return errors.New("no cleartext handshake")
	}
	if len(sf[0].body) < 64 {
		return errors.New("first server frame is not AUTH_CHALLENGE")
	}
	server := sf[0].body[32:64]
	first := name(opcodes.ClientToServer, cf[0].opcode)
	// Without a table for -build (retail 70783 moved even the auth opcodes),
	// tell the continued session by its fixed size.
	if len(cf[0].body) == world.AuthContinuedSessionLen {
		first = "CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION"
	}
	var keys [][world.EncryptionKeyLen]byte
	var sess [][]byte
	if strings.Contains(first, "CONTINUED") {
		a, err := world.DecodeAuthContinuedSession(cf[0].body)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if len(*sessionKeys) == 0 {
			return errors.New("instance connection before any realm connection decrypted")
		}
		for _, sk := range *sessionKeys {
			k, err := world.EncryptionKey(sk, a.LocalChallenge[:], server)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			keys, sess = append(keys, k), append(sess, sk)
		}
	} else {
		a, err := world.DecodeAuthSessionBody(cf[0].body)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", first, err)
		}
		for _, cs := range clientSecrets {
			for _, js := range joinSecrets {
				kd := append(append([]byte(nil), cs...), js...)
				sk, err := world.SessionKey(kd, a.LocalChallenge[:], server)
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				k, err := world.EncryptionKey(sk[:], a.LocalChallenge[:], server)
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				keys, sess = append(keys, k), append(sess, append([]byte(nil), sk[:]...))
			}
		}
	}
	// The right key opens the first encrypted server frame.
	for i, k := range keys {
		if out, ok := open(c, k, cf, sf); ok {
			if !strings.Contains(first, "CONTINUED") {
				*sessionKeys = append(*sessionKeys, sess[i])
			}
			return write(c, out, outDir)
		}
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("no key opens it (%d tried): not a session from these secrets", len(keys))
}

type msg struct {
	T      string `json:"t"`
	Dir    string `json:"dir"`
	Opcode string `json:"opcode"`
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Size   int    `json:"size"`
	Body   string `json:"body"`
	Note   string `json:"note,omitempty"`
}

func open(c *conn, key [world.EncryptionKeyLen]byte, cf, sf []frame) ([]msg, bool) {
	var out []msg
	ok := false
	for _, side := range []struct {
		fs  []frame
		dir world.Direction
		od  opcodes.Direction
		tag string
	}{{sf, world.Recv, opcodes.ServerToClient, "s2c"}, {cf, world.Send, opcodes.ClientToServer, "c2s"}} {
		inf := newInflater()
		for i, f := range side.fs {
			op, body := f.opcode, f.body
			note := ""
			if !f.clear {
				// world.Recv/Send are the client's own view: it receives SRVR.
				ci, err := world.NewCipherAt(key[:], side.dir, uint64(i))
				if err != nil {
					return nil, false
				}
				plain, err := ci.Open(nil, f.body, f.tag[:])
				if err != nil {
					if side.tag == "s2c" && !ok {
						return nil, false
					}
					note = "decrypt failed"
					out = append(out, msg{T: f.t.Format("15:04:05.000"), Dir: side.tag, Size: len(f.body), Note: note})
					continue
				}
				ok = true
				op, body = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(plain), plain[4:]
			}
			t := f.t.Format("15:04:05.000")
			var expand func(op uint32, body []byte, note string, depth int)
			expand = func(op uint32, body []byte, note string, depth int) {
				n := name(side.od, op)
				switch {
				case depth < 3 && strings.Contains(n, "COMPRESSED_PACKET") && len(body) >= 12:
					plain, err := inf.inflate(body)
					if err == nil && len(plain) >= 4 {
						expand(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(plain), plain[4:], strings.TrimPrefix(note+" inflated", " "), depth+1)
						return
					}
					note = fmt.Sprintf("inflate: %v", err)
				case depth < 3 && strings.Contains(n, "MULTIPLE_PACKETS"):
					// u16 size, u32 opcode, payload, repeated (session.handleMultiple)
					b := body
					for len(b) >= 6 {
						sz := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b))
						if len(b) < 6+sz {
							break
						}
						expand(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[2:]), b[6:6+sz], strings.TrimPrefix(note+" multiple", " "), depth+1)
						b = b[6+sz:]
					}
					if len(b) == 0 {
						return
					}
					note += fmt.Sprintf(" (%d bytes left unsplit)", len(b))
				}
				out = append(out, msg{T: t, Dir: side.tag, Opcode: fmt.Sprintf("%#08x", op), Name: n, Size: len(body), Body: hex.EncodeToString(body), Note: note})
			}
			expand(op, body, note, 0)
		}
	}
	sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].T < out[j].T })
	return out, ok
}

func write(c *conn, out []msg, dir string) error {
	path := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("conn-%d.jsonl", c.clientPort))
	f, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	enc := json.NewEncoder(f)
	fails := 0
	for _, m := range out {
		if m.Note == "decrypt failed" {
			fails++
		}
		_ = enc.Encode(m)
	}
	log.Printf("port %d (%s): %d messages decrypted, %d failed -> %s", c.clientPort, c.server, len(out)-fails, fails, path)
	return nil
}

// inflater is one connection direction's persistent raw-deflate stream
// (SMSG_COMPRESSED_PACKET: u32 size, u32 plain adler, u32 compressed adler,
// deflate bytes).
type inflater struct {
	feed *feeder
	r    io.ReadCloser
}

type feeder struct{ buf []byte }

func (f *feeder) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if len(f.buf) == 0 {
		return 0, io.ErrNoProgress
	}
	n := copy(p, f.buf)
	f.buf = f.buf[n:]
	return n, nil
}

func (f *feeder) ReadByte() (byte, error) {
	if len(f.buf) == 0 {
		return 0, io.ErrNoProgress
	}
	b := f.buf[0]
	f.buf = f.buf[1:]
	return b, nil
}

func newInflater() *inflater {
	fd := &feeder{}
	return &inflater{feed: fd, r: flate.NewReader(fd)}
}

func (in *inflater) inflate(body []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	size := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body)
	if size > 1<<20 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("claims %d bytes", size)
	}
	in.feed.buf = append(in.feed.buf, body[12:]...)
	plain := make([]byte, size)
	_, err := io.ReadFull(in.r, plain)
	return plain, err
}
```

`transport/tcp/tcp.go`:

```go
// Package tcp is the plain-stream transport: TCP with Nagle disabled.
//
// This is the route a fallback connection takes and the one the TrinityCore
// "forever" fork speaks, so it is also the route a recorded fixture replays.
// It is a plain stream, so the connection uses the tagged frame layout
// (docs/EVIDENCE.md E15).
package tcp

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"time"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/transport"
)

// Dialer dials TCP. The zero value is usable.
type Dialer struct {
	// KeepAlive is the period of TCP keep-alive probes; zero uses the OS
	// default and a negative value disables them.
	KeepAlive time.Duration
}

// Dial implements transport.Dialer.
func (d Dialer) Dial(ctx context.Context, t transport.Target) (transport.Conn, error) {
	if t.Route != "" && t.Route != transport.RouteTCP {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", transport.ErrNoRoute, t.Route)
	}
	var nd net.Dialer
	if d.KeepAlive != 0 {
		if d.KeepAlive < 0 {
			nd.KeepAlive = -1
		} else {
			nd.KeepAlive = d.KeepAlive
		}
	}
	c, err := nd.DialContext(ctx, "tcp", t.Address)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if tc, ok := c.(*net.TCPConn); ok {
		// The client disables Nagle on game sockets; per-message latency
		// matters more than packing.
		_ = tc.SetNoDelay(true)
	}
	return &conn{c: c}, nil
}

type conn struct {
	c      net.Conn
	closed bool
}

func (c *conn) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := c.c.Read(p)
	if err != nil && errors.Is(err, net.ErrClosed) {
		return n, transport.ErrClosed
	}
	return n, err
}

func (c *conn) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := c.c.Write(p)
	if err != nil && errors.Is(err, net.ErrClosed) {
		return n, transport.ErrClosed
	}
	return n, err
}

func (c *conn) Close() error {
	if c.closed {
		return nil
	}
	c.closed = true
	return c.c.Close()
}

func (c *conn) Describe() string { return "tcp " + c.c.RemoteAddr().String() }

func (c *conn) SetDeadline(t time.Time) error { return c.c.SetDeadline(t) }

var _ io.ReadWriteCloser = (*conn)(nil)

```

`transport/transport.go`:

```go
// Package transport is the only thing in the tree that touches a socket.
//
// A transport carries bytes and nothing else: it never sees an opcode, a
// message or a handshake line. Everything above it (framing, auth, dispatch)
// works through Conn, so a QUIC, TCP or BLEEP route is interchangeable and a
// recorded route can be replayed in a test.
//
// The client itself prefers QUIC and falls back to TCP
// (docs/EVIDENCE.md E4/E7: `maximumConnectionAttempts`
// "Maximum number of times to try to connect to a server using QUIC before
// doing TCP"). Only TCP is implemented; QUIC is a separate Dialer.
package transport

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"time"
)

// Route names the way a connection was made. Diagnostics and captures record
// it, because the frame layout depends on the transport (EVIDENCE.md E15).
type Route string

// Known routes.
const (
	RouteTCP   Route = "tcp"
	RouteQUIC  Route = "quic"
	RouteBLEEP Route = "bleep"
)

// Target is what to dial. Address is host:port; Host is kept separately because
// QUIC needs it for SNI and certificate checks.
type Target struct {
	Address string
	Host    string
	Route   Route
}

// Dialer opens a connection.
type Dialer interface {
	Dial(ctx context.Context, t Target) (Conn, error)
}

// Conn is one reliable byte stream.
//
// Implementations may fail with ErrClosed after Close; a second Close is a
// no-op. Deadlines are per call, as on net.Conn, and are cleared by a zero
// time.
type Conn interface {
	Read(p []byte) (int, error)
	Write(p []byte) (int, error)
	Close() error
	// Describe returns a short, log-safe description, e.g. "tcp 1.2.3.4:1119".
	Describe() string
	// SetDeadline bounds the whole connection (handshake and idle reads).
	SetDeadline(t time.Time) error
}

var (
	// ErrClosed is returned once the connection is closed.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("transport: connection closed")
	// ErrNoRoute means the dialer cannot serve the target's route.
	ErrNoRoute = errors.New("transport: unsupported route")
)

```

`world/auth.go`:

```go
// Package world is the world-connection protocol that sits above transport:
// the handshake line pair, the frame stream, the auth exchange, the cipher and
// the dispatch loop.
//
// Everything here is read off the client's own code for build 1.60.1.70707
// (addresses in the comments, write-up in research/encryption.md and
// docs/EVIDENCE.md E15/E18) and cross-checked byte-for-byte against the
// TrinityCore "forever" fork's server side, which agrees on the layout, the
// constants and the challenge orderings.
package world

import (
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"crypto/sha512"
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"hash"
	"math/bits"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/codec"
)

// Sizes of the auth material. The names follow the client's own field offsets
// (connAuth and the NetClient above it, research/encryption.md §3).
const (
	// KeyDataLen is the Battle.net session-key material delivered with the
	// realm-join ticket (client +0x08, 64 bytes).
	KeyDataLen = 64
	// BuildKeyLen is the per-build auth key folded into the digest.
	BuildKeyLen = 16
	// ChallengeLen is the length of both the local and the server challenge.
	ChallengeLen = 32
	// DigestLen is how much of the auth digest is sent.
	DigestLen = 24
	// SessionKeyLen is the length of the derived session key.
	SessionKeyLen = 40
	// EncryptionKeyLen is the length of the GCM key.
	EncryptionKeyLen = 32
)

// ForeverBuildAuthKey is the 16-byte per-build auth key for wowf 1.60.1.70707,
// folded into the AUTH_SESSION digest (see AuthDigest). It is not in the
// shipped file: the client builds it at runtime in an obfuscated, anti-tamper
// provider (installed through the BSS cell 0x104083778, EVIDENCE.md E22/E28).
// Recovered by reading that provider out of a live process and resolving its
// four movz/movk/add/eor word builds — static and live agree
// (docs/EVIDENCE.md E28, /tmp/wowkey/live). The value belongs to the build, not
// to any account.
var ForeverBuildAuthKey = [BuildKeyLen]byte{
	0xb4, 0x51, 0x5b, 0x53, 0x1d, 0xd2, 0x21, 0x3c,
	0xaf, 0x4f, 0x3b, 0xd2, 0x77, 0xe1, 0x4b, 0x8f,
}

// BuildAuthKey70755 is the per-build auth key for wowf 1.60.1.70755. Its
// provider is 0x102c9797c (installed by 0x102c96f0c, the same
// `mov w0,'WoW'; bl; adrp x0,provider; bl` site as 70707's 0x102c95f08). Read
// statically from the decrypted 70755 image: the four words are
// 0x9b4f1c7f-0x165, (0xea145245^0x9c5)+0x8d2, ((0x2d44be0e-0x49d)^0x1103)+0x17e
// and ((0x7653670a-0x883)+0xc9f)^0x202 (the last behind the same return-address
// gate). The same hand reading of 70707's provider reproduces
// ForeverBuildAuthKey exactly, and a Unicorn run of the 70755 bytes gives the
// first two words; it has not been seen in a live 70755 process
// (docs/EVIDENCE.md E31).
var BuildAuthKey70755 = [BuildKeyLen]byte{
	0x1a, 0x1b, 0x4f, 0x9b, 0x52, 0x64, 0x14, 0xea,
	0xf0, 0xa9, 0x44, 0x2d, 0x24, 0x69, 0x53, 0x76,
}

// BuildAuthKey returns the auth key of a known build.
func BuildAuthKey(build int) ([BuildKeyLen]byte, bool) {
	switch build {
	case 70707:
		return ForeverBuildAuthKey, true
	case 70755:
		return BuildAuthKey70755, true
	}
	return [BuildKeyLen]byte{}, false
}

// Seeds, byte-identical to the client's __const and to the fork's constants.
// The client VAs are the second source: 0x10319cc20, 0x10319cc40, 0x10319cc60,
// 0x10319cc80, 0x10319cca0 (research/encryption.md §3).
var (
	authCheckSeed = []byte{
		0xDE, 0x3A, 0x2A, 0x8E, 0x6B, 0x89, 0x52, 0x66, 0x88, 0x9D, 0x7E, 0x7A, 0x77, 0x1D, 0x5D, 0x1F,
		0x4E, 0xD9, 0x0C, 0x23, 0x9B, 0xCD, 0x0E, 0xDC, 0xD2, 0xE8, 0x04, 0x3A, 0x68, 0x64, 0xC7, 0xB0,
	}
	continuedSessionSeed = []byte{
		0x56, 0x5C, 0x61, 0x9C, 0x48, 0x3A, 0x52, 0x1F, 0x61, 0x5D, 0x05, 0x49, 0xB2, 0x9A, 0x39, 0xBF,
		0x4B, 0x97, 0xB0, 0x1B, 0xF9, 0x6C, 0xDE, 0xD6, 0x80, 0x1D, 0xAB, 0x26, 0x02, 0xA9, 0x9B, 0x9D,
	}
	sessionKeySeed = []byte{
		0xE8, 0x1E, 0x8B, 0x59, 0x27, 0x62, 0x1E, 0xAA, 0x86, 0x15, 0x18, 0xEA, 0xC0, 0xBF, 0x66, 0x8C,
		0x6D, 0xBF, 0x83, 0x93, 0xBC, 0xAA, 0x80, 0x52, 0x5B, 0x1E, 0xDC, 0x23, 0xA0, 0x12, 0xB7, 0x50,
	}
	encryptionKeySeed = []byte{
		0x71, 0xC9, 0xED, 0x5A, 0xA7, 0x0E, 0x4D, 0xFF, 0x4C, 0x36, 0xA6, 0x5A, 0x3E, 0x46, 0x8A, 0x4A,
		0x5D, 0xA1, 0x48, 0xC8, 0x30, 0x47, 0x4A, 0xDE, 0xF6, 0x0D, 0x6C, 0xBE, 0x6F, 0xE4, 0x55, 0x73,
	}
	// enableEncryptionSeed keys the HMAC over the ENTER_ENCRYPTED_MODE
	// signature payload (0x10319cca0).
	enableEncryptionSeed = []byte{
		0x66, 0xBE, 0x29, 0x79, 0xEF, 0xF2, 0xD5, 0xB5, 0x61, 0x53, 0xF6, 0x5F, 0x45, 0xAE, 0x81, 0xCB,
		0x32, 0xEC, 0x94, 0xEC, 0x75, 0xB3, 0x5F, 0x44, 0x6A, 0x63, 0x43, 0x67, 0x17, 0x20, 0x44, 0x34,
	}
	// EnableEncryptionContext is the 16-byte ed25519ctx context (0x10319cc10).
	EnableEncryptionContext = []byte{
		0xA7, 0x1F, 0xB6, 0x9B, 0xC9, 0x7C, 0xDD, 0x96, 0xE9, 0xBB, 0xB8, 0x21, 0x39, 0x8D, 0x5A, 0xD4,
	}
)

// Auth material sizes that do not fit the const block above.
var (
	// ErrDoSUnsolved means the hashcash search hit its nonce cap.
	ErrDoSUnsolved = errors.New("world: DoS proof not found")
	// ErrBadZeroBits means the server asked for more zero bits than the client
	// supports (it caps at 48).
	ErrBadZeroBits = errors.New("world: DoS zero bits above 48")
)

func hmacSHA512(key, msg []byte) []byte {
	m := hmac.New(sha512.New, key)
	m.Write(msg)
	return m.Sum(nil)
}

// AuthDigest is the 24-byte digest of CMSG_AUTH_SESSION (client 0x1014b6730):
//
//	HMAC-SHA512(SHA512(KeyData ‖ buildKey), LocalChallenge ‖ ServerChallenge ‖ AuthCheckSeed)[0..24)
//
// buildKey may be nil, in which case it is left out of the hash input; the
// client always passes it, and a nil value only exists for a server that skips
// the check.
func AuthDigest(keyData []byte, buildKey []byte, local, server []byte) ([DigestLen]byte, error) {
	var out [DigestLen]byte
	if len(keyData) != KeyDataLen || len(local) != ChallengeLen || len(server) != ChallengeLen {
		return out, errors.New("world: bad digest input size")
	}
	if buildKey != nil && len(buildKey) != BuildKeyLen {
		return out, errors.New("world: bad build key size")
	}
	inner := sha512.New()
	inner.Write(keyData)
	if buildKey != nil {
		inner.Write(buildKey)
	}
	msg := make([]byte, 0, 2*ChallengeLen+len(authCheckSeed))
	msg = append(msg, local...)
	msg = append(msg, server...)
	msg = append(msg, authCheckSeed...)
	copy(out[:], hmacSHA512(inner.Sum(nil), msg))
	return out, nil
}

// sessionKeyGenerator is the fork's SessionKeyGenerator<SHA512>, inlined
// (client 0x1014b6d98): split the seed, hash each half, then iterate
// SHA512(o1 ‖ o0 ‖ o2) until enough bytes exist.
//
// The first o0 is SHA512(o1 ‖ 0 × 64 ‖ o2), not SHA512(seed): the generator
// starts its state at all zeroes and hashes it with the two halves before the
// first output byte (SessionKeyGenerator.h, `o0 = Hash::GetDigestOf(o1, o0, o2)`
// with `o0 = {}`).
func sessionKeyGenerator(seed []byte, n int) []byte {
	half := len(seed) / 2
	o1 := sha512.Sum512(seed[:half])
	o2 := sha512.Sum512(seed[half:])
	buf := make([]byte, 0, n)
	cur := make([]byte, sha512.Size) // all zeroes: the first o0
	for len(buf) < n {
		h := sha512.New()
		h.Write(o1[:])
		h.Write(cur)
		h.Write(o2[:])
		cur = h.Sum(cur[:0])
		buf = append(buf, cur...)
	}
	return buf[:n]
}

// SessionKey derives the 40-byte session key (client 0x1014b6b70). Note the
// challenge order: server first.
func SessionKey(keyData, local, server []byte) ([SessionKeyLen]byte, error) {
	var out [SessionKeyLen]byte
	if len(keyData) != KeyDataLen || len(local) != ChallengeLen || len(server) != ChallengeLen {
		return out, errors.New("world: bad session key input size")
	}
	inner := sha512.Sum512(keyData)
	msg := make([]byte, 0, 2*ChallengeLen+len(sessionKeySeed))
	msg = append(msg, server...)
	msg = append(msg, local...)
	msg = append(msg, sessionKeySeed...)
	copy(out[:], sessionKeyGenerator(hmacSHA512(inner[:], msg), SessionKeyLen))
	return out, nil
}

// EncryptionKey derives the 32-byte GCM key from the session key (client
// 0x1014b706c). The session key is the HMAC key and the challenge order is
// local first.
func EncryptionKey(sessionKey, local, server []byte) ([EncryptionKeyLen]byte, error) {
	var out [EncryptionKeyLen]byte
	if len(sessionKey) != SessionKeyLen || len(local) != ChallengeLen || len(server) != ChallengeLen {
		return out, errors.New("world: bad encryption key input size")
	}
	msg := make([]byte, 0, 2*ChallengeLen+len(encryptionKeySeed))
	msg = append(msg, local...)
	msg = append(msg, server...)
	msg = append(msg, encryptionKeySeed...)
	copy(out[:], hmacSHA512(sessionKey, msg))
	return out, nil
}

// doSZeroBits counts leading zero bits of h the way the client does
// (0x10109b530): whole zero bytes, then the trailing zero bits of the first
// non-zero byte, i.e. counting up from the low bit of byte 0.
func doSZeroBits(h []byte) int {
	n := 0
	for _, b := range h {
		if b == 0 {
			n += 8
			continue
		}
		return n + bits.TrailingZeros8(b)
	}
	return n
}

// DoSProof solves the auth hashcash (client 0x10109b530): the nonce is the
// lowest value whose SHA-256 over
//
//	LocalChallenge ‖ ServerChallenge ‖ Digest ‖ DosChallenge ‖ uint64le(nonce)
//
// has at least zeroBits leading zero bits. digest may be replaced by the
// 40-byte session key for a continued session.
//
// maxNonce bounds the search; pass 0 for "until found".
func DoSProof(local, server, digest, dosChallenge []byte, zeroBits uint8, maxNonce uint64) (uint64, error) {
	if zeroBits > 48 {
		return 0, ErrBadZeroBits
	}
	h := sha256.New()
	nonceBuf := make([]byte, 8)
	for nonce := uint64(0); maxNonce == 0 || nonce < maxNonce; nonce++ {
		h.Reset()
		h.Write(local)
		h.Write(server)
		h.Write(digest)
		h.Write(dosChallenge)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(nonceBuf, nonce)
		h.Write(nonceBuf)
		if doSZeroBits(h.Sum(nil)) >= int(zeroBits) {
			return nonce, nil
		}
	}
	return 0, ErrDoSUnsolved
}

// DoSCheck verifies a DoS nonce against the same preimage DoSProof searches.
// A server lets a handful of attempts through per nonce, so callers normally
// accept nonce or nonce+1 ... on the same challenge.
func DoSCheck(local, server, digest, dosChallenge []byte, nonce uint64, zeroBits uint8) (bool, error) {
	if zeroBits > 48 {
		return false, ErrBadZeroBits
	}
	h := sha256.New()
	h.Write(local)
	h.Write(server)
	h.Write(digest)
	h.Write(dosChallenge)
	var nb [8]byte
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(nb[:], nonce)
	h.Write(nb[:])
	return doSZeroBits(h.Sum(nil)) >= int(zeroBits), nil
}

// AuthSession is CMSG_AUTH_SESSION (opcode 0x460001), in the client's writer
// order (0x100731a98 / 0x100731af4).
type AuthSession struct {
	DosResponse    uint64
	RegionID       uint32
	BattlegroupID  uint32
	RealmID        uint32
	LocalChallenge [ChallengeLen]byte
	Digest         [DigestLen]byte
	UseIPv6        bool
	Ticket         []byte
}

// Encode serializes the message body, opcode included.
func (a *AuthSession) Encode(opcode uint32) []byte {
	w := codec.NewWriterCap(24 + 8 + 4 + 4 + 4 + ChallengeLen + DigestLen + 4 + len(a.Ticket))
	w.Uint32(opcode)
	w.Uint64(a.DosResponse)
	w.Uint32(a.RegionID)
	w.Uint32(a.BattlegroupID)
	w.Uint32(a.RealmID)
	w.RawBytes(a.LocalChallenge[:])
	w.RawBytes(a.Digest[:])
	w.Bit(a.UseIPv6)
	w.FlushBits()
	w.Uint32(uint32(len(a.Ticket)))
	w.RawBytes(a.Ticket)
	return w.Bytes()
}

// DecodeAuthSessionBody parses a CMSG_AUTH_SESSION body (opcode already
// stripped) back into its fields. It is the inverse of Encode minus the
// leading opcode, so a recorded real-client packet and ours can be compared
// field by field (see replay fingerprinting).
func DecodeAuthSessionBody(body []byte) (AuthSession, error) {
	var a AuthSession
	r := codec.NewReader(body)
	var err error
	if a.DosResponse, err = r.Uint64(); err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	if a.RegionID, err = r.Uint32(); err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	if a.BattlegroupID, err = r.Uint32(); err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	if a.RealmID, err = r.Uint32(); err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	lc, err := r.Bytes(ChallengeLen)
	if err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	copy(a.LocalChallenge[:], lc)
	dg, err := r.Bytes(DigestLen)
	if err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	copy(a.Digest[:], dg)
	bit, err := r.Bit()
	if err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	a.UseIPv6 = bit
	r.ResetBits()
	n, err := r.Uint32()
	if err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	if a.Ticket, err = r.Bytes(int(n)); err != nil {
		return a, err
	}
	return a, nil
}

// AuthContinuedSessionLen is the CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION body size.
const AuthContinuedSessionLen = 8 + ChallengeLen + DigestLen + 8 + 4 + 4

// AuthContinuedSession is CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION (opcode 0x460003), the
// auth message of a connection the server asked for with SMSG_CONNECT_TO. It
// is 80 bytes, in the fork's AuthContinuedSession::Read order and the real
// client's (capture 2026-11-04-goldshire-70755 #192): the hashcash nonce, the
// local challenge, the 24-byte digest, then Key, NativeRealmAddress and Key3
// copied from SMSG_CONNECT_TO. There is no ticket: the server finds the
// session key by the account id inside Key.
type AuthContinuedSession struct {
	DosResponse        uint64
	LocalChallenge     [ChallengeLen]byte
	Digest             [DigestLen]byte
	Key                uint64
	NativeRealmAddress uint32
	Key3               uint32
}

// Encode serializes the message body, opcode included.
func (a *AuthContinuedSession) Encode(opcode uint32) []byte {
	w := codec.NewWriterCap(4 + AuthContinuedSessionLen)
	w.Uint32(opcode)
	w.Uint64(a.DosResponse)
	w.RawBytes(a.LocalChallenge[:])
	w.RawBytes(a.Digest[:])
	w.Uint64(a.Key)
	w.Uint32(a.NativeRealmAddress)
	w.Uint32(a.Key3)
	return w.Bytes()
}

// DecodeAuthContinuedSession parses the body (no opcode).
func DecodeAuthContinuedSession(body []byte) (AuthContinuedSession, error) {
	var a AuthContinuedSession
	if len(body) != AuthContinuedSessionLen {
		return a, fmt.Errorf("world: AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION is %d bytes, want %d", len(body), AuthContinuedSessionLen)
	}
	a.DosResponse = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(body)
	copy(a.LocalChallenge[:], body[8:])
	copy(a.Digest[:], body[8+ChallengeLen:])
	o := 8 + ChallengeLen + DigestLen
	a.Key = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(body[o:])
	a.NativeRealmAddress = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[o+8:])
	a.Key3 = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[o+12:])
	return a, nil
}

// ContinuedSessionDigest is the continued-session variant of AuthDigest
// (client 0x1014b69ac): the session key is the HMAC key and the 8-byte
// reconnection key leads the message.
func ContinuedSessionDigest(sessionKey []byte, key uint64, local, server []byte) ([DigestLen]byte, error) {
	var out [DigestLen]byte
	if len(sessionKey) != SessionKeyLen || len(local) != ChallengeLen || len(server) != ChallengeLen {
		return out, errors.New("world: bad continued digest input size")
	}
	msg := make([]byte, 0, 8+2*ChallengeLen+len(continuedSessionSeed))
	var kb [8]byte
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(kb[:], key)
	msg = append(msg, kb[:]...)
	msg = append(msg, local...)
	msg = append(msg, server...)
	msg = append(msg, continuedSessionSeed...)
	copy(out[:], hmacSHA512(sessionKey, msg))
	return out, nil
}

// EnableEncryptionMessage is the payload the server signs: HMAC-SHA512 over
// one enabled byte and the seed (client 0x1014b7218).
func EnableEncryptionMessage(encryptKey []byte, enabled bool) []byte {
	b := byte(0)
	if enabled {
		b = 1
	}
	msg := make([]byte, 0, 1+len(enableEncryptionSeed))
	msg = append(msg, b)
	msg = append(msg, enableEncryptionSeed...)
	return hmacSHA512(encryptKey, msg)
}

// VerifyEnterEncryptedMode checks a SMSG_ENTER_ENCRYPTED_MODE signature with
// the shipped verifier. verify is the ed25519ctx verify function, injected so
// the package needs no key store.
//
// The client verifies an ed25519ctx signature with EnableEncryptionContext over
// EnableEncryptionMessage and tears the connection down on mismatch
// (0x1014b738c).
func VerifyEnterEncryptedMode(verify func(pub, msg, sig, ctx []byte) bool, pub []byte, signed []byte, sig []byte, enabled bool) bool {
	if len(pub) != 32 || len(sig) != 64 {
		return false
	}
	return verify(pub, EnableEncryptionMessage(signed, enabled), sig, EnableEncryptionContext)
}

// hashFn is exported for tests that want to assert the primitives directly.
func hashFn() hash.Hash { return sha512.New() }

```

`world/auth_test.go`:

```go
package world

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/hex"
	"testing"
)

// The vectors below are produced by an independent implementation (Python
// hashlib/hmac, /tmp/ref.py) from fixed inputs, so a mistake in the Go port
// shows up as a diff instead of agreeing with itself.
var (
	vectorKeyData = func() []byte {
		b := make([]byte, KeyDataLen)
		for i := range b {
			b[i] = byte(i)
		}
		return b
	}()
	vectorBuild = func() []byte {
		b := make([]byte, BuildKeyLen)
		for i := range b {
			b[i] = byte(i + 0x10)
		}
		return b
	}()
	vectorLocal  = bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xAA}, ChallengeLen)
	vectorServer = bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xBB}, ChallengeLen)
	vectorDos    = bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x11}, 32)
)

func TestAuthDigestVector(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := AuthDigest(vectorKeyData, vectorBuild, vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want, _ := hex.DecodeString("59e8bb8e6d10ad8c33665c8c5df1fb99fd7fff857340c444")
	if !bytes.Equal(got[:], want) {
		t.Fatalf("digest = %x, want %x", got, want)
	}
}

func TestAuthDigestWithoutBuildKey(t *testing.T) {
	with, err := AuthDigest(vectorKeyData, vectorBuild, vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	without, err := AuthDigest(vectorKeyData, nil, vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if with == without {
		t.Fatal("build key did not change the digest")
	}
}

func TestSessionKeyVector(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := SessionKey(vectorKeyData, vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// The generator starts its state at 64 zero bytes (SessionKeyGenerator.h,
	// `o0 = {}`), not at SHA512(seed): regenerated from that reference after a
	// live session proved the old vectors wrong (E34).
	want, _ := hex.DecodeString("604277d03b95fda426bcca8881d5f869a46b2c4bf118fe76816b7d5767480e714171a996fa6c227d")
	if !bytes.Equal(got[:], want) {
		t.Fatalf("session key = %x, want %x", got, want)
	}
}

func TestEncryptionKeyVector(t *testing.T) {
	session, err := SessionKey(vectorKeyData, vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, err := EncryptionKey(session[:], vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want, _ := hex.DecodeString("d63f405554a41413f331925920812695371bfdc145e771c30bdf9513b7b74296")
	if !bytes.Equal(got[:], want) {
		t.Fatalf("encryption key = %x, want %x", got, want)
	}
}

func TestDoSProofVector(t *testing.T) {
	digest, err := AuthDigest(vectorKeyData, vectorBuild, vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	nonce, err := DoSProof(vectorLocal, vectorServer, digest[:], vectorDos, 8, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if nonce != 180 {
		t.Fatalf("nonce = %d, want 180", nonce)
	}
}

func TestDoSZeroBitsCountsFromLowBit(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		h    []byte
		want int
	}{
		{[]byte{0x01}, 0},
		{[]byte{0x02}, 1},
		{[]byte{0x80}, 7},
		{[]byte{0x00, 0x01}, 8},
		{[]byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x10}, 36},
		{[]byte{0, 0, 0}, 24},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := doSZeroBits(c.h); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("doSZeroBits(%x) = %d, want %d", c.h, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestDoSProofRejectsTooManyZeroBits(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := DoSProof(vectorLocal, vectorServer, vectorDos, vectorDos, 49, 1); err != ErrBadZeroBits {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want ErrBadZeroBits", err)
	}
}

func TestAuthSessionEncoding(t *testing.T) {
	a := AuthSession{
		DosResponse:   0x1122334455667788,
		RegionID:      1,
		BattlegroupID: 2,
		RealmID:       3,
		UseIPv6:       true,
		Ticket:        []byte("ticket"),
	}
	copy(a.LocalChallenge[:], bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xCC}, ChallengeLen))
	copy(a.Digest[:], bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xDD}, DigestLen))
	b := a.Encode(0x460001)

	want := []byte{
		0x01, 0x00, 0x46, 0x00, // opcode
		0x88, 0x77, 0x66, 0x55, 0x44, 0x33, 0x22, 0x11, // DoS response, LE
		0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // region
		0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // battlegroup
		0x03, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // realm
	}
	want = append(want, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xCC}, ChallengeLen)...)
	want = append(want, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xDD}, DigestLen)...)
	want = append(want, 0x80)          // one bit UseIPv6, flushed as its own byte
	want = append(want, 0x06, 0, 0, 0) // ticket length
	want = append(want, "ticket"...)   // ticket
	if !bytes.Equal(b, want) {
		t.Fatalf("encoding\n got %x\nwant %x", b, want)
	}
}

func TestContinuedSessionDigestDiffersFromAuthDigest(t *testing.T) {

func TestEnableEncryptionMessageSignsTheFlag(t *testing.T) {
	key := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x42}, EncryptionKeyLen)

	off := EnableEncryptionMessage(key, false)
	if len(on) != 64 || bytes.Equal(on, off) {
		t.Fatalf("enabled flag did not change the signed message (len %d)", len(on))
	}

		t.Fatal("only the first byte should differ")
	}
}

func TestVerifyEnterEncryptedModeChecksLengths(t *testing.T) {
	called := false
	verify := func(pub, msg, sig, ctx []byte) bool { called = true; return true }
	if VerifyEnterEncryptedMode(verify, make([]byte, 31), nil, make([]byte, 64), true) {
		t.Fatal("31-byte public key accepted")
	}
	if called {
		t.Fatal("verifier called with a short key")
	}
	if !VerifyEnterEncryptedMode(verify, make([]byte, 32), nil, make([]byte, 64), true) {
		t.Fatal("valid lengths rejected")
	}
}

func TestDoSCheckMatchesProof(t *testing.T) {
	digest, err := AuthDigest(vectorKeyData, vectorBuild, vectorLocal, vectorServer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	nonce, err := DoSProof(vectorLocal, vectorServer, digest[:], vectorDos, 8, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ok, err := DoSCheck(vectorLocal, vectorServer, digest[:], vectorDos, nonce, 8)
	if err != nil || !ok {
		t.Fatalf("check rejected the proof: %v %v", ok, err)
	}
	if ok, _ := DoSCheck(vectorLocal, vectorServer, digest[:], vectorDos, nonce+1, 8); ok {
		t.Log("nonce+1 also passes (allowed, servers try a few)")
	}
	if ok, _ := DoSCheck(vectorLocal, vectorServer, digest[:], vectorDos, 0, 30); ok {
		t.Fatal("nonce 0 accepted for 30 zero bits")
	}
}

	}

	}
}
```

`world/connectto.go`:

```go
package world

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/codec"
)

// ConnectTo serials (the fork's ConnectToSerial). A failed dial is reported
// with CMSG_CONNECT_TO_FAILED carrying the serial, and the server retries with
// the next one.
const (
	ConnectToSerialRealm  = 14
	ConnectToSerialWorld1 = 17
	ConnectToSerialWorld2 = 35
	ConnectToSerialWorld3 = 53
	ConnectToSerialWorld4 = 71
	ConnectToSerialWorld5 = 89
)

// ConnectTo address types.
const (
	ConnectAddrNone  = 0
	ConnectAddrIPv4  = 1
	ConnectAddrIPv6  = 2
	ConnectAddrNamed = 3
)

// ConnectTo is SMSG_CONNECT_TO (0x4E0008): the server asking for a second
// connection, the one world entry continues on.
//
// Layout (the fork's ConnectTo::Write, and the real capture's 45-byte #190):
// u32 payload count, u32 serial, u8 con, u64 key, u32 native realm address,
// u32 key3, then per payload u8 address type, the address (4 or 16 bytes, or
// a C string for a named socket), u16 port and a BLEEP token.
type ConnectTo struct {
	Serial             uint32
	Con                uint8
	Key                uint64
	NativeRealmAddress uint32
	Key3               uint32
	Payloads           []ConnectPayload
}

// ConnectPayload is one address the client may dial.
type ConnectPayload struct {
	Type uint8
	IP   net.IP
	Name string
	Port uint16
	// Token is the BLEEP token; empty on the fork.
	Token BleepToken
}

// BleepToken is the per-address proxy token: 5-, 24- and 6-bit lengths, an
// i64 lifespan in nanoseconds, then the token, the proxy id (a sized C string
// whose length counts its NUL) and the address.
type BleepToken struct {
	Token, ProxyID, Address string
	LifespanNanos           int64
}

// AccountID is the low 32 bits of Key (the fork's ConnectToKey.AccountId).
func (c ConnectTo) AccountID() uint32 { return uint32(c.Key) }

// Instance reports the ConnectionType bit of Key: set for the instance
// (world) connection, the only kind the fork accepts a continued session for.
func (c ConnectTo) Instance() bool { return c.Key>>32&1 == 1 }

// Target returns the first dialable address as host:port, IPv4 first unless
// ipv6 is set.
func (c ConnectTo) Target(ipv6 bool) (string, error) {
	want := uint8(ConnectAddrIPv4)
	if ipv6 {
		want = ConnectAddrIPv6
	}
	for _, pass := range []bool{true, false} {
		for _, p := range c.Payloads {
			if p.Type != ConnectAddrIPv4 && p.Type != ConnectAddrIPv6 {
				continue
			}
			if pass && p.Type != want {
				continue
			}
			return net.JoinHostPort(p.IP.String(), strconv.Itoa(int(p.Port))), nil
		}
	}
	return "", errors.New("world: CONNECT_TO lists no IP address")
}

// DecodeConnectTo parses the SMSG_CONNECT_TO body (no opcode).
func DecodeConnectTo(body []byte) (ConnectTo, error) {
	var c ConnectTo
	r := codec.NewReader(body)
	n, err := r.Uint32()
	if err != nil {
		return c, err
	}
	if n > 16 {
		return c, fmt.Errorf("world: CONNECT_TO claims %d payloads", n)
	}
	if c.Serial, err = r.Uint32(); err != nil {
		return c, err
	}
	if c.Con, err = r.Uint8(); err != nil {
		return c, err
	}
	if c.Key, err = r.Uint64(); err != nil {
		return c, err
	}
	if c.NativeRealmAddress, err = r.Uint32(); err != nil {
		return c, err
	}
	if c.Key3, err = r.Uint32(); err != nil {
		return c, err
	}
	for i := uint32(0); i < n; i++ {
		p, err := decodeConnectPayload(r)
		if err != nil {
			return c, fmt.Errorf("world: CONNECT_TO payload %d: %w", i, err)
		}
		c.Payloads = append(c.Payloads, p)
	}
	return c, nil
}

func decodeConnectPayload(r *codec.Reader) (ConnectPayload, error) {
	var p ConnectPayload
	var err error
	if p.Type, err = r.Uint8(); err != nil {
		return p, err
	}
	switch p.Type {
	case ConnectAddrIPv4:
		b, err := r.Bytes(4)
		if err != nil {
			return p, err
		}
		p.IP = net.IPv4(b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3])
	case ConnectAddrIPv6:
		b, err := r.Bytes(16)
		if err != nil {
			return p, err
		}
		p.IP = append(net.IP(nil), b...)
	case ConnectAddrNamed:
		if p.Name, err = r.CString(); err != nil {
			return p, err
		}
	case ConnectAddrNone:
	default:
		return p, fmt.Errorf("address type %d", p.Type)
	}
	if p.Port, err = r.Uint16(); err != nil {
		return p, err
	}
	p.Token, err = decodeBleepToken(r)
	return p, err
}

func decodeBleepToken(r *codec.Reader) (BleepToken, error) {
	var t BleepToken
	tokLen, err := r.Bits(5)
	if err != nil {
		return t, err
	}
	proxyLen, err := r.Bits(24)
	if err != nil {
		return t, err
	}
	addrLen, err := r.Bits(6)
	if err != nil {
		return t, err
	}
	r.ResetBits()
	life, err := r.Uint64()
	if err != nil {
		return t, err
	}
	t.LifespanNanos = int64(life)
	tok, err := r.Bytes(int(tokLen))
	if err != nil {
		return t, err
	}
	t.Token = string(tok)
	// The proxy id's length counts its NUL, which is not on the wire: the
	// fork's empty id has length 1 and no bytes (capture #190).
	if proxyLen > 0 {
		px, err := r.Bytes(int(proxyLen - 1))
		if err != nil {
			return t, err
		}
		t.ProxyID = string(px)
	}
	ad, err := r.Bytes(int(addrLen))
	if err != nil {
		return t, err
	}
	t.Address = string(ad)
	return t, nil
}

// ConnectToFailedBody is the CMSG_CONNECT_TO_FAILED body: u8 con, u32 serial
// (the fork's ConnectToFailed::Read).
func ConnectToFailedBody(con uint8, serial uint32) []byte {
	w := codec.NewWriterCap(5)
	w.Uint8(con)
	w.Uint32(serial)
	return w.Bytes()
}
```

```go
package world

import (

func TestDecodeConnectToCapture(t *testing.T) {
	body, _ := hex.DecodeString(captureConnectTo)
	c, err := DecodeConnectTo(body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if c.Serial != ConnectToSerialWorld1 || c.Con != 1 {
		t.Errorf("serial %d con %d, want 17 1", c.Serial, c.Con)
	}
	if c.Key != 0xd5ecaa9b00000001 || c.AccountID() != 1 || !c.Instance() {
		t.Errorf("key %#x account %d instance %v", c.Key, c.AccountID(), c.Instance())
	}
	// 70-1-70: region 70, battlegroup 1, realm 70.
	if c.NativeRealmAddress != 0x46010046 || c.Key3 != 0 {
		t.Errorf("native realm %#x key3 %#x", c.NativeRealmAddress, c.Key3)
	}
	if len(c.Payloads) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d payloads", len(c.Payloads))
	}
	p := c.Payloads[0]
	if p.Type != ConnectAddrIPv4 || p.Port != 8085 || (p.Token != BleepToken{}) {
		t.Errorf("payload %+v", p)
	}
	target, err := c.Target(false)
	if err != nil || target != "127.0.0.1:8085" {
		t.Errorf("target %q %v", target, err)
	}
}

func TestDecodeConnectToTruncated(t *testing.T) {

// The continued session echoes CONNECT_TO's key, native realm address and
// key3 in the real client's 80-byte layout.
func TestAuthContinuedSessionCapture(t *testing.T) {
	want, _ := hex.DecodeString(captureContinued)
	a, err := DecodeAuthContinuedSession(want)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ct, _ := hex.DecodeString(captureConnectTo)
	c, _ := DecodeConnectTo(ct)
	if a.Key != c.Key || a.NativeRealmAddress != c.NativeRealmAddress || a.Key3 != c.Key3 {
		t.Errorf("echo key %#x realm %#x key3 %#x, CONNECT_TO had %#x %#x %#x",
			a.Key, a.NativeRealmAddress, a.Key3, c.Key, c.NativeRealmAddress, c.Key3)
	}
	got := a.Encode(0x460003)
	if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(got) != 0x460003 || !bytes.Equal(got[4:], want) {
		t.Fatalf("encode\n got %x\nwant %x", got[4:], want)
	}
}

// forkContinuedDigest is the fork's check, written independently of
// ContinuedSessionDigest (HandleAuthContinuedSessionCallback).
func forkContinuedDigest(sessionKey []byte, key uint64, local, server []byte) []byte {
	m := hmac.New(sha512.New, sessionKey)
	_ = binary.Write(m, binary.LittleEndian, key)
	m.Write(local)
	m.Write(server)
	m.Write(continuedSessionSeed)
	return m.Sum(nil)[:DigestLen]
}

const testAuthContinued = 0x460003

func continuedTable(t *testing.T) *opcodes.Table {
	t.Helper()
	ent := func(name string, dir opcodes.Direction, id uint32) string {
		return `{"name":"` + name + `","direction":"` + string(dir) + `","id":` +
			itoa(id) + `,"confidence":"verified"}`
	}
	raw := `{"protocol":"wowf","product":"wowf","build":70755,"status":"test","entries":[` +
		ent("SMSG_AUTH_CHALLENGE", opcodes.ServerToClient, testAuthChallenge) + `,` +
		ent("SMSG_ENTER_ENCRYPTED_MODE", opcodes.ServerToClient, testEncMode) + `,` +
		ent("CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION", opcodes.ClientToServer, testAuthContinued) + `,` +
		ent("CMSG_ENTER_ENCRYPTED_MODE_ACK", opcodes.ClientToServer, testAck) + `,` +
		ent("CMSG_LOG_DISCONNECT", opcodes.ClientToServer, testDisc) + `,` +
		ent("SMSG_PING", opcodes.ServerToClient, testPing) + `]}`
	tbl, err := opcodes.Load([]byte(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return tbl
}

func TestConnectContinuedFullExchange(t *testing.T) {
	d := newPipeDialer()
	var sk [SessionKeyLen]byte
	if _, err := rand.Read(sk[:]); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ct, _ := hex.DecodeString(captureConnectTo)
	cto, _ := DecodeConnectTo(ct)
	pub, priv, _ := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)

	srvErr := make(chan string, 1)
	go func() {
		fail := func(s string) { srvErr <- s; d.serverNet.Close() }
		conn := d.serverNet
		conn.Write(append([]byte(framing.ServerConnect), '\n'))
		line := make([]byte, len(framing.ClientConnect)+1)
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(conn, line); err != nil {
			fail(err.Error())
			return
		}
		dos := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x33}, 32)
		server := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x44}, ChallengeLen)
		ch := append(append(append([]byte(nil), dos...), server...), 4)
		conn.Write(framing.Frame(framing.Tagged{}, testAuthChallenge, ch))

		ss := &serverSide{t: t, conn: conn}
		msg, err := ss.readMessage()
		if err != nil {
			fail(err.Error())
			return
		}
		if msg.Opcode != testAuthContinued {
			fail("not AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION")
			return
		}
		a, err := DecodeAuthContinuedSession(msg.Body)
		if err != nil {
			fail(err.Error())
			return
		}
		if a.Key != cto.Key || a.NativeRealmAddress != cto.NativeRealmAddress || a.Key3 != cto.Key3 {
			fail("CONNECT_TO fields not echoed")
			return
		}
		if !bytes.Equal(a.Digest[:], forkContinuedDigest(sk[:], cto.Key, a.LocalChallenge[:], server)) {
			fail("digest mismatch")
			return
		}
		if ok, _ := DoSCheck(a.LocalChallenge[:], server, sk[:], dos, a.DosResponse, 4); !ok {
			fail("hashcash does not use the session key")
			return
		}
		enc, _ := EncryptionKey(sk[:], a.LocalChallenge[:], server)
		sig, _ := priv.Sign(rand.Reader, EnableEncryptionMessage(enc[:], true), &ed25519.Options{Context: string(EnableEncryptionContext)})
		body := binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(nil, 0)
		body = append(append(body, sig...), 0x80)
		conn.Write(framing.Frame(framing.Tagged{}, testEncMode, body))
		if msg, err = ss.readMessage(); err != nil || msg.Opcode != testAck {
			fail("no ACK")
			return
		}
		send, _ := NewCipherAt(enc[:], Recv, 2)
		plain := binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(nil, testPing)
		plain = append(plain, "resume"...)
		sealed, _ := send.Seal(nil, plain)
		c, tag := sealed[:len(plain)], sealed[len(plain):]
		conn.Write(append(framing.TaggedCrypt{}.EncodeSealed(c, [framing.TagLen]byte(tag)), c[4:]...))
		srvErr <- ""
	}()

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	s, err := ConnectContinued(ctx, &ContinuedConfig{
		Dialer: d, Target: transport.Target{Address: "pipe"}, Table: continuedTable(t),
		SessionKey: sk, ConnectTo: cto, Timeout: 5 * time.Second,
		Verifier: Ed25519Verifier{Pub: pub},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ConnectContinued: %v (server: %s)", err, <-srvErr)
	}
	defer s.Close()
	m, err := s.Read()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if m.Opcode != testPing || string(m.Body) != "resume" {
		t.Fatalf("read %#x %q", m.Opcode, m.Body)
	}
	if e := <-srvErr; e != "" {
		t.Fatal(e)
	}
	if s.SessionKey() != sk {
		t.Error("session key not kept")
	}
}

// The first connection keeps the session key the continued one needs.
func TestConnectKeepsSessionKey(t *testing.T) {
	d := newPipeDialer()
	pub, priv, _ := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
	cfg := testConfig(t, d, Ed25519Verifier{Pub: pub})
	srv := &serverSide{t: t, conn: d.serverNet, key: cfg.KeyData, build: cfg.BuildKey, priv: priv, pub: pub}

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)

	defer s.Close()
	// the fake server ends with one encrypted message; take it so it returns
	if _, err := s.Read(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	<-done
	want, _ := SessionKey(cfg.KeyData, srv.gotLocal[:], bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x22}, ChallengeLen))
	if s.SessionKey() != want {
		t.Fatal("Connect did not keep the session key")
	}
}
```

`world/crypt.go`:

```go
package world

import (
	"crypto/aes"
	"crypto/cipher"
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/Ltz-lab/wow-live/protocol/framing"
)

// Direction selects which of the two per-connection GCM contexts a Cipher is:
// the client keeps separate send and receive contexts with separate counters
// and separate IV magics (client flags byte bit 0, research/encryption.md §1).
type Direction int

const (
	// Recv decrypts server-to-client frames, IV magic "SRVR".
	Recv Direction = iota
	// Send encrypts client-to-server frames, IV magic "CLNT".
	Send
)

// IV magics, as the client stores them (0x52565253 "SRVR", 0x544E4C43 "CLNT").
var (
	magicRecv = [4]byte{'S', 'R', 'V', 'R'}
	magicSend = [4]byte{'C', 'L', 'N', 'T'}
)

// AEADNonceLen is the GCM nonce length: the 8-byte little-endian counter then
// the 4-byte magic (client 0x101093a5c receive, 0x101093634 send).
const AEADNonceLen = 12

var (
	// ErrBadKeyLen means the key is not 32 bytes (AES-256).
	ErrBadKeyLen = errors.New("world: encryption key must be 32 bytes")
	// ErrBadTag means the frame's tag is the wrong length.
	ErrBadTag = errors.New("world: frame tag must be 12 bytes")
	// ErrAuthFailed means GCM authentication failed.
	ErrAuthFailed = errors.New("world: frame authentication failed")
)

// Cipher is one direction of the post-ENTER_ENCRYPTED_MODE connection cipher:
// AES-256-GCM over the opcode and payload, no AAD, a per-frame counter-derived
// nonce, and the first 12 of the 16 tag bytes on the wire.
//
// A Cipher is not safe for concurrent use; the connection serializes reads and
// writes.
type Cipher struct {
	aead    cipher.AEAD
	magic   [4]byte
	counter uint64
}

// NewCipher arms a direction with the derived key, its nonce counter at 0.
func NewCipher(key []byte, dir Direction) (*Cipher, error) {
	return NewCipherAt(key, dir, 0)
}

// NewCipherAt arms a direction with the nonce counter already at start.
//
// The counter is not reset by the switch to encrypted mode: it counts every
// frame of its direction from the first one, cleartext frames included
// (research/encryption.md \u00a71, "both start at 0 and increment after each
// frame"). A session that already exchanged two cleartext frames therefore
// starts its send cipher at 2, not 0 \u2014 which is what the server's own
// DecryptRecv expects, because it increments its counter for the cleartext
// frames too (the fork: WorldPacketCrypt::DecryptRecv, WorldSocket.cpp
// HandleEnterEncryptedModeAck).
func NewCipherAt(key []byte, dir Direction, start uint64) (*Cipher, error) {
	if len(key) != EncryptionKeyLen {
		return nil, ErrBadKeyLen
	}
	block, err := aes.NewCipher(key)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// The wire carries only the first 12 of the 16 tag bytes and the client's
	// own verifier compares exactly those 12 (0x102e4eb7c), which is what a
	// 12-byte GCM tag size produces.
	aead, err := cipher.NewGCMWithTagSize(block, framing.TagLen)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c := &Cipher{aead: aead, counter: start}
	if dir == Send {
		c.magic = magicSend
	} else {
		c.magic = magicRecv
	}
	return c, nil
}

// Counter reports the next nonce counter.
func (c *Cipher) Counter() uint64 { return c.counter }

func (c *Cipher) nonce() []byte {
	var n [AEADNonceLen]byte
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(n[:8], c.counter)
	copy(n[8:], c.magic[:])
	c.counter++
	return n[:]
}

// Seal encrypts plaintext (opcode included) and returns the ciphertext with
// the 12-byte wire tag after it, i.e. exactly the frame body the wire carries
// once the opcode's header is in front of it.
func (c *Cipher) Seal(dst, plaintext []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	out := c.aead.Seal(dst, c.nonce(), plaintext, nil)
	if len(out) != len(plaintext)+framing.TagLen {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("world: seal returned %d bytes for %d plus %d", len(out), len(plaintext), framing.TagLen)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// Open authenticates and decrypts a frame body with its wire tag, appending
// the plaintext to dst.
func (c *Cipher) Open(dst, body, tag []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	if len(tag) != framing.TagLen {
		return dst, ErrBadTag
	}
	sealed := make([]byte, 0, len(body)+framing.TagLen)
	sealed = append(sealed, body...)
	sealed = append(sealed, tag...)
	out, err := c.aead.Open(dst, c.nonce(), sealed, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return dst, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrAuthFailed, err)
	}
	return out, nil
}
```
